info.description:
# Merged Masterclass Backend - All APIs

GENERATED from the live URLconf by `Miscellaneous/Scripts/generate_postman_collection.py` on 2026-10-09.
Do not hand-edit: re-run the script after any routing change.

**229 mounted API routes** -> **238 requests** across **22 folders**. The Django admin UI is excluded; it is not an API surface.

Request bodies: 68 of 84 write endpoints carry a template generated from the view's own validator. The rest either take no body by design (stated on the request) or use a pattern the generator does not yet read.

## Breaking changes, shipped 2026-09-24

Re-import rather than merging. A client built before this date still calls paths that MOVED, and the old ones 404 with no redirect shim.

- **Maintenance split three ways (2026-09-24).** `account/app-maintainance/` -> `app-api/v1/account/maintainance-status/`, `account/web/app-status/` -> `web-api/v1/account/maintainance-status/`, and the staff POST toggle moved to `account/universal/maintainance-status/`. Both probes are now anonymous and answer the same two keys, `is_maintenance` and `force_logout_all_user`.
- **The web probe lost three keys.** `is_web_maintenance` is now `is_maintenance`; `is_pathway` and `is_onboarding_completed` are gone from it entirely - `GET account/user-details/` already answers both.
- **`account/user_details/` (underscore) was DELETED**, along with its PATCH. `account/user-details/` (hyphen) is the only one left and is GET-only; write profile fields through `PATCH account/profile/`.
- **Six lead-capture routes** now file a Salesforce enquiry: `talk-to-us/`, `enquiry/`, and the four programme funnels under `caira/`, `cpa/` and `cma/`. The four funnels take NO body - any key is a 400.

## Setup

1. Import all four files and select the LOCAL, UAT or PROD environment.
2. Set `login_identifier` to the e-mail or phone you are testing with.
3. Send **POST auth-otp-send-v1**, put the code you receive in `otp_code`, then send **POST auth-otp-verify-v1**.

That is the whole setup. `token` and `refresh_token` are written by the scripts - do not paste a token in by hand, and do not expect one to survive a logout.

Webhook requests are the exception: they are `noauth` and carry their own secret header, so set `lms_notification_webhook_key` and `miles_one_webhook_secret` for **19. Inbound Webhooks (no JWT)**.

## What runs automatically

Everything below is Postman-side scripting. There is no companion runner and nothing writes to disk; the environment is the only state.

- **The access token renews itself.** The collection pre-request script reads `exp` out of the JWT and refreshes when fewer than `token_refresh_skew_seconds` (120) remain. Refresh tokens ROTATE, so the new pair is stored immediately - which is also why nothing here ever refreshes twice at once. Set `auto_refresh` to `off` to stop it.
- **Path parameters fill themselves.** After any 2xx JSON response the collection test script walks the body and writes any key matching a path variable into the environment, so a list request sets up the detail request that follows it. `id` is deliberately NOT harvested - it is the path parameter of one route (the certificate webhook) and the commonest key in every list body, so set it by hand. It fills a variable ONLY WHEN THAT VARIABLE IS EMPTY, so a value you pinned yourself is never overwritten - clear it if you want it re-harvested. Set `auto_capture` to `off` to stop it. Only the FIRST element of a list is read, and only keys named exactly like the path variable.
- **Every response is checked for the baseline**: no 5xx, and a JSON content type parses. Response time is logged, never asserted - it is a property of the machine the run is on.
- **A 401 or 403 explains itself** in the console instead of leaving a bare status code: whether a token is set at all, and whether a webhook secret rather than a token is what the route wanted.
- **The three session routes carry their own scripts** - verify stores the minted pair, refresh stores the rotated pair, logout clears both, and only on a 2xx.

Query parameters are present but DISABLED, so a request sends nothing it was not asked to send.

## What each request tells you

Open any request's Documentation pane. It carries the view and permission behind the route, the body it accepts, the query parameters it declares, every error `code` it can return and what each one means, and the shape of the response - taken from the contracts the frontend web team works to. There is no separate documentation folder to go and read: the detail is on the request you are about to send.

## Saved examples

Every request carries saved examples - 1267 of them, 5.3 per request - one per outcome that request can produce. Pick them from the dropdown beside Send to see the success body, each validation failure, the authentication refusal and the 500 envelope without having to provoke them.

**They are READ OFF THE HANDLER, not written by hand.** Each one comes from a `Response(...)` in the view's own source - including the ones built in a shared helper or in the function the handler delegates to - so when a handler changes shape the examples change with it on the next run. A saved example is the part of a collection that normally rots first, and a tester comparing a live 400 against a stale example cannot tell which of the two is wrong.

**A value in angle brackets was not invented.** `"user_id": "<str(user_id)>"` means the key is there and the script could not resolve its value from the source - it shows you where the value comes from instead of fabricating one that would look like a format guarantee. The response SHAPE in those cases is in the contract text further down the same pane.

**Status codes with no example are not outcomes that cannot happen.** A route whose response is proxied from an upstream service carries that service's status, which is not readable from this side - the five sign-in routes are the case in point, and their success bodies are documented in the contract text instead.

## Folders

- **01. Authentication and Session** - 5 routes, 5 requests (5 UNIVERSAL).
- **02. Account, Profile and Reference Content** - 21 routes, 24 requests (3 APP, 17 UNIVERSAL, 1 WEB).
- **03. Masterclass - Learning Flow (app)** - 31 routes, 31 requests (30 APP, 1 WEBHOOK).
- **04. Masterclass - Learning Flow (web)** - 29 routes, 29 requests (29 WEB).
- **05. AI Labs** - 40 routes, 40 requests (14 APP, 12 UNIVERSAL, 14 WEB).
- **06. Events and Bookings** - 19 routes, 19 requests (9 APP, 6 UNIVERSAL, 4 WEB).
- **07. CAIRA - Badges, Certificates, CPE** - 1 routes, 1 requests (1 UNIVERSAL).
- **08. Notifications and Bell** - 5 routes, 5 requests (5 UNIVERSAL).
- **09. Catalogue** - 9 routes, 9 requests (9 UNIVERSAL).
- **10. Commerce** - 13 routes, 19 requests (13 UNIVERSAL).
- **11. Engagement - Likes, Saves, Watches** - 2 routes, 2 requests (2 UNIVERSAL).
- **14. Varun Masterclass** - 7 routes, 7 requests (6 APP, 1 UNIVERSAL).
- **15. Learn Page (app)** - 1 routes, 1 requests (1 APP).
- **16. Home Page (app)** - 2 routes, 2 requests (2 APP).
- **17. Badges - CPE Tracker (app and web)** - 5 routes, 5 requests (3 APP, 1 UNIVERSAL, 1 WEB).
- **18. Webinar Feedback (app and web)** - 6 routes, 6 requests (3 APP, 3 WEB).
- **19. Inbound Webhooks (no JWT)** - 5 routes, 5 requests (1 UNIVERSAL, 4 WEBHOOK).
- **20. Referral** - 6 routes, 6 requests (6 UNIVERSAL).
- **21. Favourites (app)** - 1 routes, 1 requests (1 APP).
- **22. Programs Page (app)** - 8 routes, 8 requests (8 APP).
- **23. Seven-Day Challenge (partner LMS)** - 9 routes, 9 requests (9 UNIVERSAL).
- **99. Unclassified (new prefix - add it to FOLDERS)** - 4 routes, 4 requests (4 UNIVERSAL).

## Conventions that apply to every request

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 1. Conventions

### 1.1 Every path moved under `account/`, and there is no redirect

Ported paths were namespaced under `account/` on 2026-08-12. Django does not treat `faqs` and
`account/faqs` as the same route, so an un-updated build gets a **404, not a redirect**. No shim exists.

Two legacy oddities are reproduced on purpose and are not typos to fix on your side:

- `maintainance` is **misspelt** in all three maintenance paths, matching `settings.APP_UNDER_MAINTENANCE`'s
  readers. It stays: a path that spells it correctly next to settings that do not is worse than one
  consistent mistake.
- Every path now carries a trailing slash, including `country` and `faqs`, which did not have one in legacy.

### 1.2 Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` where the table says JWT. A **bad or expired token answers `403`, not `401`** -
DRF downgrades an authentication failure when the authenticator does not implement `authenticate_header()`, and
ours does not. Do not key token-refresh on 401 alone.

The endpoints marked "enforced in handler" are a different shape: they carry no permission class, so an
anonymous request reaches the handler and gets a **401** from an explicit check inside it. So on those four you
can see 401 for anonymous and 403 for a broken token, from the same route.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: both paragraphs are wrong today. `JWTAuthentication` DOES implement
`authenticate_header()`, so a missing, bad or expired token answers **401** with
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"` (measured on every JWT route here). Only `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` is read. No Accounts route is "enforced in handler" any more; the project default permission is
`IsAuthenticated`, and the public routes declare `AllowAny` with no authenticator.

### 1.3 Undeclared keys are rejected

Request bodies and query strings are validated strictly. A key the endpoint does not declare is a 400 naming
it. Sending a known key as `null` is also rejected where the field does not allow null - strict validation
forbids the key's *presence*, so "send it as null to be safe" does not work.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: only where a serializer reads the input. The GETs with no query serializer - both
maintenance probes, `universal/` GET, `user-details/`, `profile/` GET, `name/` GET, `privacy-policy/`,
`terms-and-conditions/`, `faqs/` - ignore any query string (measured: `?bogus=1` answers 200 on the probes),
and `auth-logout/` ignores its body.

### 1.4 Error envelopes

The auth proxy routes (section 2) return **the SSO's own body, whole and untouched**, whatever it contains.
Everything this backend generates itself uses one of:

```json
{ "message": "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." }
{ "code": "account_blocked", "message": "This account has been blocked..." }
{ "message": "Invalid request.", "details": { "country": ["..."] } }
```

DRF validation failures on the serializer-backed routes come back as DRF's native shape - a map of field name
to a list of messages - not the `{status, code, errors[]}` envelope the Events routes use. **The two apps do
not share an error shape.** Handle both.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: every body above, the SSO's included, reaches the wire inside the platform envelope
`{success, message, data}` (`EnvelopeJSONRenderer`, the default renderer). A string `message` is lifted into
the envelope's `message`; everything else lands under `data`. A validation failure is
`{"success": false, "message": "The request could not be completed.", "data": {<field>: ...}}`, and an SSO
503 is `{"success": false, "message": "Sign-in is not configured on this environment.", "data": null}`.

---

## 2. The login flow

Five routes, in order. All five are proxies onto the Miles SSO auth API: they OBTAIN a token, they do not
verify one. Verification is local, against the issuer's JWKS, on every subsequent request.

```
auth-identify  ->  auth-otp-send  ->  auth-otp-verify  ->  (session)
                                                             |
                                            auth-token-refresh (rotate)
                                                             |
                                                       auth-logout
```

## 6. Maintenance probes

RESTRUCTURED 2026-09-24, and this is a **breaking change on three counts**: both probe paths moved,
the web payload lost three keys and renamed a fourth, and the POST toggle moved to a third route.
There is no shim; an un-updated build 404s on the first call it makes.

| was | is |
| --- | --- |
| `GET account/app-maintainance/` | `GET app-api/v1/account/maintainance-status/` |
| `GET account/web/app-status/` | `GET web-api/v1/account/maintainance-status/` |
| `POST account/app-maintainance/` | `POST account/universal/maintainance-status/` |

### 8.2 The two apps do not share an error shape

Events returns `{status, code, errors[]}` and asks you to switch on `code`. Accounts returns DRF's native
validation shape, a bare `{message}`, or the SSO's body untouched. There is no single error parser that covers
both. See 1.4.

### 8.3 The auth routes return the SSO's body, not ours

Everything on the five auth routes except the two local flags and the refusals listed in 2.3 is passed through
from the Miles SSO verbatim, including fields not documented here. Treat unknown keys as additive, and do not
assume our version pins their schema. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: verbatim but enveloped - read the SSO's fields
from `data`, and its `message` from the envelope's `message` (see 1.4).

## 1. Conventions

### 1.1 Three path prefixes, and the split is deliberate

- `api/v1/events/...` - SHARED. The registration handshake. One write path, one contract, one set of side
  effects (Zoom -> Booking -> Salesforce). A web caller and an app caller register identically.
- `web-api/v1/events/...` - WEB-ONLY READS. The landing feed and the detail page behind it.
- `app-api/v1/events/...` - APP-ONLY READS. The bookings feed.

What a page renders is genuinely surface-shaped: bucket counts, ordering and payload width differ between a
browser and a phone, so a read belongs to the surface that renders it. No route has a twin on the other read
prefix yet.

The rule this encodes: writes stay shared, reads split by surface.

`app-api/` was added on 2026-09-17 and `all-bookings/` moved onto it. An earlier version of this document
described that route as web-only; that was wrong, and the prefix is the part of this scheme that names the
surface, so it was corrected rather than left. It was MOVED, not aliased - this document went out the same
day, so there is no shipped client on the old path.

Note that `Masterclass` splits web from app a DIFFERENT way, by domain segment (`api/v1/masterclass/` vs
`api/v1/masterclass-web/`). Which scheme a surface uses is a fact to look up, not to derive.

### 1.2 Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every route above, except `webinar-main-page?login_type=pre_login`, which is
served anonymously.

**`webinar-details-page` TAKES NO `login_type` AND IS NOT GATED.** It derives the surface from the request:
send a token and you get the post-login page with its `registration` block, send none and you get the
pre-login page without it. A signed-out visitor can open a webinar page.

**CHANGED 2026-09-18.** It shipped on 2026-09-17 as `IsAuthenticated`, answering `403` to anonymous callers.
If you built against that, the 403 is gone and `data.login_type` now tells you which surface you received.

A BAD OR EXPIRED TOKEN ANSWERS `403`, NOT `401`. This is true of every authenticated route in this backend,
not just these four: DRF downgrades an authentication failure to 403 when the authenticator does not implement
`authenticate_header()`, and ours does not. Do not key token-refresh logic on 401 alone. The one `401` this app
returns is a different case entirely - see section 6.2.

### 1.3 Undeclared parameters are rejected, not ignored

Every request body and query string is validated strictly. A key the endpoint does not declare is a 400 naming
that key; it is not silently dropped. A typo'd filter therefore fails loudly instead of returning an
unfiltered 200.

### 1.4 Error envelopes

Validation failure (400):

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "errors": [{ "field": "login_type", "message": "Field required" }]
}
```

`field` is dot-joined, so a bad key inside a list element reads as `chapters.0.chapter_id`. An undeclared key
comes back with that key as `field`.

Domain refusal (400 / 404 / 409):

```json
{ "status": "error", "code": "webinar_not_found", "detail": "Webinar does not exist." }
```

SWITCH ON `code`, NEVER ON THE HTTP STATUS AND NEVER ON `detail`. The `code` values are the stable contract;
wording and status can move.

One inconsistency to handle before you write the error handler: the `authentication_required` refusal from
`webinar-main-page` carries `message` where every other refusal carries `detail`. Read `detail ?? message`.

### 1.5 Status codes are real

The legacy V4 register endpoint answered `500` for every input and state problem, because FE reserved 400/404
for token-refresh and logout flows. These routes return the real `400` / `404` / `409` / `401`. If an
interceptor still treats any 4xx as a session problem, that has to change before you point at these routes.
A client that switches on `code` rather than on status needs no change.

---

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AuthIdentifyViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `auth-identify-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

POST - how does this person authenticate?

Proxies `POST /auth/identify`. The first call of any login, always.

THE CLIENT MUST RENDER `methods` RATHER THAN ASSUME A FORM. When enterprise SSO ships, this same endpoint starts answering `saml` with a redirect, and a client that renders the list needs no change while one that hardcoded a password box needs a rewrite.

DO NOT BUILD A "no such account" MESSAGE FROM THIS RESPONSE. An identifier the SSO has never seen returns the same `methods`, `defaultMethod` and masks as a known one - the masks are built from what was typed, not from anything stored.

ACCOUNT DISCLOSURE, ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY. `communicationId` is passed through to the caller by maintainer decision (2026-09-07); it is null for an unknown identifier, so a non-null value confirms the account exists and hands over the UUID other Miles systems key off. The route is therefore FIRST-PARTY ONLY. See the plan document, section 6.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it said "and is throttled". It is NOT throttled today: `throttle_scope = 'sso_identify'` is declared and settings carry a 20/min rate for it, but this view declares no `throttle_classes` and settings have no `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES`, so DRF never consults the scope. The same holds for every `throttle_scope` in this module. DEFECT, not fixed here.

Body template generated from `AuthIdentifyRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Some values are ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES rather than placeholders - set `login_identifier` once and the three sign-in requests all read it. `refresh_token` is written by a script; do not type it.

**This request carries its own test script** on top of the collection-level one - open the Scripts tab to read what it writes into the environment.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 2.1 `POST auth-identify/` - how does this person authenticate?

The first call of any login, always.

```json
{ "identifier": "learner@example.com" }
```

`identifier` is an email, phone number or username - the SSO works out which. `appCode` is **not accepted from
the client**; it is added server-side, because it names which application is asking and a caller must not be
able to claim to be another one.

The response is the SSO's, and carries `methods`, `defaultMethod`, masked destinations and `communicationId`.

**Render `methods` rather than assuming a form.** When enterprise SSO ships, this same endpoint starts
answering `saml` with a redirect. A client that renders the list needs no change; one that hardcoded an OTP box
needs a rewrite.

**Do not build a "no such account" message from this response.** An identifier the SSO has never seen returns
the same `methods`, `defaultMethod` and masks as a known one - the masks are built from what was typed, not
from anything stored. There is no negative signal here to render, by design.

This route discloses account existence through `communicationId` (null for an unknown identifier), which is why
it is **first-party only** and the most tightly throttled of the five at 20/min. Do not expose it to an
untrusted origin. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it is not throttled at all today (see the note under the route
table), and its nominal 20/min is not the tightest - `auth-otp-send/` is 10/min.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AuthLogoutViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `auth-logout-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

POST - end the session at the SSO.

Proxies `POST /auth/logout`, which is Bearer-authenticated.

`scope` IS FORWARDED, `local` BY DEFAULT. It used to send a hardcoded `{}` with no request serializer at all, so a client asking for `{"scope": "global"}` got a `200` and a local logout - the field was dropped without a word. See `AuthLogoutRequestSerializerV1`.

THE BEARER IS TAKEN FROM THE INBOUND HEADER AND FORWARDED, rather than resolved to a local user first. Logout must work for a token this database has no row for - a user who was provisioned at the SSO but never reached this service still has a session worth ending, and refusing them would leave it open.

**No request body by design.** Bearer header only; the SSO reads the token, not a body.

**This request carries its own test script** on top of the collection-level one - open the Scripts tab to read what it writes into the environment.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 2.5 `POST auth-logout/` - end the session at the SSO

Empty body. Takes the bearer from the inbound `Authorization` header and forwards it.

Missing or non-Bearer header is a 401 with
`{"message": "Authorization header with a Bearer token is required."}`.

Note this deliberately does **not** resolve the token to a local user first: logout must work for a token this
database has no row for, because a session worth ending still exists.

---

response.name: 400 Bad Request - DRF renders a failed `is_valid(raise_exception=True)` itself, keyed by parameter name
401 Unauthorized
502 Bad Gateway
503 Service Unavailable

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AuthOtpSendViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `auth-otp-send-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST login-with-phone-otp`

POST - send a one-time code.

Proxies `POST /auth/otp/send`.

WRITE UI COPY FROM THE RETURNED `channel`, NEVER FROM WHAT WAS SENT. It is `email`, `sms` or `whatsapp`, and phone routing is a table at the SSO, so it changes with no deploy on either side. AS OF 2026-09-08 EVERY COUNTRY RESOLVES TO `sms`, India included: WhatsApp routing is switched off until delivery is proved end to end, and no WhatsApp transport is configured. An earlier revision of this docstring recorded Indian numbers as routed to WhatsApp with SMS as an automatic fallback - that was the 2026-09-04 reference and it has not been true since.

`cooldownSeconds` COMES BACK BESIDE `channel` and is how long the client's resend button stays disabled. It is forwarded untouched, like every other field, because this view returns the SSO's body whole. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: whole, but enveloped - the fields arrive under the envelope's `data`, with a string `message` lifted out beside it.

`channel` IS NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE CLIENT YET. The SSO takes it as an optional `sms` / `whatsapp` override for "send it the other way", but `AuthOtpSendRequestSerializerV1` does not declare it and the outbound body below is built field by field, so it would be rejected here and dropped there. Deliberate: with routing resolving to `sms` everywhere there is no other channel to ask for. See section 13 of the integration plan.

A `503` MEANS NOTHING WAS SENT AND NOTHING WILL BE. The identity store accepted the request and then refused to deliver it. Advance the user to a retry, never to a code-entry screen. It says our mailer is broken, never anything about the account - every identifier-specific outcome is a 200.

PHASE 1 IS EMAIL. Phone identifiers are proxied faithfully rather than refused (maintainer decision, 2026-09-07), because the reference requires that `methods` be rendered as given. THE CLIENT IS THEREFORE THE ONLY THING preventing a WELL-FORMED Indian phone number from reaching a silent failure: SMS there is accepted by the provider and dropped by the carrier, so a 200 does not mean a message arrived. A MALFORMED number is no longer the client's problem - since 2026-09-04 the SSO answers `400` with a message written for a learner to read, and that message reaches the phone field unaltered.

Body template generated from `AuthOtpSendRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Some values are ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES rather than placeholders - set `login_identifier` once and the three sign-in requests all read it. `refresh_token` is written by a script; do not type it.

**This request carries its own test script** on top of the collection-level one - open the Scripts tab to read what it writes into the environment.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 2.2 `POST auth-otp-send/` - send a one-time code

```json
{ "identifier": "learner@example.com" }
```

The response carries `channel` and `cooldownSeconds`.

**Write UI copy from the returned `channel`, never from what you sent.** It is `email`, `sms` or `whatsapp`,
and phone routing is a table at the SSO that changes with no deploy on either side. **As of 2026-09-08 every
country resolves to `sms`, India included** - WhatsApp routing is off until delivery is proved end to end.

`cooldownSeconds` is how long the resend button stays disabled. Read it; do not hardcode one.

`channel` is **not accepted as an input** yet. The SSO takes it as an optional override, but this route does not
declare it, so sending it is a 400.

**A `503` means nothing was sent and nothing will be.** The identity store accepted the request and then
refused to deliver. Advance the user to a retry, never to a code-entry screen. It says our mailer is broken -
it never says anything about the account. Every identifier-specific outcome is a 200.

One caveat on phone identifiers: they are proxied faithfully rather than refused, so a **well-formed Indian
phone number can reach a silent failure** - the provider accepts the SMS and the carrier drops it, so a 200 does
not prove a message arrived. The client is currently the only thing preventing that. A *malformed* number is
not your problem: the SSO answers 400 with copy written for a learner, and that message reaches the phone field
unaltered - render it.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AuthOtpVerifyViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `auth-otp-verify-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST verify-otp`

POST - exchange a one-time code for a session.

Proxies `POST /auth/otp/verify`. On success the body carries `accessToken` and `refreshToken`; for a web client the SSO ALSO sets the httpOnly `miles_sso_refresh` cookie, which is forwarded verbatim.

THE ACCESS TOKEN RETURNED HERE IS WHAT THIS BACKEND ALREADY VERIFIES. It is an ES256 token from the configured issuer, and `MilesPlatform.authentication.JWTAuthentication` checks it against the JWKS on every subsequent request.

A FIRST-TIME USER IS REGISTERED BY THIS CALL and comes back with `miles.onboarding_required = true`. After the profile is completed, the token MUST be refreshed - the claim is minted with the token, so skipping the refresh re-reads a stale `true` and bounces the user into onboarding they just finished.

A wrong or expired code is a `401`; repeated failures lock the identifier and return `429`.

Body template generated from `AuthOtpVerifyRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Some values are ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES rather than placeholders - set `login_identifier` once and the three sign-in requests all read it. `refresh_token` is written by a script; do not type it.

**This request carries its own test script** on top of the collection-level one - open the Scripts tab to read what it writes into the environment.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 2.3 `POST auth-otp-verify/` - exchange the code for a session

```json
{ "identifier": "learner@example.com", "code": "123456" }
```

`code` is a **string, and its length is not validated here**. The code length is set server-side at the SSO -
read it rather than hardcoding six boxes.

On success the body carries `accessToken` and `refreshToken`. For a web client the SSO **also** sets the
httpOnly `miles_sso_refresh` cookie, which is forwarded verbatim. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: if the SSO sends
more than one `Set-Cookie`, only the last is forwarded (`copy_set_cookie` overwrites) - a known defect.

Two **local** flags are merged into the success body, and they are the reason this route is worth reading
carefully. Neither is in the token, and the SSO knows nothing about either:

| Key | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `profile_status` | `new_user`, `onboard_completed`, `profile_completed` | This platform's onboarding milestone. |
| `is_test_user` | boolean | Gates `#TestCourse` visibility. Always `false` on a fresh account - set by an admin. |

**`profile_status` IS NOT the token's `miles.onboarding_required`.** That claim describes the identity store -
whether the SSO still needs a name before it considers the account known - and it is a boolean of the
**opposite polarity**. A user can be fully known to the SSO and still be `new_user` here. Reading one for the
other is how a sign-up gate ends up inverted.

Failure modes, and each wants different UI:

| HTTP | Body | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | SSO's | Wrong or expired code. | Let them retype. |
| 429 | SSO's | Too many failures; the identifier is locked. | Show the lockout, do not retry. |
| 403 | `code: "account_blocked"` | Partner-imposed block. | **Terminal.** Show a permission message, not a login screen. Point at Miles support. |
| 403 | `code: "account_deactivated"` | Miles deactivation. | **Terminal.** Same, different team. |
| 502 | `{"message": "Sign-in could not be completed. Please request a new code."}` | Provisioning failed after a valid token. | **Retryable.** The code they used is spent - send them for a new one. |
| 503 | `{"message": "Sign-in is not configured on this environment."}` | Our configuration fault. | Not the user's problem. |

The two 403s are deliberately distinct: `active` and `is_blocked` are separate columns set by different people
for different reasons, and telling a blocked learner their account is "deactivated" sends them to the wrong
team. Neither carries a token or a cookie.

**A SUCCESSFUL VERIFY NOW WRITES THE PHONE NUMBER ONTO THE ACCOUNT** (2026-10-10). Nothing in the response
changed - this is a server-side effect, and there is no new key to read. When the identifier the SSO proved is a
phone number, it is written to `User.country_code` / `User.phone_number` on EVERY successful verify, not only on
the one that creates the account. Before this, a returning learner's number was stamped in the phone ledger and
the account column was left exactly as it was, so anyone who had signed up by e-mail could not be resolved by
their number on the legacy-SSO and admin token paths at all. An e-mail sign-in writes nothing.

The consequence worth knowing: if a DIFFERENT active account still carries that number, it is CLEARED from that
account. The displaced learner is not notified - no notification path exists - so support finds them from the
`phone_displaced_other_account` log event or from the User Phone Numbers admin screen, where the ledger lists
every number an account has held, newest verification first.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AuthTokenRefreshViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `auth-token-refresh-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST refresh`

POST - exchange a refresh token for a new session.

Proxies `POST /auth/token/refresh`, and serves both client shapes: an app sends `refreshToken` in the body, a browser sends an empty body and its httpOnly cookie is forwarded upstream.

REFRESH BEFORE EXPIRY, NOT AFTER A 401. The access token is short on purpose

- it is the window in which a suspended or refunded user keeps access, and

it cannot be revoked once issued.

DO NOT RUN TWO REFRESHES CONCURRENTLY. Refresh tokens rotate and the old one dies about ten seconds after use, so parallel refreshes invalidate the caller's own session. Serialise them behind one in-flight request.

Body template generated from `AuthTokenRefreshRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Some values are ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES rather than placeholders - set `login_identifier` once and the three sign-in requests all read it. `refresh_token` is written by a script; do not type it.

**This request carries its own test script** on top of the collection-level one - open the Scripts tab to read what it writes into the environment.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 2.4 `POST auth-token-refresh/` - rotate the session

Serves both client shapes:

```json
{ "refreshToken": "..." }   // app clients
{}                          // web clients - the httpOnly cookie is forwarded upstream
```

`refreshToken` is optional for exactly that reason; requiring it would lock every browser out of refresh.

The same two local flags (`profile_status`, `is_test_user`) are merged into a 200 here, and **they matter more
on this route than on verify.**

**THE ONBOARDING SEQUENCE, which is the single most common integration bug on this surface:**

1. A first-time user verifies and comes back `profile_status: "new_user"`.
2. They complete the profile (section 4).
3. **You must refresh the token.** The claim is minted with the token, so skipping the refresh re-reads a stale
   value and bounces the user straight back into onboarding they just finished.

Two more rules:

- **Refresh before expiry, not after a 401.** The access token is deliberately short - it is the window in
  which a suspended user keeps access, and it cannot be revoked once issued.
- **Never run two refreshes concurrently.** Refresh tokens rotate and the old one dies about ten seconds after
  use, so parallel refreshes invalidate the caller's own session. Serialise them behind one in-flight request.

A `401` from this route (`"Session could not be refreshed. Please sign in again."`) means the refreshed token
would not resolve to a local row - the account is gone or deactivated. Send them to sign-in.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL

**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `country-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** none

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET country`

Retrieve country details, optionally filtered by a name prefix.

Returns countries from the local `CountryData` table. With the optional `country` query parameter, results are limited to names starting with it.

Method:

```
GET
```

Query Parameters:

```
country (str, optional): Prefix filter on `country_name__startswith`.
    Example: `?country=Ind`
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: `{"data": [<serialized country objects>]}`
400 BAD REQUEST: `{"message": "<error message>"}` on a database error.
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: also 400 `{"message": "Invalid request.",
"details": {...}}` for an undeclared or over-long query parameter
(measured: `?bogus=1` -> 400). On the wire every body is wrapped by
`EnvelopeJSONRenderer` as `{success, message, data}`.
```

Notes:

```
Filtering is case-sensitive unless the database collation says otherwise;
use `country_name__istartswith` if case-insensitivity is ever wanted
explicitly.
```

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `country` - Optional. Case-sensitive prefix of country_name to filter on.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 7.1 `GET country/` - public

Optional `?country=Ind` filters on a **case-sensitive** prefix of the country name. An empty `?country=` means
no filter, not "match the empty string".

`200` -> `{"data": [...]}`. A bad parameter is `400` -> `{"message": "Invalid request.", "details": {...}}`.

A typo'd parameter name is a 400, deliberately: it used to be ignored in silence, which returned the full
country list and looked like a successful filtered call.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `EmailVerificationViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `account-email-verify-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Check whether an address is usable by the caller.

GET /api/v1/account/email-verify/?email=someone@example.com

UNIVERSAL. Both surfaces ask the same question about the same learner and read the same answer, so this keeps the shared prefix and a bare `V1`.

TWO GATES, IN THIS ORDER:

1. IS IT FREE? Asked of the SSO, because the SSO owns identity and this

```
database does not - an address unused here may be bound to another
account there. SKIPPED when the address is already the caller's own,
which is the common case of a learner re-submitting the form.
```

2. IS IT REAL? Asked of Reoon, which probes the mailbox.

Free-but-fake and real-but-taken are both refusals, and they are refused with different messages because they need different actions from the learner.

`email_verified` IS WRITTEN ONLY ON A CLEAN PASS, and it is evidence the address EXISTS rather than proof the learner controls it - nothing here sends a confirmation link. See the column's own comment.

WHAT LEGACY DID THAT THIS DOES NOT:

- IT DECODED THE BEARER TOKEN ITSELF, with `jwt.decode` under `settings.SSO_JWT["SECRET_KEY"]`, to read the token's email. That secret IS `None` in this tree - the SSO moved to ES256 with a JWKS, and `MilesPlatform.authentication` verifies against it. Re-decoding would raise, and decoding a token the framework has already verified would mean two implementations of "what does a valid token mean". The caller's own address comes from `request.user` instead.
- IT RETURNED 400 FOR A MISSING OR MALFORMED `Authorization` HEADER, inside its own try block. Here `IsAuthenticated` answers that with a 401 before the view runs, which is what an unauthenticated request should get.
- IT CONSULTED A MILESFINISHERS READ REPLICA to force `show_referral_code` to False for a known lead. That call was COMMENTED OUT in the legacy source on 2025-12-24 and its result defaulted to False, so the override could not fire. Porting the dead branch would carry a rule nothing has applied for nine months; the base rule is ported and the override is not.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `email` - Optional. The address to check for deliverability.

Record the caller's interest in one programme.

POST /api/v1/account/enquiry/

```
{"programme": "CPA" | "CMA" | "USP" | "CAIRA",
 "lead": {"comment": null, "is_referral": null, "referrer_uuid": null}}
```

`lead` IS OPTIONAL AND SO IS EVERY FIELD IN IT. The ordinary call is `{"programme": "CAIRA"}` and nothing else.

ONE ROUTE FOR EVERY PROGRAMME AS OF 2026-09-29 (maintainer). This absorbed `POST api/v1/account/enquiry/  (legacy: `caira/enquire-now/`)`, which is retired - the two filed the same kind of lead and differed only in which programme they named, so the programme moved into the body. What each programme DOES downstream is unchanged; `Accounts.utils.lead_capture.capture_enquiry` carries the table and says why the two behaviours could not simply be averaged.

IN `Accounts`, NOT `EventsPage`, though legacy declared it in `event/views.py`. It touches no webinar, no booking and no event row; it captures a lead against the authenticated user, which is what this app is for.

SHARED PREFIX for the same reason as `TalkToUsViewV1`: it is a write.

Body template generated from `EnquiryRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 10. Lead capture - three routes that file a Salesforce enquiry

**THERE WERE SIX UNTIL 2026-09-29, AND FIVE UNTIL 2026-09-30.** Two collapses, for the same reason
each time. `POST api/v1/caira/enquire-now/` is RETIRED and answers 404: it filed the same kind of lead
as `account/enquiry/` and differed only in naming CAIRA, so the programme moved into that endpoint's
body - see 10.1. The three `*/brochure-download/` routes are likewise RETIRED and answer 404; they
differed only in which programme the URL named, so that moved to a query parameter - see 10.2.

A brochure download is still its own endpoint rather than a fourth `programme` value on
`account/enquiry/`, because it pushes a Netcore event and answers "a brochure was downloaded", not
"somebody enquired".

All three take a JWT, POST only, and answer the SAME envelope. **None of them proxies Salesforce's
response body**, which is a deliberate change from legacy: returning `response.json()` straight through
made the CRM's schema part of this contract and leaked internal lead ids to a handset.

```json
{ "message": "Your request has been received. Our team will be in touch.", "status": "Success" }
```

- `200` - Salesforce accepted the lead.
- `502` - Salesforce refused or was unreachable. `{"message": "This service is temporarily unavailable,
  please try again later.", "status": "Failed"}`.

The learner is always taken from the token, never from the body.

### 10.1 The two contact routes

| Route | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `POST account/talk-to-us/` | none - pinned to US CPA, as legacy did |
| `POST account/enquiry/` | `programme`, plus an optional `lead` block |

`talk-to-us` starts the learner's **pathway-driven** webinar auto-registration, which fans out to
every audience their `user.pathway` implies - up to three webinars.

#### `POST account/enquiry/` - one route, every programme

```json
{
  "programme": "CPA",
  "lead": {
    "comment": "Asked about CMA pricing from the pricing page",
    "is_referral": true,
    "referrer_uuid": "99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555"
  }
}
```

`lead` is optional and so is every field in it. **The ordinary call is `{"programme": "CAIRA"}`.**

| field | type | required | what `null` means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `programme` | `CPA` \| `CMA` \| `USP` \| `CAIRA` | **yes** | - absent is a 400 |
| `lead.comment` | string, max 500 | no | keep the flow's own comment |
| `lead.is_referral` | bool | no | keep the flow's own value |
| `lead.referrer_uuid` | uuid | no | forwarded to Salesforce as `null` |

**`programme` replaced `course_id` on 2026-09-29 and the old field is now a 400.** `course_id` made
the client state Salesforce's own id, so this contract moved whenever the remote catalogue did. The id
is resolved server-side now.

**What each programme does downstream.** They are not uniform, and the differences are the two
endpoints this route merged:

| `programme` | Salesforce `course_id` | `is_referral` | Webinars booked |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `CPA` | 1 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `CMA` | 2 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `USP` | 3 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `CAIRA` | **18** | `false` | exactly **1** - the CAIRA audience |

**CAIRA files under course 18 as of 2026-09-29, and that is a change.** The retired
`caira/enquire-now/` sent no course id at all, so a CAIRA enquiry filed against whatever the learner's
pathway implied - course 1 for anyone with an empty pathway. It had no choice: the route took no body,
so nothing carried the programme into the payload. The body states it now, and 18 is the CRM's own id
for CAIRA. **Any report that counted CAIRA enquiries by course id must look at 18 from this date.**

**Identity and `campaign_id` are NOT accepted in `lead`** - they are a 400, not ignored. The learner
comes from the token, or a caller could file a lead against somebody else; `campaign_id` decides which
Salesforce campaign the lead lands in.

### 10.3 What happens after the 200

The Salesforce lead is **awaited** - you are told whether it was recorded. The webinar booking and the
Netcore push are **detached**, and their outcome is not in the status code. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: only the
booking is detached. The Netcore push is AWAITED, before the lead - `notify_brochure_downloaded` runs through
`sync_to_async` and makes a blocking POST - so a slow Netcore delays the response; its outcome still never
changes the status code. A 200 means the lead was
filed; it does not mean a seat was confirmed.

Auto-registration fires even when Salesforce refused. A CRM outage is not a reason to withhold a
webinar seat from a learner who just expressed interest.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `FAQsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `faqs-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET faqs`

Retrieve FAQs grouped by category.

A category literally named "all" (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed) receives every FAQ across all categories rather than only its own.

PUBLIC BY DECISION (maintainer, 2026-09-17), and declared as such rather than left to a default. FAQs are help content on a pre-login screen; there is nothing here to protect and nothing in this handler reads `request.user`.

THIS DOCSTRING USED TO SAY "JWT required" AND THE CODE NEVER DID THAT. The class declared `authentication_classes = [JWTAuthentication]` and NO `permission_classes`, and naming an authenticator only ATTEMPTS authentication - with no permission class DRF falls back to `AllowAny`, so this endpoint already answered 200 to anyone. The same defect was found and fixed on `QuestionsViewV1` on 2026-09-09; it is the pairing that is easy to miss, so it is worth stating twice in one file.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES HERE IS THE BROKEN-TOKEN CASE, and it is the reason the authenticator is removed rather than kept beside an explicit `AllowAny`. `JWTAuthentication` returns None when there is no `Authorization` header, but RAISES for a header that is present and bad - which DRF renders as 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"` (RECHECKED 2026-10-07: measured; this said 403). So a client holding a STALE OR EXPIRED token - exactly what lingers in a browser on a signed-out help page - used to be refused the FAQs. With no authenticator the header is never inspected and that cannot happen. A public help page must not fail on a credential it does not need.

THE COST, stated rather than discovered: the `ActivityLogger` span for this endpoint no longer carries user attribution, because nothing resolves `request.user` any more. That is accepted for anonymous read-only content. Restoring it would need an authenticate-if-possible-ignore-failures class, which does not exist in this repository and is not worth inventing for a FAQ list.

Authentication:

```
None. Reachable anonymously, deliberately.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: A list of categories, each with `id`, `category`, `order`
and a `faqs` list of `{id, question, answer, order}`.
```

Notes:

```
Exactly two queries, and no model instances are built for the FAQs
themselves - `values()` returns dicts, which is also what the response
needs. `all_faqs` is accumulated in the same single pass that fills the
per-category buckets, so grouping is O(total_faqs) with no second loop.
```

```
`created_at` / `modified_at` ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT (maintainer,
2026-09-30), and dropped from the `values()` projection too rather than
only from the payload - there is no reason to fetch two columns nothing
ships. They are authoring metadata: a help page renders a question and an
answer, and when an admin last touched a row is not the reader's concern.
```

```
THIS IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM LEGACY, and the only one on this
endpoint. Legacy MilesOne publishes both keys, so before this change the
merged response was BYTE-IDENTICAL to legacy's - measured 2026-09-30,
both 55,588 bytes. It no longer is. The change brings FAQs into line with
`PrivacyPolicy` and `TermsAndConditions`, which already omit the same
authoring fields, so the three content endpoints now answer consistently.
```

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 7.2 `GET faqs/`

A list of categories, each `{id, category, order, faqs: [{id, question, answer, order, created_at,
modified_at}]}`. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `created_at` / `modified_at` were dropped on 2026-09-30; each FAQ is
`{id, question, answer, order}`.

A category literally named `all` (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed) receives **every** FAQ across all
categories rather than only its own.

**Public by decision, and safe to call before login.** No `Authorization` header is inspected, so a stale or
expired token cannot turn a help page into a 403. Send a token or do not - it changes nothing.
(RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the failure it prevents would be a 401, not a 403.)

### 8.1 `faqs/` is public on purpose, and now says so

Its docstring used to claim "JWT required" while the code served anyone - it declared an authenticator but no
permission class, and **declaring an `authentication_classes` does not require authentication**: without a
permission class DRF falls back to `AllowAny`. The same defect was found and fixed on `questions/` on
2026-09-09.

Resolved on 2026-09-17 by making the intent explicit rather than by adding a token check: FAQs are help content
on a pre-login screen, and the maintainer's decision is that they stay open. The authenticator was removed
entirely, so a **stale or expired token can no longer 403 the FAQ list** - which is what would have happened
had the declaration simply been left in place beside an `AllowAny`.

`privacy-policy/` and `terms-and-conditions/` still carry the same missing permission class but compensate with
an explicit check in the handler, so they do refuse anonymous callers - with a 401 rather than a 403.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that last paragraph is no longer true - both are public now (see 7.3). Two further
corrections to this section: a view with no permission class now falls back to `IsAuthenticated` (the project
default), not `AllowAny`; and the stale-token failure removed here would have been a 401, not a 403.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `LMSAccountLinkViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `account-lms-account-link-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST v2/lms-access`

`POST api/v1/account/lms-account-link/` - claim an existing LMS account.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `event/views.py::GetLMSCredsView` (`v2/lms-access`) on 2026-09-29.

IT GRANTS NOTHING, AND THE LEGACY NAME HID THAT. "lms-access" reads like the endpoint that hands over a credential; it is not. A learner says "I already have a CPA account under this email", this asks the LMS whether that is true, and if it is, raises a PENDING ticket for a human to approve. Access itself comes later, from `app-api/v1/account/lms-login/<course>/`. The route is renamed to say so.

THE ORDER OF THE TWO REFUSALS MATTERS AND IS LEGACY'S. "That LMS account is already in use" is checked before "you already have a ticket", because the first is about somebody else's claim on the account and the second is only about this learner repeating themselves.

THE DOUBLE-FIRE IS REAL AND IS HANDLED BY THE DATABASE. The app sends this twice a few milliseconds apart, so both requests pass both checks before either inserts. `LMSLoginTickets` carries a unique constraint on `(lms_course, lms_candidate_id)`, so Postgres rejects the loser and only one ticket can exist - the loser is answered as though its ticket already existed, which is what has effectively happened.

DELIBERATELY NOT A REDIS LOCK, and legacy records the reasoning: the DB is already the guarantee, and under `IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS` a Redis blip makes `cache.add` return `None`, which a truthiness test reads as "already held" - refusing every caller while creating nothing.

STATUS CODES ARE THE REAL ONES, WHICH IS A CHANGE FROM LEGACY. Every legacy answer was `202`, including both refusals and the not-found case, so a client could not tell success from refusal without reading `message`. Here: `201` created, `409` for both refusals, `404` not found in the LMS, `502` when the LMS cannot be reached. The `message` strings are carried verbatim so an existing client that reads them still matches.

PUBLIC BY DECISION, AND DECLARED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED. `authentication_classes` is cleared AND `AllowAny` is explicit, so neither half can be re-tightened by a change to the project defaults without someone deleting a line that says why it is here.

### 4.1 READ THIS FIRST: `profile/` changed meaning on 2026-09-09

Until 2026-09-09, `api/v1/account/profile/` served the **user row**. It does not any more - that is

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `user_details/` was deleted 2026-09-24 and no route serves the user row; section 3 is
`user-details/`, the routing payload. `profile/` also carries three derived keys - see 4.3.

The rename was done deliberately while there was only one claimant, so the two never shared a name. If you have
code written against the old `profile/`, it is now pointing at a different resource that will return a
completely different shape.

### 4.4 `PATCH profile/` - write them back

Query: `?form=onboarding` (default) or `?form=profile` - it names which milestone is in scope.

Body: the **same flat map** the GET returns, so you read, edit and send back without reshaping.

```json
{ "highest_qualification": "CA", "years_experience": 3 }
```

- **Partial by definition.** A code you omit is left exactly as it was, so a user can fill half a form, leave,
  and come back. This is why it is PATCH and not PUT.
- **`null` is refused**, not read as "clear". There is no clearing requirement yet and inventing one would fix
  that meaning forever.
- **Idempotent.** The same body twice yields the same rows and the same milestone. A retry after a mobile
  timeout is safe.

Response:

```json
{
  "answers": { },
  "profile_status": "onboard_completed",
  "is_onboarding_completed": true,
  "is_profile_completed": false,
  "missing": []
}
```

`answers` is the same flat map, nested rather than top-level because a bare map keyed by question code has
nowhere safe to carry metadata - a `profile_status` key would collide with a question coded `profile_status`.

**The write always succeeds; the milestone advances only when every required, shown question of that form has
an answer.** A partial save comes back with `missing` naming what is still outstanding rather than failing. Do
not treat a non-empty `missing` as an error.

A 400 is keyed by question code, one message per bad answer. Validation runs before the transaction opens, so a
rejected submission never partially applies.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07, three corrections:

- The response also carries `referral_code_applied` (bool), and `profile_picture` at the TOP level beside
  `answers` when the request sent one.
- `country_name` and `show_referral_code` in the body are dropped silently; `profile_picture` is accepted
  (a base64 image data URI, or `null` to remove it).
- The avatar is the exception to "never partially applies": it is validated and written BEFORE the answers,
  outside their transaction, so a good picture sent with a bad answer is stored while the 400 refuses the
  answers. A known defect.

**After this advances the milestone, refresh the token** - see 2.4.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `QuestionsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `account-questions-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET account/v2/question/`

Return one questionnaire's questions, ordered for rendering.

Serves whichever set `?form=` names - `onboarding` (the default) or `profile` - selected on `Question.visibility`, which includes `both` in either answer. That third enum member is why membership is one column rather than the pair of booleans legacy carried.

AUTHENTICATION IS ENFORCED AS OF 2026-09-09, and was not before. `authentication_classes` alone only ATTEMPTS authentication; with no `permission_classes` DRF falls back to `AllowAny`, so this endpoint answered `200` to anyone - while the docstring above it said "JWT required". Measured against a running server, not inferred. The pairing is the thing to remember: naming an authentication class does not require one.

Method:

```
GET
```

Query:

```
form: `onboarding` (default) or `profile`. Validated - an
    unrecognised value is a 400 naming the accepted set, never a silent
    fallback that would serve the wrong questionnaire.
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: `{"Questions": [...]}` - a FLAT LIST sorted by
`display_order`, each question carrying its `options`. `section` is
a label a client may group by; it does NOT affect ordering, and there are
no screen buckets.
400 Bad Request: an unrecognised `form`, or a database error.
```

Notes:

```
Two queries, both natively async, and no `sync_to_async` anywhere. The
legacy view wrapped its whole read-and-format step in
`sync_to_async(self._fetch_and_format)` because `prefetch_related`
and a `ModelSerializer` are sync-only ORM paths. This version drops the
threadpool hop entirely: the options are fetched as a second `async for`
keyed by question id instead of via `Prefetch(to_attr=...)`, and the
serializer then runs over instances that are ALREADY in memory, which
issues no query - `parent_question` is its only relation, and DRF's
`PrimaryKeyRelatedField` reads it through the pk-only optimisation, off
the FK column already on the row. Same queries, same response, one less
thread.
```

```
THREE CLAIMS WERE CORRECTED HERE ON 2026-09-09, all of them describing a
model that the 2026-09-08 rewrite removed: membership by
`question_type="Onboarding_Questions"` / `new_set_questions` /
`question_toggle` (now `visibility`), a response keyed by
`Screen1`/`Screen2` (it is a flat list), and a serializer using
`fields = '__all__'` (it enumerates them, and this repository has zero
live occurrences of `'__all__'`).
```

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `form` - Optional. One of: `onboarding`, `profile`. Default `onboarding`. Which questionnaire to return: onboarding or profile. Questions marked `both` are returned for either.
- `login_via` - Optional. One of: `phone`, `email`. How the learner signed in. `phone` omits the mobile-number question, `email` omits the email question. Omit to return both.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 4.2 `GET questions/` - what to render

Query: `?form=onboarding` (default) or `?form=profile`. An unrecognised value is a **400 naming the accepted
set**, never a silent fallback that would serve the wrong screen.

Response: `{"Questions": [...]}` - a **flat list** sorted by `display_order`, each question carrying its
`options`. `section` is a label you may group by; it does **not** affect ordering, and there are no screen
buckets. (Legacy keyed this by `Screen1` / `Screen2`. That is gone.)

A question whose `visibility` is `both` appears under **either** `form` value - that is why membership is one
column rather than two booleans.

**This route now requires authentication.** It did not before 2026-09-09: it declared an authentication class
but no permission class, which only *attempts* authentication, so it answered 200 to anyone. If you were
calling it pre-login, that no longer works.

UPDATED 2026-10-09 - three things a client renders differently:

- **Every option is `{"text", "description", "value"}`.** `description` is the option's second line - the
  `user_intent` cards carry a sentence each ("I am a working finance professional seeking cutting-edge AI
  workflows and career growth."). It is `""` when an option has none, and it is present on EVERY option,
  including the three the graduation question builds, so never guard for the key being absent.
- **`?login_via=phone|email` asks for the identifier the sign-in did NOT use.** `email` drops the `email`
  question and keeps the phone question; `phone` drops the phone question (`mobile_number`) and keeps `email`.
  Absent means both are served. Any other value is a 400. The parameter is unchanged from 2026-10-05; only the
  rule is now settled.
- **The phone question reads "What is your phone number?" and sits in the email question's slot** -
  `display_order` 105 for both, ties broken by `code`, so with no `login_via` `email` comes first. Its code is
  still `mobile_number`; answers are keyed by code, so nothing already saved moves.

Record that the caller wants customer care to contact them.

POST /api/v1/account/talk-to-us/

No body. The learner is the JWT's user and the programme is pinned to US CPA, both as legacy sent them.

SHARED PREFIX, NOT `app-api/`. This is a write with one set of side effects, and a browser and a handset asking to be called back are asking for exactly the same thing - the versioning standard puts writes on `api/` for that reason. Only reads whose PAYLOAD differs by surface get their own prefix.

WHY THE COURSE IS PINNED. Legacy sends `course=1` here whatever the learner is pursuing, so every talk-to-us lead files against US CPA. That is carried unchanged: it is what the CRM's reports have counted since the endpoint existed. The pathway-driven auto-registration that runs alongside it does NOT use this value - it reads `user.pathway` - so the two are deliberately answering from different sources.

**No request body by design.** Pins US CPA; the learner comes from the token.

---

## 10. Lead capture - three routes that file a Salesforce enquiry

**THERE WERE SIX UNTIL 2026-09-29, AND FIVE UNTIL 2026-09-30.** Two collapses, for the same reason
each time. `POST api/v1/caira/enquire-now/` is RETIRED and answers 404: it filed the same kind of lead
as `account/enquiry/` and differed only in naming CAIRA, so the programme moved into that endpoint's
body - see 10.1. The three `*/brochure-download/` routes are likewise RETIRED and answer 404; they
differed only in which programme the URL named, so that moved to a query parameter - see 10.2.

A brochure download is still its own endpoint rather than a fourth `programme` value on
`account/enquiry/`, because it pushes a Netcore event and answers "a brochure was downloaded", not
"somebody enquired".

All three take a JWT, POST only, and answer the SAME envelope. **None of them proxies Salesforce's
response body**, which is a deliberate change from legacy: returning `response.json()` straight through
made the CRM's schema part of this contract and leaked internal lead ids to a handset.

```json
{ "message": "Your request has been received. Our team will be in touch.", "status": "Success" }
```

- `200` - Salesforce accepted the lead.
- `502` - Salesforce refused or was unreachable. `{"message": "This service is temporarily unavailable,
  please try again later.", "status": "Failed"}`.

The learner is always taken from the token, never from the body.

### 10.1 The two contact routes

| Route | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `POST account/talk-to-us/` | none - pinned to US CPA, as legacy did |
| `POST account/enquiry/` | `programme`, plus an optional `lead` block |

`talk-to-us` starts the learner's **pathway-driven** webinar auto-registration, which fans out to
every audience their `user.pathway` implies - up to three webinars.

#### `POST account/enquiry/` - one route, every programme

```json
{
  "programme": "CPA",
  "lead": {
    "comment": "Asked about CMA pricing from the pricing page",
    "is_referral": true,
    "referrer_uuid": "99999999-8888-7777-6666-555555555555"
  }
}
```

`lead` is optional and so is every field in it. **The ordinary call is `{"programme": "CAIRA"}`.**

| field | type | required | what `null` means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `programme` | `CPA` \| `CMA` \| `USP` \| `CAIRA` | **yes** | - absent is a 400 |
| `lead.comment` | string, max 500 | no | keep the flow's own comment |
| `lead.is_referral` | bool | no | keep the flow's own value |
| `lead.referrer_uuid` | uuid | no | forwarded to Salesforce as `null` |

**`programme` replaced `course_id` on 2026-09-29 and the old field is now a 400.** `course_id` made
the client state Salesforce's own id, so this contract moved whenever the remote catalogue did. The id
is resolved server-side now.

**What each programme does downstream.** They are not uniform, and the differences are the two
endpoints this route merged:

| `programme` | Salesforce `course_id` | `is_referral` | Webinars booked |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `CPA` | 1 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `CMA` | 2 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `USP` | 3 | `true` | pathway fan-out - **up to 3** |
| `CAIRA` | **18** | `false` | exactly **1** - the CAIRA audience |

**CAIRA files under course 18 as of 2026-09-29, and that is a change.** The retired
`caira/enquire-now/` sent no course id at all, so a CAIRA enquiry filed against whatever the learner's
pathway implied - course 1 for anyone with an empty pathway. It had no choice: the route took no body,
so nothing carried the programme into the payload. The body states it now, and 18 is the CRM's own id
for CAIRA. **Any report that counted CAIRA enquiries by course id must look at 18 from this date.**

**Identity and `campaign_id` are NOT accepted in `lead`** - they are a 400, not ignored. The learner
comes from the token, or a caller could file a lead against somebody else; `campaign_id` decides which
Salesforce campaign the lead lands in.

### 10.3 What happens after the 200

The Salesforce lead is **awaited** - you are told whether it was recorded. The webinar booking and the
Netcore push are **detached**, and their outcome is not in the status code. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: only the
booking is detached. The Netcore push is AWAITED, before the lead - `notify_brochure_downloaded` runs through
`sync_to_async` and makes a blocking POST - so a slow Netcore delays the response; its outcome still never
changes the status code. A 200 means the lead was
filed; it does not mean a seat was confirmed.

Auto-registration fires even when Salesforce refused. A CRM outage is not a reason to withhold a
webinar seat from a learner who just expressed interest.

### 6.3 `account/universal/maintainance-status/` - the override

**GET is public** and reports the override plus what each surface is consequently serving:

```json
{
  "override_active": true,
  "override_value": true,
  "app": { "is_maintenance": true, "source": "cache" },
  "web": { "is_maintenance": true, "source": "cache" }
}
```

`source` is `cache` when a live override decided it and `env` when the surface fell back to its own
secret. It reports per surface because with no override live there is no single answer: the two
surfaces read two different secrets and can legitimately differ.

**POST requires a STAFF token.** It sets a cache override that outranks BOTH secrets for up to 7 days,
so it is gated on `is_staff` rather than on merely being signed in - there are far more learners than
there are people who should be able to take the platform down. A signed-in non-staff caller gets 403.

```json
{ "value": true, "ttl_seconds": 3600 }
```

- `value` is **required and nullable**, and those are different things. `null` CLEARS the override so
  each surface falls back to its own secret; omitting the key is a 400.
- `ttl_seconds` is optional. Default 86400 (24h), clamped to [60, 604800].
- Any undeclared key is a 400 naming the field.

The response is the GET body plus `ttl_seconds` on a set, or `"cleared": true` on a clear.

**ONE OVERRIDE COVERS BOTH SURFACES** - that is what "universal" names. A single POST puts app and web
into maintenance together; there is no per-surface override and a flip cannot be aimed at one client.

Every set and clear is audit-logged with the acting staff account's id at WARNING severity. This is an
operations tool - do not build a learner-facing UI onto it.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `PathwayLogoutRouteViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `account-pathway-logout-route-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces 2 legacy MilesOne routes:** `GET V2/pathway-based-logout-route/`, `GET caira/other_badge_status/`

Everything the app needs to decide where to send the caller after logout.

GET /api/v1/account/user-details/

THE NAME COLLISION IS GONE. `api/v1/account/user_details/` - one character from this path, returning the 28-field user row - was DELETED on 2026-09-24 (maintainer). This is now the only `user-details` endpoint, which is why the hyphen spelling no longer needs defending.

WHAT IT ANSWERS. Post-logout routing is a set of independent questions - who is this learner, how far through onboarding are they, do they have a pathway, are they enrolled. The client needs all of them at once to pick one destination, so they travel as one payload rather than several round trips.

`show_referral_code` MOVED TO `api/v1/account/profile/` ON 2026-09-24 (maintainer). It is a property of the learner rather than of where to send them next, and it was the only field here that no routing decision read. CLIENT VISIBLE.

THE BOOKING PAIR AND THE SEVEN-DAY CHALLENGE LEFT ON 2026-09-24 (maintainer): `career_counselling_booked`, `office_visit_booked`, `show_seven_day_challenge` and `seven_day_challenge_answer`. They were the only reads beyond the enrolment column, so the endpoint went from four queries to one that day. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it is back to SIX on a cache miss - see `_compute` - and `career_counselling_booked` itself RETURNED to the payload that day. CLIENT VISIBLE - anything branching on them needs telling.

IT NEVER FAILS THE CALLER. Every error resolves to a 200 carrying the conservative defaults - RECHECKED 2026-10-07: see `_safe_fallback`. Logout routing that 500s leaves a learner on a dead screen at the exact moment they have no session to retry with, so the endpoint answers something usable and records the fault on the span instead.

CACHED FOR 30 SECONDS PER USER, at the TTL and key prefix the cache registry already carried for it.

ONE WRITE PATH INVALIDATES IT, as of 2026-10-07: `ProfileViewV1`'s POST patches `user_data_fully_filled` through `aupdate_pathway_cache` after a submission, because that is the only thing that can change the answer and the reader no longer recomputes it on a cache hit. (`SevenDaysChallenge` calls the same helper, but still serves no route.)

EVERYTHING ELSE STILL LAGS A WRITE BY UP TO THE TTL - `pathway`, the programme rows and `career_counselling_booked` have no invalidation, so a booking taken this second can take 30 more to appear. The name and the two onboarding flags are exempt: they are recomputed off the request user on every cache hit, because they cost no query.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 3. `api/v1/account/user-details/` - post-logout routing

REWRITTEN 2026-09-24. This section used to document `UserDetailsViewV1` and its 28-field user row on
`api/v1/account/user_details/` (underscore), **with a PATCH writing 16 of them**. That endpoint and that
view were DELETED. The hyphen spelling is now the only one, it is served by
`PathwayLogoutRouteViewV1`, and **there is no PATCH on it** - a client still sending one gets 405.

To write profile fields, use `PATCH account/profile/` (4.4).

### 3.1 `GET user-details/` - JWT

Answers, in one call, every independent question the app needs to pick a destination after login or
logout, so it does not make five round trips to decide one thing.

```json
{
  "first_name": "Sohan",
  "full_name": "Sohan Biswas",
  "is_onboarding_completed": true,
  "is_profile_completed": true,
  "pathway": "Yes",
  "enrolled_status": "Yes",
  "enrolled_course": ["US CPA"],
  "onboarding_fully_completed": true
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `first_name` | Display name. Falls back to the first token of `full_name`. |
| `full_name` | Stored full name, whitespace-stripped. |
| `is_onboarding_completed` | The stored column. |
| `is_profile_completed` | The stored column. |
| `pathway` | `"Yes"` / `"No"` - **a string, not a boolean**. Lowercased 2026-10-05; it was `Pathway` until then, and there is no alias. |
| `enrolled_status` | `"Yes"` / `"No"`, same caveat. |
| `enrolled_course` | List of programme names. Empty list when not enrolled. |
| `onboarding_fully_completed` | DERIVED - every always-asked onboarding field is filled. Not the same as `is_onboarding_completed`, which is a stored flag. See 8.4. |

**`show_referral_code` MOVED TO `GET account/profile/` on 2026-09-24.** It is a property of the learner,
not of where to route them, and no routing decision read it. CLIENT VISIBLE.

**`career_counselling_booked`, `office_visit_booked` and `show_seven_day_challenge` were REMOVED** on the
same day. If you read any of the four, move or drop the read before deploying.

**A read failure degrades rather than fails.** If the enrolment lookup cannot be completed the endpoint
answers 200 with the conservative payload - `"pathway": "No"`, `"enrolled_status": "No"`,
`"enrolled_course": []` - because a routing endpoint that 500s leaves the app with nowhere to send the
learner. Treat "No" as "we could not confirm", not as proof of absence.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07, against `PathwayLogoutRouteViewV1` as it stands today:

- `enrolled_course` is no longer a list of names. It is FOUR programme rows (cpa, cma, usp, caira), each
  `{course_name, is_enrolled, is_alumni, has_claimed, is_loggedin, lms_token}`, on every path; the
  fallback sends the same four rows with nothing asserted, not `[]`.
- `career_counselling_booked` (bool) is BACK, added 2026-10-07; the fallback sends `false`. The other
  three removed keys stay removed.
- `onboarding_fully_completed` is being renamed `user_data_fully_filled` in the working tree (another
  change in flight on 2026-10-07); read the key from the code before binding.
- `first_name` falls back to the WHOLE `full_name`, not its first token.
- The payload is cached 30 s per learner and no write invalidates it.

### 8.4 `profile_status` has three values, and two booleans say the same thing

`profile_status`, `is_onboarding_completed` and `is_profile_completed` all encode the same two milestones and
all three are returned. They are consistent; the booleans exist because they are cheaper to branch on. None is
writable.

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET v2/lms_login/<course>`

Bind an LMS session to the caller, or return the one they already have.

POST /app-api/v1/account/lms-login/<course>/

With `access_token` and `uid` in the body it BINDS; with neither it READS. See `LMSAccessRequestSerializerV1` for why sending exactly one is a 400.

SIDE EFFECTS ON A NEW GRANT, in order: the learner's cached Learn page is dropped, then a Salesforce net enquiry and the pathway-driven webinar auto-registration are each fired detached. None of the three runs on a token rotation or a read - a rotated token is the same learner on the same programme, and a second lead or a second booking for it is a duplicate rather than a signal.

Body template generated from `LMSAccessRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Revoke the caller's LMS credential for one course.

POST /app-api/v1/account/lms-logout/<course>/

THIS HARD-DELETES, WHICH IS A DELIBERATE EXCEPTION TO H-14. Soft delete exists so a record stays recoverable; this row is a live CREDENTIAL, and a revoked credential that is still readable is the opposite of revoked. The table also carries no `active` column to soft-delete with, so keeping the row would mean keeping a usable token. Legacy hard-deleted for the same reason.

**No request body by design.** Course is in the path; bearer only.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppUnderMaintainanceV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `app-maintainance-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET app-maintainance/`

Mobile maintenance probe. `GET app-api/v1/account/maintainance-status/`.

Falls back to `settings.APP_UNDER_MAINTENANCE`, which is loaded through `MilesPlatform.aws_secrets.get_secret` - `os.environ` in LOCAL, the AWS Secrets Manager blob in UAT/PROD. It is read ONCE at process boot, so changing the secret alone needs a restart to take effect; the override on `universal/maintainance-status/` is the no-redeploy path.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 6.1 `GET app/maintainance-status/` - public

```json
{ "is_maintenance": false, "force_logout_all_user": false }
```

Is the **mobile** surface down. No `Authorization` header is inspected at all, so a stale token can
never stop a client reading the maintenance flag - which is exactly the client most likely to be
asking. Deliberately trivial, so it is safe to poll on every cold start.

`force_logout_all_user` **mirrors `is_maintenance` exactly** today: maintenance on means clear the
session and go to login, off means do not. It is a separate key because the two answer different
questions - "show the maintenance screen" and "discard this session" - and they are only equal for
now. Read both; do not infer one from the other, or the day a maintenance window is declared that
does not invalidate sessions, your build will be wrong and this endpoint will not.

### 6.4 Where the values come from, and why a secret edit is not enough

Both fall-back values load through AWS Secrets Manager (`APP_UNDER_MAINTENANCE`,
`WEB_APP_UNDER_MAINTENANCE`) and are read **once at process boot**. Editing a secret therefore changes
nothing until the service restarts. The override on 6.3 is the only live switch.

```
GET app|web/maintainance-status/
  -> Redis override live?  yes -> that value           source: cache
                            no -> this surface's secret source: env
```

---
