request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `MasterclassFinalAssessmentQuestionsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `masterclass-assessment-questions-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The final-assessment question batch, with its cooldown state.

`GET api/v1/masterclass/<course_id>/assessment/questions/`

UNIVERSAL - the app and the web ask this of the same learner and read the same answer, so it keeps the shared `api/` prefix.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE BATCH IS DRAWN ON EVERY REQUEST, not per attempt - `aget_random_questions` runs on each GET and the served set is not stored, so two reads before one submit can differ. A client must not cache this payload. The submit endpoint therefore checks only that each id is in the bank, not that it was served. DEFECT, not fixed here.

THE COOLDOWN IS PART OF THE ANSWER, not a separate read. A learner inside the wait window after a failed attempt is told when they may retry, so the client renders the timer rather than computing it. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it arrives as a `403` with `reason: cool_off_active`, `cool_off_seconds_remaining` and `cool_off_ends_at`, not inside a 200.

NO CORRECT ANSWERS IN THE PAYLOAD. Grading is server-side in the submit endpoint - a NASBA boundary, not a UI preference.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: refusals, in order - `409` AI Lab lock and `403 caira_access_required` (`_arefuse_course_step`), `404` no config, `403 chapters_not_complete`, `403 already_passed` (the activity log records 409 for this one while the response is 403 - DEFECT, not fixed here), `403 cool_off_active`.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The questions.
403 Forbidden: A `reason` - see the refusal list above.
404 Not Found: When the course or its assessment configuration is
    unknown.
409 Conflict: When the course is closed by its AI Lab.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

6.9c GET /api/v1/masterclass/<course_id>/assessment/report/

The learner's own Final Assessment report for one course: `passed`, `failed` or `not_attempted`, with the questions served in their latest attempt and the answers they gave.

ALWAYS ANSWERS, which is the whole point and the difference from `assessment/result/` next door. That endpoint 404s both when there is no attempt and when the course has no assessment configured, so a client cannot tell those apart from a wrong course id. Here the only 404 is a course that does not exist or is not visible to this caller.

THE APP TWIN OF `WebMasterclassFinalAssessmentReportViewV1`. The two share `abuild_final_assessment_report` and nothing else - separate class, separate route, separate operation name, per the surface-split rule.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `MasterclassFinalAssessmentResultViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `masterclass-assessment-result-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The latest final-assessment attempt, question by question.

`GET api/v1/masterclass/<course_id>/assessment/result/`

UNIVERSAL - the app and the web ask this of the same learner and read the same answer, so it keeps the shared `api/` prefix.

THE REVIEW SCREEN. Each question returns what the learner selected, what was correct, and whether it was skipped - safe because the attempt is already scored. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it is not the ONE place correct answers are published - the passing submit response and the chapter-quiz submit carry them too. On a FAILED attempt at a bank-less assessment the answer key is stripped (`assessment_feedback_permitted` -> `_withhold_assessment_feedback`).

THE LATEST ATTEMPT ONLY. There is no attempt id in the path; a learner reviewing their work means the one they just finished. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: latest ACTIVE attempt made since the current enrolment's `started_at`.

THREE DIFFERENT ABSENCES, THREE DIFFERENT MESSAGES: an unknown course, a course with no assessment configured, and a learner who has never attempted it are all `404` but say which. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: no entitlement is `403 caira_access_required` (`_arefuse_course_step`, no AI Lab check).

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The attempt detail.
403 Forbidden: `caira_access_required`.
404 Not Found: When the course, its assessment configuration, or any
    attempt is absent.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Submit the final assessment, score it, and close the course on a pass.

`POST api/v1/masterclass/<course_id>/assessment/submit/`

UNIVERSAL - the app and the web ask this of the same learner and read the same answer, so it keeps the shared `api/` prefix.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: A PASS DOES NOT CLOSE THE COURSE. It writes the attempt and stamps `UserCourseCompletion.final_assessment_passed_at` in one transaction and answers `next_step: "feedback"`; the closure pipeline that awards CPE, reserves the badge allocation, calls Credly and triggers the certificate runs from `masterclass-feedback-submit-v1`. A CREDLY BADGE CANNOT BE RECALLED once issued, so whatever this endpoint refuses, it refuses BEFORE scoring rather than after.

A PREVIEW-MODE RUN MUST NEVER REACH HERE. `UserEnrollment.course_mode` of `preview` is video-only and can never earn CPE. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOTHING ENFORCES THAT ON THIS ROUTE - no `api/` or `app-api/` Masterclass view reads `course_mode`, and this app's detail read (`masterclass-course-detail-v1`) has no mode; only the WEB course-detail payload withholds `show_final_assessment`. A preview learner can submit, pass and go on to the CPE-awarding feedback step. DEFECT, not fixed here.

THE WHOLE PAPER ARRIVES AT ONCE, unlike the chapter quiz, because the score is computed against the batch and a partial submission has no meaning. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: "the batch" is not recorded - any `questions_to_show` distinct active questions from the bank are accepted.

SCORED SERVER-SIDE against the stored key - which is why the questions read never carries correct answers. On a PASS the response returns every answer graded (`correct_option_ids`, `options_feedback`); a fail returns only the score and message.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: refusals, in order - `409` AI Lab lock and `403 caira_access_required`, `404` no config, `200 reset_required` on an expired window (checked inline), `403 chapters_not_complete`, `403 already_passed` (logged as 409 - DEFECT, not fixed here), `403 cool_off_active`, `400` on an answer count other than `questions_to_show` or an id outside the bank.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

POST
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The score (`passed`, `score_percent`), or `reset_required`.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed body, a wrong answer count or an id
    outside the bank.
403 Forbidden: When the attempt is refused (see the list above).
404 Not Found: When the course or its assessment configuration is
    unknown.
409 Conflict: When the course is closed by its AI Lab.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

The response carries `cpe_awarded`, `badge_issued` and `certificate_triggered`. Guards before the gates: `_arefuse_course_step` with the default `check_expiry=True` - an expired window answers `200 reset_required`, no entitlement `403 caira_access_required`; no AI Lab check.

SUBMITTED ONCE, NEVER EDITED. There is no PATCH here - an evaluation that can be rewritten after the fact is not the record NASBA asks for.

**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Begin a chapter, creating the enrolment and progress row if needed.

`POST api/v1/masterclass/chapter/<chapter_id>/start/`

UNIVERSAL - the app and the web ask this of the same learner and read the same answer, so it keeps the shared `api/` prefix.

THE FIRST WRITE OF THE WHOLE LEARNING FLOW. A learner has no `UserEnrollment` until this runs, so every later read - progress, quiz, assessment - depends on it having happened. Idempotent: starting an already-started chapter re-reads the row rather than duplicating it.

EVERY GUARD RUNS BEFORE THE WRITE, IN THIS ORDER, and each is a distinct answer rather than one generic refusal. RECHECKED 2026-10-07 - the order as the code runs it:

- an unknown or inactive chapter, or one on an inactive course, is a `404`;
- `_arefuse_course_step(check_ai_lab=True)`: a course closed by its AI Lab is `409` with the lab `reason`; no Masterclass entitlement (`can_access_masterclass_course`) is `403` with `reason: caira_access_required`;
- a TEST COURSE is a `404` to anyone without `is_internal_test_user`. It runs AFTER the two checks above, so a caller without entitlement gets the `403`/`409` for a test course rather than the `404` - the course is not invisible to them. DEFECT, not fixed here;
- a chapter the ladder has not unlocked is `403` with `reason: chapter_locked`;
- a 365-day enrolment window that has EXPIRED answers `200` with `reset_required: true`. Progress has already been reset and a new window started, so this is a state change the client must render, not an error;
- a course already started through the 7DC partner flow is `409` with `reason: already_started_via_7dc`: the learner cannot be in both flows at once and the closure pipeline would race. Once the course is closed that override lifts.

No request body is read; whatever is sent is ignored.

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

```
200 OK: On success or on an expired window.
403 Forbidden: `chapter_locked` or `caira_access_required`.
404 Not Found: When the chapter or course is unknown or is a test
    course the caller may not see.
409 Conflict: AI Lab lock, or `already_started_via_7dc`.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

`GET api/v1/masterclass/coming-soon/` - the teaser rail on its own.

THE SAME ROWS `home` ALREADY RETURNS under its `coming_soon` key. It exists so a client that wants only the rail does not have to fetch tracks, bookmarks, completions and continue-watching and throw them away.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: SAME ROWS, NOT THE SAME PROJECTION. This view builds its cards by hand in `level_rails.coming_soon_payload` - keys `id`, `slug`, `name`, `thumbnail_url`, `trailer_url`, `priority`, `fields_of_study`, ordered by `priority` then `course_name` - while `home` uses `MasterclassComingSoonCourseSerializer` - `course_name` (not `name`), `total_cpe_credits`, `instructors`, no `slug` / `priority`, ordered by `priority` alone. The two rails ALREADY disagree about what a coming-soon card is; the shared-projection rule below is not met. Any query parameter is a 400 (`NoQueryParams`), with this view's success sentence as the envelope `message` - DEFECT, not fixed here.

KEEPING THE PROJECTION SHARED IS THE POINT. If the serializer grows a field both surfaces gain it together; forking it here is how the standalone rail and the home rail start disagreeing about what a coming-soon course is.

ENTIRELY USER-AGNOSTIC. A `ComingSoonCourse` is a display artefact - nobody enrols on one, bookmarks one or completes one - so there is no per-user phase and no test-viewer partitioning: these rows are not `Course` rows and carry no `is_test_course` flag to partition on.

POST api/v1/masterclass/course-progress/<course_id>/update/ (legacy: /caira/masterclass/course-progress/<course_id>/update/) Unified video progress update. Accepts a single chapter or bulk list. Updates DB progress and returns full course progress for all chapters. Replaces the combination of video/update + resume-state/save.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: guards in order - strict `400` body, `404` unknown or inactive course, `403 caira_access_required` (no AI Lab check), `404` test course for a non-test user, `200 reset_required` on an expired window, `400` not enrolled, `200` no-op on a closed course. A chapter that is missing or still locked is NOT an error: it is reported under `skipped` with `reason` `not_found` / `chapter_locked` and the rest are applied, one transaction per item.

**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `MasterclassCourseDetailViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `masterclass-course-detail-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One course in full, for the signed-in learner.

`GET api/v1/masterclass/course/<course_id>/`

UNIVERSAL, and the APP-ERA detail read. The web has its own much larger endpoint, `WebMasterclassCourseDetailViewV1`, which additionally serves the SIGNED-OUT page and the cpe/preview mode toggle; this one is post-login only and has neither.

AUTHENTICATION IS MANDATORY HERE. There is no `login_type` parameter, so there is no anonymous branch to serve - a caller without a token is refused by the permission class before the handler runs.

AN UNKNOWN OR INACTIVE COURSE IS A `404`. H-14 makes retirement a soft flag, so "withdrawn" and "never existed" are deliberately the same answer.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE QUERY STRING IS NOT VALIDATED. The handler never reads it, so an undeclared parameter is silently ignored rather than a 400; `CourseDetailQueryV1` (`mode`) in `Masterclass/utils/schemas.py` names this route but nothing imports it. DEFECT, not fixed here. An entitlement miss is NOT a refusal here: the answer is `200` with `course_is_locked` true and every `hls_video_url` nulled.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The course.
401 Unauthorized: Without a valid Bearer token
    (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
404 Not Found: When the course is unknown or inactive.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `MasterclassCoursesByLevelViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `masterclass-courses-by-level-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET api/v1/masterclass/courses-by-level/` - cards grouped by ladder rung.

A FLAT LIST OF CARDS, NOT A LIST OF LEVELS. Every card carries its own `level_details`, which makes the flat shape carry strictly MORE information than a nested one: the client can group it, and a card pulled out of context still knows which rung it came from. Legacy made the same call and for the same reason.

ONE CARD PER COURSE, AND THAT IS NEWLY TRUE HERE. Legacy documented a course linked to two levels appearing TWICE, once per level, and warned against deduping it. That case cannot arise in this tree any more: `uq_course_single_level` (2026-09-30) makes one rung per course a database constraint, so the duplicate the legacy docstring defends against is now impossible rather than merely unwanted.

NO PER-USER OVERLAY. No progress, no bookmark, no continue-watching - exactly as legacy. The learner is read for ONE thing: hiding test courses from everyone who is not a test viewer. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THAT READ IS INERT. It is `getattr(request.user, "is_test_viewer", False)`, and `User` has no such attribute (the field is `is_internal_test_user`), so it is always False and NOBODY - test viewers included - sees a test course here. DEFECT, not fixed here.

Ordering is level `number` ascending, then the per-level `CourseLevelLink.priority` - the rung first, then the editorial order inside it (then course name). RECHECKED 2026-10-07: a REPEATED `level_id` is not a 400 - the query dict keeps only the LAST value before validation (measured on `QueryDict`). Any undeclared parameter is a 400, but that 400's envelope `message` is this view's success sentence (`envelope_message`) - DEFECT, not fixed here. `data` is the card list.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `level_id` - Optional.

**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `MasterclassCertificateWebhookViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `masterclass-certificate-webhook-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

Inbound webhook carrying certificate events from the Masterclass service.

`POST api/v1/masterclass/webhooks/certificate/<id>/`

NOT A LEARNER-FACING ENDPOINT. It is called by the Masterclass service, not by an app or a browser. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it is the one route in this group whose authenticator list is EMPTY; it is not the only `AllowAny` one - `AppMasterclassComplimentaryCourseViewV1` is `AllowAny` too.

`AllowAny` IS NOT "UNAUTHENTICATED" - the mandatory `id` in the path IS the credential. It is the PK of a `UserAccumulatedCertificateBadge` row, so a caller who cannot name an existing one cannot do anything: an unknown id is a `404` and nothing is written.

THE ENVELOPE STILL APPLIES, unlike the four inbound webhooks that are exempt from it - this one is first-party and the sender tolerates it.

Authentication:

```
None - the authenticator is cleared, so no `Authorization` header is read.
```

Permission:

```
AllowAny. PUBLIC - declared, not defaulted.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: When the event is applied; `data` is `{"status": "ok"}`.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed payload. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the
    serializer's error dict carries no `message`/`detail`, so the
    envelope falls back to `envelope_message` and answers
    `success: false` with `message: "Certificate callback accepted."`
    (measured through the URLconf). DEFECT, not fixed here. The body is
    validated BEFORE the row lookup, so a bad body on an unknown id is a
    400, not a 404. An UNDECLARED key is accepted, not refused -
    `MasterclassCertificateWebhookSerializer` is a
    `NonPersistingSerializer`, not a `StrictInputSerializer`
    (measured). DEFECT, not fixed here.
404 Not Found: When the id names no certificate row. A non-UUID id never
    reaches the view - `<uuid:id>` fails URL resolution first, so the
    handler's own "Invalid id UUID." 400 is unreachable.
```

Legacy `ComplimentaryCourseView` (and its V2 twin, which differed only in serializer). Matches the caller's email domain to an `AllowedEmailDomain` and returns the courses every active `ComplimentaryCourseMapping` on that domain grants.

`AllowAny` matches the legacy `OptionalJWTUserPermission`: the endpoint is reachable unauthenticated, and simply returns 400 when there is no email to match - which is what the legacy view did for an anonymous caller. - `course_type` - Optional. Read directly; no validator declares it.

The app's Masterclass home screen, section by section.

`GET app-api/v1/masterclass/home/`

ONE READ PER SCREEN, NOT ONE PER RAIL. The whole home page - every section and the cards inside it - comes back in a single response, so a cold open is one request rather than one per carousel.

THE SHARED STRUCTURE IS CACHED AND THE PER-LEARNER OVERLAY IS NOT. Section layout and course cards are identical for everybody; progress and bookmarks are read live and laid over the top. Folding a user into the shared key would multiply a shared blob by the user base with no invalidation.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: "IDENTICAL FOR EVERYBODY" DOES NOT HOLD FOR TEST COURSES. The shared blob (`COURSES_CATALOG_CACHE_KEY`, 600s + 60s stale) is built from `get_masterclass_course_queryset(request)`, which hides test courses unless the CALLER is `is_internal_test_user` - so whoever misses the cache decides for everyone: a test user's build shows test courses to all learners, an ordinary build hides them from test users. DEFECT, not fixed here. Nothing busts the key on a course write (the Masterclass receivers connect 0); only the admin's question-bank delete calls `invalidate_course_caches`.

TAKES NO PARAMETERS. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: but rejects none either - the query string is never read. DEFECT, not fixed here.

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

```
GET
```

```
200 OK: The sections.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppMasterclassLevelsPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `app-masterclass-levels-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

GET app-api/v1/masterclass/levels-page/ - levels page (tabs + sections + items). (legacy: /caira/masterclass/levels-page/)

Builds the Masterclass levels screen in one call:

- level tabs from `Level` (active, on an active subject; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: ordered by subject name, then number - not number alone),
- left-side section cards from parent `LevelLearningObjective` rows (`parent` is null),
- each section's right-side items from that parent's child rows,
- static page header whose `{level_name}` subtitle token is filled per level.

Query params:

```
`id`: A `Level` UUID. Narrows the response to
    that single level, keeping the identical shape - `levels` simply
    holds one entry - so the client needs no second parsing path.
    A malformed UUID returns 400; a UUID matching no ACTIVE level
    returns 404 (distinguishing "no such level" from "level with no
    sections yet", which is a normal 200 with `sections: []`).
`type`: A parent section title. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: returns a LIST OF
    SECTION objects - every active parent whose title matches
    case-insensitively, across all levels, each with its nested

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: not literally - it is the home-page CARD plus prose (objectives, instructors, skills, topics, tags, NASBA copy fields and a flags-only `miscellaneous_data`), with a different key set from `course-detail`: no `nasba_section`, related-course rails, enrolment or progress keys.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/ai-labs/?login_type=pre_login|post_login`

The AI Labs rail on the web Masterclass home page (maintainer, 2026-10-09): every course that has an AI Lab, as the SAME card the tracks rail serves.

A FLAT LIST, NOT LABS WITH COURSES UNDER THEM. Under the live relation a lab belongs to at most one course, so a tracks-style "lab -> its courses" block would hold one card each. The maintainer chose the flat course list.

`data` IS THE PAGINATION BLOCK - `data.count`, `data.results` - with no key naming the list, the shape `highlight/` answers since 2026-10-09. The list's name is `results` (slug `masterclass_ai_labs_courses_web`), so the bare `?page=` / `?page_size=` form is legal; default 6, max 100.

LOGIN IS HANDLED AS ON `tracks-page/`: `login_type` is required, `post_login` without a token is the same hand-built 401, and a malformed token is the authenticator's 401 on both branches. ONE DIFFERENCE, ON PURPOSE: `pre_login` IGNORES a valid token, so every pre-login card answers `is_bookmarked: false`. tracks-page still passes the user on that branch and its own docstring records that as a defect; it is not repeated here.

NO CACHE, like the tracks rail. Every call reads Postgres.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassAllInstructorsPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-all-instructors-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/all-instructors-page/?search=&page=&page_size=`

The web instructor library: every active instructor's full profile, with the courses each one teaches. Web-only, for the Masterclass web team.

QUERY PARAMETERS:

`search`     Optional. Case-insensitive match on name or designation. `page`       Optional, default 1. Also accepted as `instructors.page`. `page_size`  Optional, default 6, ceiling 100. See `utils.pagination`.

Anything else is a 400, from whichever validator owns it.

PUBLIC, WITH AN OPTIONAL SIGNED-IN OVERLAY. An instructor profile and a course card are catalogue content, so the library is served anonymously. A valid bearer token adds the caller's bookmark state to each card, and a malformed one is still rejected - same contract as the home page.

NO CACHE YET. Every call hits Postgres; the anonymous, search-free pages are the obvious first thing to cache.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `instructors.page` - Optional. Page of the `instructors` list, 1-based. Default 1.
- `instructors.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `instructors` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`instructors`).
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`instructors`).
- `search` - Optional. Matches instructor name or designation, case-insensitive.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFinalAssessmentQuestionsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-assessment-questions-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The final-assessment question batch, with its cooldown state.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/assessment-questions/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassFinalAssessmentQuestionsViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers, NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

THE BATCH IS DRAWN PER ATTEMPT, so two attempts are not guaranteed the same questions - a client must not cache this payload across attempts.

THE COOLDOWN IS PART OF THE ANSWER, not a separate read. A learner inside the wait window after a failed attempt is told when they may retry, so the client renders the timer rather than computing it. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that answer is a `403` with `reason: cool_off_active`, `cool_off_seconds_remaining` and `cool_off_ends_at` - the 200 carries no cooldown state.

NO CORRECT ANSWERS IN THE PAYLOAD. Grading is server-side in the submit endpoint - a NASBA boundary, not a UI preference.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: refusals, in order - `404` course (test courses hidden correctly here, via `get_masterclass_course_queryset`); `409` AI Lab lock and `403 caira_access_required`; `404` no config; `403 chapters_not_complete`; `403 already_passed` (logged as 409 - DEFECT, not fixed here); `403 cool_off_active`. The three gathered reads run one after another, not in parallel.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The questions.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
403 Forbidden: `caira_access_required`, `chapters_not_complete`,
    `already_passed` or `cool_off_active`.
404 Not Found: When the course or its assessment configuration is
    unknown.
409 Conflict: When the course is closed by its AI Lab.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFinalAssessmentResultViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-assessment-result-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The latest final-assessment attempt, question by question.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/assessment-result/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassFinalAssessmentResultViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers, NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

THE REVIEW SCREEN. Each question returns what the learner selected, what was correct, and whether it was skipped. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT THE ONE PLACE correct answers are published - the assessment submit returns them on a pass, and the chapter-quiz submit and a resumed quiz read return them per question. Here they are WITHHELD on a failed attempt against a bank-less assessment (`assessment_feedback_permitted`, NASBA 6.01.2(1)(ii)).

THE LATEST ATTEMPT ONLY. There is no attempt id in the path; a learner reviewing their work means the one they just finished.

THREE DIFFERENT ABSENCES, THREE DIFFERENT MESSAGES: an unknown course, a course with no assessment configured, and a learner who has never attempted it are all `404` but say which. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: between the course and the attempt, no entitlement is `403 caira_access_required` (no AI Lab check on this read); the attempt is the latest within the current lease.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The attempt detail.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
403 Forbidden: `caira_access_required`.
404 Not Found: When the course, its assessment configuration, or any
    attempt is absent.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFinalAssessmentSubmitViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-assessment-submit-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Submit the final assessment, score it, and close the course on a pass.

`POST web-api/v1/masterclass/assessment-submit/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassFinalAssessmentSubmitViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers, NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: A PASS DOES NOT CLOSE THE COURSE. It writes the attempt, stamps `UserCourseCompletion.final_assessment_passed_at` and answers `next_step: "feedback"`; the closure pipeline that awards CPE, issues the Credly badge and triggers the certificate runs from `web-masterclass-feedback-submit-v1`. A CREDLY BADGE CANNOT BE RECALLED once issued, so whatever this endpoint refuses, it refuses BEFORE scoring rather than after. UNLIKE THE APP TWIN, the attempt row and the completion stamp are two separate awaited writes with no `transaction.atomic` around them, so a failure between them leaves a passing attempt with no pass recorded. DEFECT, not fixed here.

A PREVIEW-MODE RUN MUST NEVER REACH HERE. `UserEnrollment.course_mode` of `preview` is video-only and can never earn CPE, which is why the course-detail payload withholds `show_final_assessment` in that mode. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOTHING HERE ENFORCES IT - this handler never reads `course_mode`, so a preview learner who posts the paper is scored, can pass and can go on to the CPE-awarding feedback step. DEFECT, not fixed here.

THE WHOLE PAPER ARRIVES AT ONCE, unlike the chapter quiz, because the score is computed against the batch and a partial submission has no meaning.

SCORED SERVER-SIDE against the stored key - which is why the questions read never carries correct answers. On a PASS the response returns every answer graded (`correct_option_ids`, `options_feedback`); a fail returns only the score and message.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: refusals, in order - body `400`; `404` course; `409` AI Lab lock and `403 caira_access_required`; `404` no config; `200 reset_required` on an expired window; `403 chapters_not_complete`; `403 already_passed` (logged as 409 - DEFECT, not fixed here); `403 cool_off_active`; `400` on a wrong answer count or an id outside the bank.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The score (`passed`, `score_percent`), or `reset_required`.
400 Bad Request: Malformed body, wrong answer count or a foreign id.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
403 Forbidden: When the attempt is refused (see the order above).
404 Not Found: When the course or its assessment configuration is
    unknown.
409 Conflict: When the course is closed by its AI Lab.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

SCOPED TO THE AUTHENTICATED LEARNER - the path names the course, never the user, so a client cannot bookmark on somebody else's behalf.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassChapterStartViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-chapter-start-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Begin a chapter, creating the enrolment and progress row if needed.

`POST web-api/v1/masterclass/chapter-start/<chapter_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassChapterStartViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share the guard helpers (`_arefuse_course_step`, `ais_chapter_locked`, `acheck_enrollment_expiry`), NOT the handler - this class carries its own copy of the handler body - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

THE FIRST WRITE OF THE WHOLE LEARNING FLOW. A learner has no `UserEnrollment` until this runs, so every later read - progress, quiz, assessment - depends on it having happened. Idempotent: starting an already-started chapter re-reads the row rather than duplicating it.

EVERY GUARD RUNS BEFORE THE WRITE, IN THIS ORDER, and each is a distinct answer rather than one generic refusal. RECHECKED 2026-10-07 - the order as the code runs it:

- an unknown or inactive chapter, or one on an inactive course, is a `404`;
- `_arefuse_course_step(check_ai_lab=True)`: a course closed by its AI Lab is `409` with the lab `reason`; no Masterclass entitlement is `403` with `reason: caira_access_required`;
- a TEST COURSE is a `404` to EVERY caller, internal testers included: the guard reads `getattr(request.user, 'is_test_viewer', False)`, an attribute `User` does not have (the flag is `is_internal_test_user`). DEFECT, not fixed here;
- a chapter the ladder has not unlocked is `403` with `reason: chapter_locked`;
- a 365-day enrolment window that has EXPIRED answers `200` with `reset_required: true`. Progress has already been reset and a new window started, so this is a state change the client must render, not an error;
- a course already started through the 7DC partner flow is `409` with `reason: already_started_via_7dc`: the learner cannot be in both flows at once and the closure pipeline would race. Once the course is closed that override lifts.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: On success or on an expired window.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
403 Forbidden: `chapter_locked` or `caira_access_required`.
404 Not Found: When the chapter or course is unknown or is a test
    course (for every caller - see above).
409 Conflict: AI Lab lock, or `already_started_via_7dc`.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

**Surface:** WEB

**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-coming-soon-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/coming-soon/` - the teaser rail, web half.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NO HOME PAGE CARRIES THESE ROWS IN THIS SHAPE. The web tracks page dropped `coming_soon` on 2026-10-07, and the app home builds it through `MasterclassComingSoonCourseSerializer` (different keys and order). This rail is `level_rails.coming_soon_payload` paged as the standard block under `results` (slug `coming_soon_web`, default 6, max 100). Any other query parameter is a 400 (`NoQueryParams`). A DatabaseError is not caught - measured, it escaped as Django's HTML 500. DEFECT, not fixed here.

SIGNED OUT IS THE NORMAL CASE HERE. A coming-soon course is a display artefact with no enrolment, progress or bookmark story, so the payload is byte-identical for every caller including none - `AllowAny` costs nothing and lets the rail render on a marketing page. The app twin stays authenticated because every app endpoint is.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`results`).
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`results`).

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassCourseDetailViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-course-detail-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/course-detail/<course_id>/?login_type=`

The web course page, for BOTH SIDES OF LOGIN since 2026-10-07 (maintainer).

ONE ENDPOINT FOR BOTH LOGIN STATES, NOT TWO, and the same reasoning as `WebMasterclassTracksPageViewV1` and `WebWebinarMainPageViewV1`: the two surfaces answer the same question about the same course and share every visibility rule, which is exactly where two endpoints drift apart. The parameter selects the surface.

AUTHENTICATION IS OPTIONAL AT THE FRAMEWORK LAYER AND MANDATORY AT THE APPLICATION LAYER. DRF resolves `permission_classes` during dispatch, BEFORE the view can read `login_type`, so `IsAuthenticated` would 401 the anonymous caller this page now exists to serve and no permission class can branch on a query parameter it has not been handed. `AllowAny` plus an explicit check in `get()` is therefore the design, not a relaxation:

- `pre_login`  - served anonymously. A bearer token, if sent, is resolved and then IGNORED; the caller asked for the signed-out page.
- `post_login` - refused with 401 unless the request authenticated.

A MALFORMED TOKEN IS REJECTED ON BOTH BRANCHES, including `pre_login`. `JWTAuthentication` returns None when there is no `Authorization` header and RAISES for a header that is present but bad, so a client sending a broken token sees the problem instead of being silently downgraded to the anonymous page.

THE TWO RESPONSES CARRY THE IDENTICAL KEY SET. Both run `_web_course_state_overlay`; the pre-login branch simply hands it an empty `_CourseUserState`. So `is_bookmarked` is `false` rather than absent, RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `enrollment` is present as `null` on both for a learner who has none (a `SerializerMethodField`), and the chapter lock ladder is the same one a signed-in learner with no progress sees. One client component renders both pages, and a key added to the overlay reaches both at once.

NOTHING PLAYABLE PRE-LOGIN. `_CourseUserState` defaults `course_is_locked` to True, and the overlay strips every `hls_video_url` when it is set, so an anonymous visitor browses the course and its chapter metadata and streams none of it. That is the same rule `can_access_masterclass_course` applies post-login, taken at its safe end rather than asked.

THE GLOBAL KEYS ARE SERVED ON BOTH SIDES, because they are what a marketing page is for: `total_cpe_credits`, `show_credly_icon`, `credly_badge_name`, the NASBA boilerplate, the related and instructor-related rails, and the full chapter list.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: TWO CACHES, AND ONLY ONE IS READ PRE-LOGIN. The shared course base is cached globally and is the expensive half; the per-user response cache is keyed on `user.id` and the mode and is never touched anonymously. The anonymous overlay costs one small assessment-config read, one CPE read and pure Python on top of the global entry - the obvious next cache if it shows up in a profile.

`login_type` IS REQUIRED. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `mode` was NOT removed; `WebCourseDetailQueryV1` declares it (post-login only, a 400 pre-login) and `get` passes it to `_for_user`. BREAKING for a caller that sends no `login_type`.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:

- `chapters.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `chapters` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.

- `mode` - Optional. One of: `cpe`, `preview`. cpe or preview. POST-LOGIN ONLY. Omit to keep the mode already stored on the enrollment.
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`chapters`).
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`chapters`).

POST web-api/v1/masterclass/course-progress-update/<course_id>/ (legacy: /caira/masterclass/course-progress/<course_id>/update/) Unified video progress update. Accepts a single chapter or bulk list. Updates DB progress and returns full course progress for all chapters. Replaces the combination of video/update + resume-state/save.

Chapters that are unknown or locked are reported in `skipped` rather than refused. Shares helpers with the app twin, not the handler.

**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassUnifiedCourseProgressGetViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-course-progress-get-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Every chapter's progress for one course, plus the flags that drive the UI.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/course-progress/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassUnifiedCourseProgressGetViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share `abuild_full_course_progress`, NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

THE ONE READ A PLAYER SCREEN NEEDS: per-chapter progress, the RESUME POSITION, the enrolment window, and the two flags a client would otherwise derive - `show_quiz` and `show_final_assessment`.

THE FLAGS ARE COMPUTED HERE SO TWO CLIENTS CANNOT DISAGREE. Deriving "may they sit the assessment yet" in the app and again on the web is how the two drift, and one of those drifts issues a credential that cannot be recalled.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: PREVIEW MODE DOES NOT SUPPRESS EITHER FLAG. `abuild_full_course_progress` never reads `UserEnrollment.course_mode`, so a preview learner sees `show_quiz` / `show_final_assessment` exactly as a CPE learner does - unlike the web course-detail page. DEFECT, not fixed here. Entitlement is not a refusal either: the answer is `200` with `course_is_locked`. An unknown or inactive course is `404`; a test course is NOT hidden on this read. Undeclared query parameters are ignored.

THE WRITE HALF IS A DIFFERENT ENDPOINT - `masterclass-course-progress-update-v1` (on this surface, `web-masterclass-course-progress-update-v1`) - which is what replaced the deprecated `progress/video/update/`.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The progress map.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
404 Not Found: When the course is unknown.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassCourseSectionViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-course-section-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/course-section/` (legacy: `/masterclass-web/Masterclass_Course_Section/`)

Returns the web-targeted "Masterclass" homepage section grouped by CAIRA Masterclass level. Logic is replicated from `caira/views.py::CAIRAMainPageViewV3` (the `elif name == "CAIRA Masterclass Course Section"` branch) but the response shape is web-specific:

- Top-level `heading` / `subheading` are HARDCODED for this web surface (admin's PageLayout copy is different - the web team wants its own wording).
- RECHECKED 2026-10-07: PAGINATED, AND FLAT. `all_courses` is the standard pagination block (slug `course_section_courses_web`, default 6, max 100, `?all_courses.page=` or bare `?page=`) over a FLAT list of course rows, each carrying its `level` int inline - not an array of per-level groups. The two bullets that stood here (no `count`, no pagination; `all_courses` as three `{level, courses}` groups) are dead.

SINCE 2026-09-08 levels belong to a `Subject` (CAIRA, CAIBA, ...) and `level` is unique only within one, so across two programmes the value `1` appears twice (RECHECKED 2026-10-07: on flat rows, not in groups). Every course row therefore carries `subject_id` and `subject_name`, and the flat ordering is `(subject_name ASC, level ASC, per-level priority ASC)` so a programme's ladder stays contiguous instead of interleaving with the next one's.

- Course fields are snake-case, trimmed to the set FE actually uses, and extended with `course_description` + `course_field_of_study` + `course_has_badge`.

Public - no JWT required. **No caching** - every request runs the underlying queries fresh so admin edits surface immediately.

Concurrency - RECHECKED 2026-10-07: four queries are `asyncio.gather`-ed (levels + level-attached courses + badge configs + Fields-of-Study M2M). None depend on another's output, but Django's async ORM runs them one after another on the single sync thread, so wall-clock is the SUM, not max(q1..q4).

**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassCoursesByLevelViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-courses-by-level-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/courses-by-level/` - the web half.

IT LIVES HERE, NOT IN `MasterclassWeb` (maintainer, 2026-10-01): every Masterclass API - app, web and universal - belongs to this app. The surfaces still get their own endpoint and their own view class, which is the rule that matters; what they no longer get is their own module, so a change to the rail is read in one file instead of two.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT THE ONLY DIFFERENCE FROM THE APP TWIN. This one is reachable signed out (`AllowAny`; the app twin keeps `IsAuthenticated`), AND it pages the cards: `data` is the standard pagination block under the registry key `results` (slug `courses_by_level_web`, default 6, max 100, bare `?page=` / `?page_size=` legal), where the app twin's `data` is the bare card list. It also has no `envelope_message`, so its 400 says "The request could not be completed." A DatabaseError is not caught here - measured with the database down, it escaped as Django's HTML 500, not the envelope. DEFECT, not fixed here.

NO `login_type` PARAMETER, and not by oversight. The other web endpoints take one because their payload CHANGES across login; this rail has no per-user field at all. A parameter selecting between two identical shapes would be a question with one answer, and a strict model would then 400 a client for omitting something that could not have mattered.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: LOGIN CHANGES NOTHING, TEST COURSES INCLUDED. The read is `getattr(request.user, "is_test_viewer", False)` and `User` has no such attribute (the flag is `is_internal_test_user`), so it is False for every caller and an internal tester never sees a test course here either. DEFECT, not fixed here.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `level_id` - Optional.
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`results`).
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`results`).
- `results.page` - Optional. Page of the `results` list, 1-based. Default 1.
- `results.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `results` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassCourseEnrollmentViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-enrollment-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

This learner's enrolment window for one course - READ ONLY.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/enrollment/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassCourseEnrollmentViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share no handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other. No entitlement check runs here; the query string is not read.

THE 365-DAY COUNTDOWN, AND NOTHING ELSE. It reports when the window opened, when it closes and how long is left, so a client shows the banner without deriving it.

READ-ONLY BY DESIGN. Enrolment is CREATED by starting a chapter, never by calling this, so there is no POST here and a client cannot enrol a learner into a course they have not opened.

A LEARNER WITH NO ENROLMENT IS A `200` DESCRIBING THAT STATE, not a 404 - "not enrolled yet" is a normal thing for a course page to render.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The enrolment state.
404 Not Found: When the course is unknown.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFeedbackQuestionsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-feedback-questions-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The post-course feedback form.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/feedback-questions/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassFeedbackQuestionsViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers, NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

GATED ON HAVING PASSED THE ASSESSMENT. A learner who has not passed is `403` with `reason: assessment_not_passed` - feedback is the last step of the completion flow, not an opinion box open from the start. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: before that, no entitlement is `403 caira_access_required` (`_arefuse_course_step`, no AI Lab check, no window reset).

ALREADY SUBMITTED IS ALSO `403`, with `reason: feedback_already_submitted`. The two refusals are distinguishable so the client can say "finish the assessment first" or "thanks, we have this" rather than showing one generic wall.

NASBA REQUIRES THE EVALUATION, which is why this sits between the pass and the certificate rather than beside them.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The form.
403 Forbidden: A `reason` when the assessment is not passed or
    feedback is already in.
404 Not Found: When the course is unknown.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFeedbackSubmitViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-feedback-submit-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Submit the post-course feedback.

`POST web-api/v1/masterclass/feedback-submit/<course_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassFeedbackSubmitViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers (`_arefuse_course_step`, `async_execute_course_closure_pipeline`), NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class.

THE LAST STEP BEFORE THE CERTIFICATE IS DOWNLOADABLE. The same two gates as the questions read, and for the same reason: `403 assessment_not_passed` before a pass, `403 feedback_already_submitted` after one submission. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: before those, `_arefuse_course_step` runs with the expiry check ON (no AI Lab check): `200 reset_required` on an expired window, `403 caira_access_required` without entitlement. A success runs the course CLOSURE PIPELINE (CPE, Credly badge, certificate) and answers `feedback_submitted`, `cpe_awarded`, `badge_issued`, `certificate_triggered`.

SUBMITTED ONCE, NEVER EDITED. There is no PATCH here - an evaluation that can be rewritten after the fact is not the record NASBA asks for.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: On success.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed body.
403 Forbidden: A `reason` when not passed or already submitted.
404 Not Found: When the course is unknown.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

Body template generated from `FeedbackSubmitRequest`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassFilterViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-filter-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/filter/` - the Masterclass Web Filter.

The web catalogue filter page: one paginated course list plus every option the filter sidebar can offer. Web-only, for the Masterclass web team.

QUERY PARAMETERS - every filter is multi-select and comma-separated; values in one parameter are OR-ed, separate parameters are AND-ed:

`instructor`           Instructor UUIDs. `field_of_study`       Field-of-study UUIDs. `additional_category`  Additional-category UUIDs (CAS, Tax, Audit). `level`                Level UUIDs. `cpe_credit`           `lt_2` / `2_to_5` / `gt_5`, on the derived

```
CPE total. 2 and 5 sit in the middle band.
```

`track`                Track UUIDs. `content_type`         `masterclass_course` / `ai_kit` / `podcast`

```
/ `reel` / `nano_learning` / `micro_learning`.
```

`page` / `page_size` Default 6, ceiling 100. Also `courses.page`.

Anything else is a 400 naming the parameter.

THE RESPONSE:

`filters`  Every option, with the id or value to send back. Not narrowed

```
by the current selection, so the sidebar stays stable.
```

`applied`  The selection as the server understood it, normalised. `courses`  The standard pagination block of home-page course cards, each

```
with `content_type`, `reels_subtype`, `instructors` and
`additional_categories` added.
```

PUBLIC, WITH AN OPTIONAL SIGNED-IN OVERLAY - the same contract as the home page and the instructor library: a valid token adds bookmark state, and a malformed one is rejected rather than silently ignored.

NO CACHE YET. The `filters` block is identical for every visitor and is the obvious first thing to cache.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `additional_category` - Optional. Comma-separated.
- `content_type` - Optional. Comma-separated. Any of: `masterclass_course`, `ai_kit`, `podcast`, `reel`, `nano_learning`, `micro_learning`.
- `courses.page` - Optional. Page of the `courses` list, 1-based. Default 1.
- `courses.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `courses` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.
- `cpe_credit` - Optional. Comma-separated. Any of: `lt_2`, `2_to_5`, `gt_5`.
- `field_of_study` - Optional. Comma-separated.
- `instructor` - Optional. Comma-separated.
- `level` - Optional. Comma-separated.
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`courses`).
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100. Bare form, accepted because this route paginates one list (`courses`).
- `track` - Optional. Comma-separated.

**Surface:** WEB

**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-global-search-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/global-search/?q=<text>` - Global Search.

The web header's search box: one query across everything a Masterclass visitor can browse. Web-only, for the Masterclass web team.

THE THIRTEEN GROUPS, in payload order, each its own pagination block:

`courses`                Courses, podcasts and reels. Found by title,

```
description or subject, OR by anything attached
```

- instructor, field of study, additional category, track, level, topic, skill, tool, tag, AI Kit. Each card says why in `matched_on`. `coming_soon`            Coming-soon teasers, by name. `chapters`               Chapters of visible courses, by name or summary. `instructors`            Active instructors, by name or designation. `fields_of_study` / `ai_kits` / `additional_categories` / `tracks` / `levels` / `topics` / `skills` / `tools` / `tags` Taxonomy rows carried by at least one visible course. Five carry a `filter` hint naming the Masterclass Web Filter parameter that lists their courses.

Results rank exact name matches first, then prefix matches, then the rest.

QUERY PARAMETERS:

`q`          Required, 2 to 100 characters. `types`      Optional comma-separated group keys. Only those run. `<group>.page` / `<group>.page_size`

```
Per group; default 6, ceiling 100. With exactly one
`types` value the bare `page` / `page_size` work too.
```

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SEARCHED: video transcripts (a substring scan of every transcript per keystroke), and `AllowedEmailDomain.company_name`, which is an access-grant table - publishing which companies get free access on an anonymous endpoint is a disclosure, not a search result.

PUBLIC, WITH AN OPTIONAL SIGNED-IN OVERLAY, like the filter page. NO CACHE YET: every keystroke is up to 26 queries, so the client should debounce. RECHECKED 2026-10-07 (counted off the code): 26 is only the count + slice per group. `GET web-api/v1/masterclass/highlight/`

Web-only endpoint that returns the admin-configured pinned courses (`PinnedCourseLink`, by `priority`) for the CAIRA Masterclass homepage.

THE TRACKS-PAGE CARD, SINCE 2026-10-09 (maintainer). Each row is built by `_home_course_cards` - the same function behind `tracks-page/` and `about-course/` - so a pinned course describes itself here exactly as it does on the tracks rail: `title`, `short_description`, `thumbnails`, `subject`, `fields_of_study`, `total_cpe_credits`, `has_individual_badge`, `has_additional_resources`, `is_bookmarked`, `first_chapter` and the rest. The legacy `course_*` keys, `course_instructors`, `course_trailer_thumbnail` and `active_in_challenge` went with the old shape.

`status: true` AND THE `all_courses` WRAPPER WERE DROPPED AT THE SAME TIME (maintainer, 2026-10-09). The envelope already answers `success`, and with one list on the page a key naming it is redundant, so `data` IS the pagination block: `data.count`, `data.results`.

Public - no JWT required. A valid bearer token fills `is_bookmarked` / `bookmark_id`; a malformed one is a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`. **No caching** - pinned-course admin edits surface on the very next call.

Test courses are excluded for every caller. The list keeps the name `all_courses` in the query string (`?all_courses.page=`, or the bare `?page=`) and slug `top_section_courses_web`; the rest of the query string is not validated (see `_rail_pagination`).

**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassLevelsProgressViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-levels-progress-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

GET web-api/v1/masterclass/levels-progress/ - slim CAIRA level 1/2/3 progress view. (legacy: /caira/levels_progress/)

RECHECKED 2026-10-07 - MUCH OF THE DESCRIPTION BELOW IS THE 2026-08-20 PORT AND NO LONGER HOLDS. As the code runs today:

- THE LADDER COMES FROM THE DATABASE, not the constant: every `Level` with `active=True`, ordered `(subject__name, number)`, every programme, its target from `Level.cpe_threshold`. `MASTERCLASS_LEVELS_WITH_IMAGES` is only the CAIRA artwork fallback (`_caira_fallback_image`). The count is not fixed at 3. It does NOT filter `subject__active`, so a level of a soft-deleted programme still appears here, unlike `levels/` and the course section. DEFECT, not fixed here.
- BADGE ROWS ARE KEYED BY LEVEL UUID, not `level__number`.
- `prev_target` (the Locked rule) resets per programme, and the Ongoing-first rotation is applied WITHIN each programme's block.
- `levels` IS A PAGINATION BLOCK (slug `levels_progress_levels_web`, default 6, max 100, `?levels.page=` or bare `?page=`), paged after the rotation. Each row also carries `level_id`, `level_actual_name`, `subject_id`, `subject_name`, `credly_assertion_id` and `credly_pdf_certificate_for_level`.
- On the wire the body is `{success, message, data: {total_cpe_credits, levels}}` - the renderer unwraps the hand-built `{status, data}`.
- Any non-pagination query parameter is discarded unvalidated (`?bogus=1` reached the database, measured). DEFECT, not fixed here.

Focused subset of `/caira/get_all_badges_V4/` - RECHECKED 2026-10-07: returns every active level from the database (see the block above), overlaid with the authenticated user's current total CPE credits. No per-course routing, no archived buckets - designed for FE surfaces that need just the "Locked / Ongoing / Completed" state to render level cards.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: per-level inputs come from `Level` (`name`, `level_actual_name`, `number`, `cpe_threshold`, `image_url`); `MASTERCLASS_LEVELS_WITH_IMAGES` supplies only fallback CAIRA artwork.

Per-user inputs:

- `UserAccumulatedTotalCPECredits.total_cpe_credits` - the same superset value `CAIRAGetAllBadgesV4View` uses as `grand_total` (sum of CAIRA + Non-CAIRA credits, lines 5756-5758 in V4).
- `UserLevelProgress` joined to `credly_allocation` - supplies the per-level Credly badge detail set (mirrors the course-detail surface): `credly_accept_or_claim_url` (accept / claim link), `credly_accepted_url` (final share-able badge URL once issued), `credly_badge_image_url` (badge image), and `credly_badge_claimed` (user clicked accept-URL bool). RECHECKED 2026-10-07: rows are keyed by LEVEL UUID, not level number - numbers repeat across programmes.

Status rules mirror V4 (lines 5769-5774), with "previous" reset at each programme boundary (RECHECKED 2026-10-07):

- `Locked`    - total < previous level's cap.
- `Ongoing`   - previous level's cap <= total < this level's cap.
- `Completed` - total >= this level's cap.

Response shape - RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the body BUILT, before the renderer turns it into `{success, message, data}`; `levels` is now a pagination block whose `results` holds these rows, and each row carries more keys (see the block above)::

```
{
  "status": true,
  "data": {
    "total_cpe_credits": 12.5,
    "levels": [
      {
        "level_number": 1,
        "level_name": "level 1",
        "target_cpe": 30,
        "progress": "12.5/30",
        "status": "Ongoing",
        "lms_web_badge_image_url": "https://.../CAIRA_LMS_WEB_Badges/Level1CAIRA.jpg",
        "credly_accept_or_claim_url": null,
        "credly_accepted_url": null,
        "credly_badge__actual_image_url_from_credly": null,
        "credly_badge_name": "CAIRA level 1 - Bronze",
        "credly_badge_claimed": false
      },
      {"level_number": 2, "...": "...", "credly_badge_claimed": false},
      {"level_number": 3, "...": "...", "credly_badge_claimed": false}
    ]
  }
}
```

level ordering: RECHECKED 2026-10-07: each PROGRAMME's block is rotated so the user's currently-Ongoing level in it appears FIRST, followed by the remaining levels in natural order wrapping around; blocks stay in programme-name order. Examples (one 3-level programme):

- user on level 1 (Ongoing)  -> [1, 2, 3]
- user on level 2 (Ongoing)  -> [2, 3, 1]
- user on level 3 (Ongoing)  -> [3, 1, 2]
- No Ongoing level (all Locked or all Completed) -> [1, 2, 3] (natural ascending order; no rotation when there's nothing to surface).

`level_number` always carries the original 1/2/3 identity, so the FE can still detect which level it's rendering regardless of array position.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: pagination params only (others are silently dropped - see above). No write side-effects. The level count is whatever `Level` holds; a new level is an admin row, not a constant edit.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassLevelsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-levels-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The CAIRA ladder for the web - levels only, no courses.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/levels/`

THE WEB HALF OF `app-masterclass-levels-v1`, AND DELIBERATELY NOT THE SAME PAYLOAD. The app route answers the ladder SCREEN, so every level carries its full `courses` array; this one answers the ladder itself - the three levels, their editorial titles, their badges and their copy - which is what a web page needs to render a chooser before anything is picked. A client that wants the courses of one level calls `web-masterclass-courses-by-level-v1`.

SEPARATE CLASS OVER A SHARED FUNCTION, never a subclass of the app view: sharing the API class is what couples two clients on different release cycles, and these two do not even return the same keys.

NOT CACHED, deliberately. It is ONE query returning a handful of rows - the ladder is three levels per programme - and both of this app's level caches are keyed for payloads that carry course cards. A cache here would buy a few milliseconds and cost a registry key plus an invalidation story on every `Level` write.

`description` AND `image_url` ARE THE LEVEL'S OWN (maintainer, 2026-10-07). `Subject` carries a `description`, a `mini_description` and three image URLs of its own; none of them is served here.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated. Matches the app ladder; there is no pre-login variant
of this route today.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: RECHECKED 2026-10-07: on the wire `{success, message, data:
    [...]}` - the renderer lifts `message`, unwraps `data` and drops
    the hand-built `status`.
401 Unauthorized: No or bad token, with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
    realm="api"`.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE QUERY STRING IS NEVER READ, so an undeclared parameter (`?bogus=1`) is ignored rather than refused - measured, it reached the database. DEFECT, not fixed here. Not paginated: no `slug_registry` row.

**Methods on this view:** GET

One chapter's quiz questions for this learner.

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/quiz-questions/<chapter_id>/`

THE WEB SURFACE of this flow. Its twin on the shared `api/` prefix is `MasterclassChapterQuizQuestionsViewV1`; RECHECKED 2026-10-07: they share helpers (`_arefuse_course_step`, `ais_chapter_locked`, `aget_random_questions`), NOT the handler - each class has its own copy - and never the API class, so two clients on different release cycles cannot block each other.

THE CORRECT ANSWER IS NOT IN THIS PAYLOAD FOR AN UNANSWERED QUESTION. Fresh questions come back with their options only; grading happens server-side in the submit endpoint, so a client cannot mark its own work. request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebMasterclassTracksPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `Masterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `web-masterclass-tracks-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/masterclass/tracks-page/?login_type=pre_login|post_login`

The web Masterclass landing page, for both sides of login.

ONE ENDPOINT FOR BOTH LOGIN STATES, NOT TWO, and the same reasoning as `WebWebinarMainPageViewV1`: the two surfaces answer the same question and share their visibility rules, which is exactly where two endpoints drift apart. The parameter selects the surface.

AUTHENTICATION IS OPTIONAL AT THE FRAMEWORK LAYER AND MANDATORY AT THE APPLICATION LAYER. DRF resolves `permission_classes` during dispatch, BEFORE the view can read `login_type`, so `IsAuthenticated` would 401 the anonymous caller this endpoint exists to serve and no permission class can branch on a query parameter it has not been handed. `AllowAny` plus an explicit check in `get()` is therefore the design, not a relaxation:

- `pre_login`  - served anonymously. A bearer token, if sent, is resolved and then ignored; the caller asked for the signed-out page. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT FULLY IGNORED - `get` passes the resolved `user` to `_home_payload_sync` on both branches, so the cards carry that user's `is_bookmarked` / `bookmark_id`; only `is_test_user` is forced False. DEFECT, not fixed here (the course-detail page does ignore it).
- `post_login` - refused with 401 unless the request authenticated. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that 401 is hand-built (`code: authentication_required`) and carries no `WWW-Authenticate` header (measured).

A MALFORMED TOKEN IS REJECTED ON BOTH BRANCHES, including `pre_login`. `JWTAuthentication` returns `None` when there is no `Authorization` header and RAISES for a header that is present but bad, so a client sending a broken token sees the problem instead of being silently downgraded to the anonymous page. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that rejection is 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`, because `JWTAuthentication` now implements `authenticate_header()` (measured).

ONE SECTION, SINCE THE 2026-10-07 NARROWING:

`tracks`   Every active track with its courses, ordered by the

```
`CourseTrackLink` priority. Both sides of login.
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: login does NOT change which courses a
track shows - both sides read `_home_visible_courses()`.
```

FOUR SECTIONS LEFT ON 2026-10-07: `coming_soon`, and the three post-login rails `highlight_courses` (editorial, from `PinnedCourseLink`), `in_progress_courses` and `completed_courses` (`UserCourseCompletion.is_course_closed`). RECHECKED 2026-10-07: three of them ARE served elsewhere, in other shapes - `coming-soon/`, `highlight/` (the same pinned courses) and `completed-course-section/`; only an in-progress rail has no web route. Their registry rows are RETIRED rather than deleted, so their published slugs cannot be reused, and their builders were removed with them - git holds the queries if any of the four comes back on a route of its own.

`PinnedCourseLink` ITSELF IS STILL LIVE. Dropping the rail did not orphan the model: `Homepage.views` still orders the app home page by its `priority` through a `Min` annotation. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: and `WebMasterclassHighlightViewV1` still reads it (`pinned_links`).

KNOWN LIMITS OF THIS PASS, none of them silent:

- NO CACHE. Every call hits Postgres. The anonymous response is identical for every visitor and is the obvious first thing to cache.
- EVERY RAIL PAGINATES, addressed by its own response key - `?tracks.page=2&tracks.page_size=6`, `?tracks.courses.page_size=4`. Default 6 per rail, ceiling 100. See `utils.pagination` for why a bare `?page=` is refused here: two lists are in flight and it cannot say which it meant. `?track=<slug>` narrows `tracks` to one track so its nested `courses` list can be paged past its first page - and since 2026-10-07 the nested block's own `next` carries that selector, so the link is followable rather than a 400.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `login_type` - Required. One of: `pre_login`, `post_login`. pre_login or post_login. Required; never inferred.
- `track` - Optional. Track slug. Narrows `tracks` to that one track so its `courses` list can be paged past page 1.
- `tracks.courses.page` - Optional. Page of the `tracks.courses` list, 1-based. Default 1.
- `tracks.courses.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `tracks.courses` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.
- `tracks.page` - Optional. Page of the `tracks` list, 1-based. Default 1.
- `tracks.page_size` - Optional. Rows per page of the `tracks` list. Default 6, ceiling 100.

**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Submit the lab's feedback, then close the lab.

Enforcement point for gate 3, and the ONLY place the lab's closure runs. Order matters and is deliberate:

```
1. Check the gate (403 if the AI assessment is still pending).
2. Write the feedback responses.
3. Latch `ai_lab_feedback_submitted`.
4. Close the lab: CPE ledger row when it carries credit, then
   `is_course_closed`; then the lab's certificate; then the parent
   course, if this was the last lab of its set.
```

Step 3 must FOLLOW step 2, and `ailab_feedback_needs_ai_assessment` means the flag cannot be set before the gate is open either way - the database backstops the same rule the service checks.

Step 4 is SKIPPED ENTIRELY when step 3 reports the flag was already set, which is what makes a double submit harmless. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that 200 `already_submitted` branch is reached only by a CONCURRENT duplicate; a later sequential submit is refused first by `_feedback_gate_refusal` with 403 `feedback_already_submitted`.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: A NASBA REFUSAL STRANDS THE LAB. Step 3 latches before step 4 runs the NASBA gate; on `nasba_conditions_unmet` the lab is left open, and every retry is then refused 403 `feedback_already_submitted` before `_run_closure`. `close_ai_lab_for_user` has no other caller, so that lab can never close or award through this API. DEFECT, not fixed here.

**Module:** `AILabs.views`  
**Route name:** `ai-lab-course-release-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated, IsAdminUser

Release an AI Lab enrollment, reopening the course it closed.

ADMIN ONLY. Entering a lab now closes its parent course PERMANENTLY - no access window reopens it - and release is the single exit from that. A learner who could call it themselves could enter a lab, release, take the course, and collect both credits; and one who called it by accident would silently lose the lab path they had already started. It is an operator unlock, so it carries an operator's permission.

The mirror of the 7DC course-released contract. Sets `ai_lab_enrollment_active=False` - which is what lifts the lock - and stamps the `released_from_ai_lab*` audit trio. The row is never deleted (H-14).

Idempotent: releasing an already-released enrollment returns `200` with `already_released=True` rather than an error, so a caller retrying after a timeout does not have to special-case it.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: IT CAN ONLY RELEASE THE CALLER'S OWN ROW. The lookup is `user=request.user` and `AILabReleaseRequestV1` carries no learner handle (only `ai_lab_course_id`, `reason`, `external_ref`), so an admin can release an enrollment only on a lab they themselves started; a learner's lock is reachable only through the admin action `release_selected_enrollments`. DEFECT, not fixed here. It also does not call `aclear_lab_path_if_abandoned` (0 callers), and the parent course reopens only if no OTHER unreleased lab under it exists and no lab has paid (`acourse_locked_by_lab`).

**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Start an AI Lab. Idempotent, and the enforcement point for the gate.

Idempotent: the first call creates the `AILabUserEnrollment` row with the lab's own access window; subsequent calls return the existing row untouched. A RELEASED row is REVIVED rather than duplicated, because `(user, ai_lab_course)` is unique - the revival re-stamps the clock and clears the release audit fields. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: an EXPIRED row is revived the same way, and revival also resets `ai_lab_enrollment_is_course_closed` / `_closed_at` while leaving every gate flag (video, quiz, assessment, feedback, CPE) as it was.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: refuses with `409` when `get_ai_lab_lock_state` locks the lab, keyed on the lab's PARENT course (`AILabCourse.masterclass_course`), not on child courses. `reason` is `credit_already_earned_via_course` (the parent's final assessment passed or its own CPE row exists) or `started_via_masterclass_course` (a live enrollment on the parent, no lab under it ever entered, and no lab has paid); the body carries `masterclass_course_id`. The code `locked_by_masterclass_course` is never produced here. The other half of the rule belongs to the Masterclass chapter-start handler.

**No request body by design.** Marks the course started; the id is in the path.

One practical's state, for the mobile app.

`GET app-api/v1/ai-labs/assignment-status/<uuid>/`

The caller's practical state, reconciling it when it is still open.

THIS READ DOUBLES AS THE MISSED-WEBHOOK RECONCILER, and that is why it exists in this shape: THE LABS SERVICE DOES NOT RETRY A FAILED WEBHOOK DELIVERY. A result we were down for is gone from their outbox and lives only behind their results read.

So whenever the stored row is still waiting, this read polls them once before answering and applies anything it finds through the same latch the webhook uses. The client polls this anyway to drive its spinner, so a missed webhook SELF-HEALS on the next tick with no cron or beat task chasing it. A grading window of one to three minutes is short enough that the learner is still watching.

A COMPLETED ROW IS ANSWERED FROM THE DATABASE WITH NO OUTBOUND CALL. Once latched there is nothing left to reconcile, and the latch would refuse a change anyway. `reconciled` on the response says which path ran.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the poll never runs today - the SSO handle is read as the non-existent `User.user_id`, so reconcile is always idle. DEFECT, not fixed here; see the shared handler.

THE PLATFORM TOKEN NEVER LEAVES THIS PROCESS. `AI_LABS_API_TOKEN` identifies the PLATFORM, not the learner, so a frontend holding it could read as anybody. The client calls with its own JWT and the SSO handle is resolved server-side; the labs service only ever hears from us.

APP AND WEB ARE SEPARATE CLASSES OVER ONE SHARED HANDLER. Sharing the API class is what couples two clients on different release cycles; sharing a function does not.

```
