The learner's Power Automate flows, for the mobile app.

`GET app-api/v1/ai-labs/flows/`

The other half of the submit picker, beside the agents read (RECHECKED 2026-10-07: route names `app-ai-lab-agents-v1` / `web-ai-lab-agents-v1`; no `ai-lab-agents-v1` route exists).

IDENTICAL TO THE AGENTS READ EXCEPT THE ARTEFACT TYPE, and kept as a second endpoint rather than one filtered list because the labs service serves them as two - a merged list would have to invent a discriminator that neither side actually publishes.

AN UNPROVISIONED LEARNER IS A `200` with `is_provisioned: false` and an empty list, not a 404.

THE PLATFORM TOKEN NEVER LEAVES THIS PROCESS. `AI_LABS_API_TOKEN` identifies the PLATFORM, not the learner, so a frontend holding it could read as anybody. The client calls with its own JWT and the SSO handle is resolved server-side; the labs service only ever hears from us.

APP AND WEB ARE SEPARATE CLASSES OVER ONE SHARED HANDLER. Sharing the API class is what couples two clients on different release cycles; sharing a function does not.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07:
200 OK: `{status, is_provisioned, flows}`; `is_provisioned:
    false` and `flows: []` when labs answers 404.
400 Bad Request: `no_sso_handle` - today EVERY learner past the
    CAIRA gate, so nothing below it runs (see `_no_sso_handle`).
401 Unauthorized: no Bearer credentials.
403 Forbidden: `caira_access_required`.
429 / 502 / 503: labs rate-limited / failed / not permitted here.
```

**Surface:** WEB

**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One practical's state, for the web.

`GET web-api/v1/ai-labs/assignment-status/<uuid>/`

The caller's practical state, reconciling it when it is still open.

THIS READ DOUBLES AS THE MISSED-WEBHOOK RECONCILER, and that is why it exists in this shape: THE LABS SERVICE DOES NOT RETRY A FAILED WEBHOOK DELIVERY. A result we were down for is gone from their outbox and lives only behind their results read.

So whenever the stored row is still waiting, this read polls them once before answering and applies anything it finds through the same latch the webhook uses. The client polls this anyway to drive its spinner, so a missed webhook SELF-HEALS on the next tick with no cron or beat task chasing it. A grading window of one to three minutes is short enough that the learner is still watching.

A COMPLETED ROW IS ANSWERED FROM THE DATABASE WITH NO OUTBOUND CALL. Once latched there is nothing left to reconcile, and the latch would refuse a change anyway. `reconciled` on the response says which path ran.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the poll never runs today - the SSO handle is read as the non-existent `User.user_id`, so reconcile is always idle. DEFECT, not fixed here; see the shared handler.

THE PLATFORM TOKEN NEVER LEAVES THIS PROCESS. `AI_LABS_API_TOKEN` identifies the PLATFORM, not the learner, so a frontend holding it could read as anybody. The client calls with its own JWT and the SSO handle is resolved server-side; the labs service only ever hears from us.

APP AND WEB ARE SEPARATE CLASSES OVER ONE SHARED HANDLER. Sharing the API class is what couples two clients on different release cycles; sharing a function does not.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The practical state and a `reconciled` flag saying whether
    this read had to poll labs to settle it.
403 Forbidden: `caira_access_required`.
404 Not Found: The caller holds no live enrollment.
```

`POST api/v1/events/attendance-session/release/` - give the lease back.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `AllowAny` (with `JWTAuthentication`) and CSRF-exempt, so a header-less `navigator.sendBeacon` (`text/plain`) is ACCEPTED with 204 rather than refused 401 - BUT IT RELEASES NOTHING. The lease is keyed on the user, and with no Authorization header `request.user.pk` is None, so `post` returns 204 before `attendance_session.release` is called (measured: an unauthenticated `text/plain` release answers 204 with zero SQL, before any cache call). Tab close therefore waits out the 45-second `LEASE_TTL`. Only the authenticated JSON caller actually releases. A present-but-bad bearer token answers 401.

WHAT STOPS IT BEING AN EVICTION PRIMITIVE is `attendance_session.release`, which deletes the lease ONLY when the given `session_id` still holds it. The id is 122 bits bound to a user at claim, so knowing it ends that one lease - and a stale release from a tab closed ten minutes ago is a no-op rather than an eviction of the session the learner is watching now.

ALWAYS 204 for any request that authenticates or carries no token, including an unknown or already-released id, so the route cannot be used to probe which session ids exist.

**Methods on this view:** GET

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET registerV4/<attempt_id>/status/`

`GET api/v1/events/register-via-zoom-status/<uuid:attempt_id>/`.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: path corrected from `events/...-v1/`; the route name is `events-register-via-zoom-status-v1`.

The polling half of the 202 handshake. Scoped to `request.user`, so one user cannot read another's attempt - and a foreign id is a 404 rather than a 403, which avoids confirming that the id exists at all.

Returns both `status` (the full internal state, for Ops and support) and `registration_status` (the three-state client contract). Clients should switch on the latter; the former is diagnostic and its value set will grow.

---

> From `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 3. `GET api/v1/events/register-via-zoom-status/<uuid:attempt_id>/`

The polling half of the handshake. Authenticated. Shared web + app. Takes NO query parameters - any query
string at all is a 400.

Scoped to the calling user, so one user cannot read another's attempt. A foreign or unknown id is
`404 attempt_not_found` rather than 403, which avoids confirming the id exists.

### 3.1 `200 OK`

```json
{
  "attempt_id": "9c2f1b70-8e4d-4a11-93cc-0d5a6f2e8b31",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "registration_status": "REGISTERED",
  "zoom_attempts": 1,
  "last_status_code": 201,
  "error_message": null,
  "error_code": null,
  "mf_retry_count": 0,
  "join_url": "https://us06web.zoom.us/w/8412...",
  "registered_email": "learner@example.com",
  "booking_id": "b41e77a2-1cf9-4c02-9c6e-3a8d5e0f1b22",
  "completed_at": "2026-09-17T09:14:22.118Z"
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attempt_id` | UUID string | Echo of the path parameter. |
| `status` | string | The TEN-state internal status. Diagnostic, for Ops and support. Do not branch on it. |
| `registration_status` | string | The THREE-state client contract. Branch on this. |
| `zoom_attempts` | integer | How many times the Zoom leg has been tried. |
| `last_status_code` | integer or null | Last HTTP status seen from the external leg. |
| `error_message` | string or null | Human-readable reason. Safe to surface. |
| `error_code` | string or null | Machine-readable reason. |
| `mf_retry_count` | integer | Salesforce/MF forward retries. |
| `join_url` | string or null | The learner's own Zoom join URL. Populated once Zoom has issued it. |
| `registered_email` | string or null | The address this attempt actually sent to Zoom. On a FAILED attempt this is the only record of it, because the pipeline reads the profile live and the learner may have edited it since. This is the attendance-matching key. |
| `booking_id` | UUID string or null | Set once the `Booking` row exists. |
| `completed_at` | ISO-8601 string or null | Set when the attempt reached a terminal state. |

### 3.2 The three-state contract

`registration_status` is always one of:

| Value | Meaning | What the UI should do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | Still working, or waiting on the Zoom host to approve the registrant. | Keep the spinner. Keep polling. |
| `REGISTERED` | The user IS registered on Zoom and holds a join URL. | Show the join affordance. Stop polling. |
| `REGISTER` | The pipeline stopped before a usable registration existed. | Show the retry CTA. Stop polling. |

The internal `status` collapses onto it like this:

| Internal `status` | `registration_status` |
| --- | --- |
| `SUCCESS` | `REGISTERED` |
| `MF_FAILED` | `REGISTERED` |
| `MF_PERMANENTLY_FAILED` | `REGISTERED` |
| `MF_SKIPPED` | `REGISTERED` |
| `ZOOM_FAILED` | `REGISTER` |
| `BOOKING_FAILED` | `REGISTER` |
| `INTERRUPTED` | `REGISTER` |
| `PENDING` | `PENDING` |
| `ZOOM_RETRYING` | `PENDING` |
| `ZOOM_PENDING_APPROVAL` | `PENDING` |

Two of these are worth understanding rather than just mapping:

- THE FOUR `MF_*` STATES ARE `REGISTERED`, not failures the user can act on. The Salesforce forward is an audit
  hand-off downstream of the fact that Zoom accepted the registrant. Telling the user to register again would
  be wrong AND would spend another Zoom registrant slot.
- `ZOOM_PENDING_APPROVAL` IS TERMINAL BUT MAPS TO `PENDING`. The Zoom host has to approve the registrant before
  a join URL is issued, and there is no action the user can take. A retry CTA there would invite a duplicate
  registration that Zoom answers with the same 409. The reason for the wait travels in `error_message` - show
  it. Note that polling this one will never resolve on its own timescale; see 4.2.

An unrecognised internal status collapses to `PENDING`, which is the safe default: a spinner rather than an
invitation to register twice.

### 3.3 Self-healing poll

If the worker handling an attempt died mid-pipeline (deploy, restart, crash), the row would otherwise sit
non-terminal forever and this endpoint would answer `PENDING` indefinitely - a spinner with nothing behind it.
Polling is exactly where that becomes observable, so it is where it is resolved: a stale attempt is reaped on
read and comes back as `INTERRUPTED` -> `REGISTER`, with

```
error_code: "stuck"
error_message: "The registration worker stopped before finishing (deploy, restart or crash).
                No Zoom registration was completed - please try again."
```

No cron has to have run for the client to get an actionable answer. Treat `REGISTER` as a genuine retry
affordance in this case - no Zoom registration was completed.

### 3.4 Refusals

| HTTP | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Any query parameter at all was sent. |
| 404 | `attempt_not_found` | No such attempt for this user. |

---

## 4. Driving the pair

### 4.1 The loop

1. `POST register-via-zoom/`.
2. `200` -> already registered, done. `202` -> take `attempt_id` and `status_url`.
3. Poll `status_url` until `registration_status` leaves `PENDING`.
4. `REGISTERED` -> show join, using `join_url`. `REGISTER` -> show retry, using `error_message`.

A sensible cadence is roughly every 2 seconds for the first 15 seconds, then back off. The happy path usually
resolves in a second or two; the pathological path is around 8 seconds of backoff.

### 4.2 Bound the poll

`ZOOM_PENDING_APPROVAL` is terminal but reads as `PENDING`, so a loop with no ceiling will spin on it forever.
Cap the poll (30-45 seconds is comfortable), and on timeout fall back to reading `status` and `error_message`
from the last response rather than continuing. That is the one place the internal `status` is worth reading on
the client, and it is for display, not for branching.

### 4.3 Do not re-POST to check state

A re-POST is safe - it will answer `200 already_registered` or `202` with the existing attempt - but it takes
the lock and writes a log line for nothing. Poll the status route.

---

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `RegisterViaZoomViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `events-register-via-zoom-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST registerV4/`

`POST api/v1/events/register-via-zoom/` - register the caller for a webinar.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the path is `api/v1/events/register-via-zoom/` (route name `events-register-via-zoom-v1`); the old `events/...-v1/` spelling here was neither.

Answers `202 Accepted` with an `attempt_id` and runs the actual work - Zoom registrant, then `Booking` plus `BookingDetails`, then the Salesforce forward - as a background task. The client polls `RegisterViaZoomStatusViewV1` for the outcome.

WHY FIRE AND FORGET AND NOT A SYNCHRONOUS ANSWER. The Zoom leg alone is three attempts with 1s and 3s backoff, and the Salesforce leg is another three with 1s and 3s - so a worst case that still ENDS IN SUCCESS takes around 8 seconds of waiting plus six round trips. Holding a request open for that long is what the 202 exists to avoid, and it is why the attempt row carries full state rather than the response.

IDEMPOTENCY, in two layers, because the expensive mistake here is a duplicate Zoom registrant:

- A live `Booking` for this `(user, webinar)` means the user already succeeded. Answered `200` with `already_registered` - not an error, and no pipeline is spawned.
- An in-flight attempt (`PENDING` or `ZOOM_RETRYING`) means a double-tap. Answered `202` with THAT attempt's id, so the client polls the one that is already running instead of starting a second.

Body template generated from `RegisterViaZoomRequestV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

---

> From `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 2. `POST api/v1/events/register-via-zoom/`

Registers the authenticated caller for a webinar. Authenticated. Shared web + app.

This is a `202` handshake, not a synchronous registration. The endpoint answers immediately with an
`attempt_id`; the actual work - Zoom registrant, then `Booking` plus `BookingDetails`, then the Salesforce
forward - runs in the background. Poll the status route (section 3) for the outcome.

The reason is latency: the Zoom leg is three attempts with 1s and 3s backoff and the Salesforce leg is another
three, so a worst case that still ENDS IN SUCCESS is around six round trips and roughly 8 seconds. That is not
a request to hold open.

### 2.1 Request body

```json
{
  "webinar_id": "3f1a9c7e-5b42-4d9a-8f10-2c6be7d41a55"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webinar_id` | UUID | yes | The `Events.Webinar` PRIMARY KEY. Not the MF/SF integer id. |

ONE FIELD, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE BODY. Nothing else is accepted - see 1.3.

THE WEBINAR IS ADDRESSED BY UUID, which is a change from legacy. Legacy took the producing service's integer
and resolved it as `(webinar_id, webinar_type)` - a compound lookup, because that integer is unique only in
combination with the type. An integer-only lookup here would either need the type threaded through the client
contract or would silently resolve to whichever row Postgres returned first. Whatever feed hands you a webinar
should expose its `id`; `webinar-main-page` (section 6) does.

ONE INPUT SURFACE. Legacy read each parameter from the query string first and fell back to the JSON body. Here
the body is canonical - a query parameter on this route is a 400.

### 2.2 `202 Accepted` - the normal answer

```json
{
  "status": "accepted",
  "registration_status": "PENDING",
  "message": "Registration started. Pull to refresh.",
  "attempt_id": "9c2f1b70-8e4d-4a11-93cc-0d5a6f2e8b31",
  "status_url": "/api/v1/events/register-via-zoom-status/9c2f1b70-8e4d-4a11-93cc-0d5a6f2e8b31/"
}
```

`status_url` is built server-side off the URLconf, so it cannot drift from the real route. Prefer following it
over assembling the path yourself.

### 2.3 `200 OK` - already registered

Not an error. The caller already holds a live booking for this webinar, and NO pipeline is spawned.

```json
{
  "status": "already_registered",
  "code": "already_registered",
  "message": "You are already registered for this webinar.",
  "booking_id": "b41e77a2-1cf9-4c02-9c6e-3a8d5e0f1b22"
}
```

### 2.4 Idempotency, in two layers

The expensive mistake here is a duplicate Zoom registrant, so a double-tap is absorbed rather than refused:

1. A LIVE BOOKING -> `200 already_registered` (section 2.3).
2. AN IN-FLIGHT ATTEMPT (`PENDING` or `ZOOM_RETRYING`) -> `202` carrying THAT attempt's id, with
   `message: "Registration already in progress."` Poll the one already running; do not start a second.

A third guard sits under both: a short per-`(user, webinar)` lock. If two taps land inside the same few
milliseconds, the loser gets `409 registration_in_progress` with `retry_after_seconds`. Retry once after that
and you will get the in-flight `202`.

### 2.5 Every refusal

| HTTP | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Body failed validation, or carried an undeclared key. Carries `errors[]`. |
| 400 | `missing_email` | The user's profile has no email. Zoom requires one. |
| 400 | `invalid_email` | Profile email is malformed. |
| 400 | `missing_first_name` | Profile has no first name. |
| 400 | `invalid_first_name` | First name contains non-ASCII - in practice an emoji pasted into a profile. Zoom rejects it with a terminal 400. |
| 404 | `webinar_not_found` | No such webinar row. |
| 409 | `unsupported_webinar_type` | The row is not a `webinar` or an `offline` event. Orientations and premiers have their own flows. |
| 409 | `webinar_inactive` | Soft-deleted or temporarily deactivated. 409 AND NOT 404 DELIBERATELY - the row exists and your copy of it is not wrong, so do not discard the webinar; it may come back. |
| 409 | `webinar_cancelled` | The session was cancelled. A cancelled webinar stays `active=True`, so this is a separate flag rather than a variant of the one above. |
| 409 | `webinar_start_time_missing` | The webinar has no scheduled start time yet. An ops data problem, not a client error - surface `detail` and let the user retry later. |
| 409 | `registration_in_progress` | Lock contention. Carries `retry_after_seconds` (currently 15). Retry once. |

The four profile refusals are worth handling specifically: each `detail` is already written as user-facing copy
naming what to fix in the profile, and none is retryable without that fix. They are checked BEFORE any Zoom
call, so the user learns synchronously instead of polling to a terminal failure.

Order of evaluation, which is the order you will hit them: body validation -> webinar resolution (404 / the
four 409s) -> profile preflight (the four 400s) -> idempotency (200 / 202) -> lock contention (409).

### 2.6 `offline` webinars take the identical path

An in-person event still goes through the full Zoom -> Booking -> Salesforce write path, and the learner still
gets a Zoom registrant record and a join URL - they simply do not use it. No client branch is needed.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppAllBookingsViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-all-bookings-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET v2/allbookings`

`GET app-api/v1/events/all-bookings/` - every booking the caller holds.

THE MERGED-TREE SUCCESSOR TO LEGACY `GET /v2/allbookings`. Renamed from `WebinarBookingsViewV1` on 2026-08-21: the webinar-only scope was a porting boundary, not the intended contract, and a name that encodes a temporary boundary outlives it.

THE WEB FEED IS A SEPARATE ENDPOINT AND SHARES NO CODE WITH THIS ONE (maintainer, 2026-09-28). `WebAllBookingsViewV1` below is written out in full rather than inheriting, and the two are free to drift from the first day. This was briefly refactored into a shared base class; that was the wrong call. A base class is a promise that the two stay alike, and they already do not - the web feed carries NO 1:1 bookings - so the shared part would have been a filter switch threaded through every method, which is coupling wearing a helper's clothes.

`Booking` is one table serving two things under a database-level XOR, and this endpoint returns both sides:

- WEBINAR bookings - returned as the flat card described below.
- 1:1 bookings - carrying the counsellor-side detail (SPOC name and phone, the Google Meet link, the calendar id that a cancellation keys on).

Each row lands in a `webinar` or `one_on_one` bucket, and the bucket is the only place the kind is stated. Split into `upcoming` and `past` about a cutoff of `now` minus the 30-minute grace period, so a session in progress still reads as upcoming.

THE 2026-10-07 RESHAPE (maintainer): EVERY WEBINAR ROW IS NOW THE ATTENDANCE CARD, byte for byte. `app-api/v1/events/webinar-attendance/` and this feed return the SAME object for the same webinar - built by the same `_flat_webinar_cards`, from the same detail projection, with the same nineteen top-level keys and the same `bookings_additonal_data` block - differing only in the `surface` passed, which selects one label and one CTA branch. The app renders one card on two screens and asked for one shape; building it twice is how the two screens come to describe one webinar two ways.

THREE THINGS FOLLOW FROM THAT AND ARE WORTH STATING OUTRIGHT:

- THE WEBINAR ROW'S OLD KEYS ARE GONE. `id`, `webinar_name`, `feedback_details`, `attendance_details` and the rest are listed in `_shape_one_on_one_row`, with the card key each became.
- THIS FEED CARRIES THE CPE VERDICT NOW. The docstring here used to record "the per-webinar badge / feedback overlay" as unbuilt work; it is built, and it is the same gate the attendance feed reads.
- UPCOMING ROWS CARRY A NULLED VERDICT, not a false one. They take the `_GROUP_UPCOMING` treatment - see `_eligibility_block` - because nothing can be claimed about a session that has not happened, and their CTA comes from the join state instead (`upcoming_card_ctas`).

NO VISIBILITY GATE ON THE WEBINAR SIDE, UNLIKE ATTENDANCE. That feed filters its ids through `_main_page_visible_webinars` so a card never leads to a 404 on a page the user could not have reached anyway. A BOOKING IS DIFFERENT: the caller holds a seat, and a webinar flipped inactive or marked cancelled must still appear in their own list rather than vanishing from it with no explanation. The difference is stated at the two call sites rather than as a flag inside the shared builder.

`?window=` selects one side or both. `status=True` is a hard filter and not an option: this project soft-deletes, so a cancelled booking is a row with `status=False` and must never reach a user-facing feed.

ONE QUERY PER WINDOW, NOT ONE PER KIND. Both kinds live in the same table, so a single projection returns them together and they are split in Python on whether the webinar join produced a row. Splitting in SQL instead would double the query count to four for `window=all` and buy nothing.

AND ONE CARD BUILD FOR BOTH WINDOWS. `window=all` projects the webinars of both sides together and runs the overlays once over the union, because every one of those reads is keyed by webinar id and nothing in them cares which side of the cutoff a booking fell on. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: calling the builder per window would double a fixed batch of up to about nineteen queries (counted off the code: three injects, `standing_bulk` 8, badge links 2, credential loop 6), not six.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE TWO WINDOW QUERIES ARE GATHERED BUT DO NOT OVERLAP. Django's async ORM runs each query through `sync_to_async(thread_sensitive=True)`, so within one request they execute one at a time on one thread (measured: two gathered thread-sensitive 0.5s calls take 1.0s). `return_exceptions=True` degrades one failing side to an empty result and records it on the span rather than failing the whole response: half a bookings list beats none.

WHAT LEGACY RETURNED THAT THIS DOES NOT, and why:

- The `office` bucket. Out of scope, and already dead in legacy - every office-visit view there sits behind `# Office Visit disabled`. `office` remains a legal STORED value (see `One_On_One_Type`), so any historical row still resolves and appears here; it simply cannot be created.
- The `OneOnOneChecklist` payload. Legacy pre-fetched checklist rows and passed them through serializer context for the office and career cards. No booking card read them, and a checklist is a property of the TYPE rather than of one person's booking - so it belongs on its own endpoint, not duplicated into every row of this one.

A NOTE ON THE 1:1 SIDE. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the career-counselling write path IS ported (`app-api/v1/events/booking/career-counselling/`, via `acreate_career_booking`), so the `one_on_one` list fills from that route; it is no longer empty by construction.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `window` - Optional. One of: `all`, `upcoming`, `past`. Default `all`. One of all / upcoming / past.

---

> From `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 5. `GET app-api/v1/events/all-bookings/`

Every booking the calling user holds. Authenticated. App only; the web twin is not built.

**MOVED FROM `web-api/v1/events/all-bookings/` ON 2026-09-17.** Same view, same response, same route name
(`events-all-bookings-v1`) - only the prefix changed. There is no redirect.

`Booking` is one table serving two things under a database-level XOR: a row either points at a webinar or
carries a 1:1 `booking_type`, never both and never neither. This endpoint returns BOTH sides, each row tagged
with its `kind`.

### 5.1 Query parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `window` | string | `all` | `all`, `upcoming`, `past` |

There is deliberately NO `kind` filter: both kinds come from one table in one query, so filtering server-side
would save no work, and you already receive them pre-bucketed.

Any other parameter is a 400.

### 5.2 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Bookings retrieved successfully.",
  "data": {
    "upcoming": { "webinar": [], "one_on_one": [] },
    "past": { "webinar": [], "one_on_one": [] }
  }
}
```

`data.upcoming` is present only when `window` is `all` or `upcoming`; `data.past` only when `window` is `all`
or `past`. Both inner keys are always present when their window is, empty rather than omitted.

THE SPLIT POINT IS NOW MINUS 30 MINUTES, not now. A session that is running right now still reads as
`upcoming` while the user is in it.

A booking with no start time is filed under `upcoming` and sorts to the top. That is not a bug: a booking we
cannot date is not yet KNOWN to be past, and it needs attention.

Cancelled bookings never appear on either side.

### 5.3 One row

```json
{
  "kind": "webinar",
  "booking": {
    "id": "b41e77a2-1cf9-4c02-9c6e-3a8d5e0f1b22",
    "booking_type": null,
    "booking_type_label": null,
    "active_till": "2026-09-20T13:30:00Z",
    "status": true,
    "mf_log": true,
    "created_at": "2026-09-17T09:14:20.004Z",
    "attended_status": "1",
    "poll_questions_answered": 3,
    "total_poll_questions_available": 4,
    "total_webinar_duration_seconds": 3600,
    "attended_webinar_duration_seconds": 3240,
    "force_override_by_leadership_team": false
  },
  "details": {
    "id": "0f2b...",
    "book_id": "MF-99812",
    "datetime": "2026-09-20T13:00:00Z",
    "booking_url": "https://us06web.zoom.us/w/8412...",
    "registered_email": "learner@example.com",
    "spoc_name": null,
    "spoc_phone": null,
    "gmeet_link": null,
    "calendar_id": null
  },
  "webinar": { }
}
```

`booking` object:

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string | |
| `booking_type` | string or null | `null` on a webinar booking. One of `career` / `office` / `resume` / `alumni` on a 1:1. |
| `booking_type_label` | string or null | The human label for the same value - `Career Counselling`, `Office Visit`, `Resume Review`, `Alumni Connect`. Carried so you never map a code to a label yourself; re-deriving it client-side is how two surfaces end up wording one workflow differently. |
| `active_till` | ISO-8601 or null | The booking's effective time. For a webinar this is its start time. This is the ONLY column the upcoming/past split reads. |
| `status` | boolean | Always `true` in this feed - cancelled bookings are filtered out. |
| `mf_log` | boolean or null | The registration was forwarded to MF / Salesforce. Pipeline bookkeeping. |
| `created_at` | ISO-8601 | |
| `attended_status` | string | One-character MF code. See 5.4. |
| `poll_questions_answered` | integer | Written by the poll ingest, so `0` on a fresh booking. |
| `total_poll_questions_available` | integer | |
| `total_webinar_duration_seconds` | integer | **SECONDS.** Named `total_webinar_duration`
  until 2026-09-27; it was always seconds, so the RENAME carries no value change. |
| `attended_webinar_duration_seconds` | integer | **SECONDS.** Named
  `attended_webinar_duration` until 2026-09-27; same rename, same values. This is the FACT that
  `WebinarDetails.required_attendance_seconds` is compared against. |
| `force_override_by_leadership_team` | boolean or null | Eligibility override. `null` when no details row exists, which reads as "no override". |

`details` object:

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string or null | Nullable in practice: a booking written before the pipeline became atomic can lack its companion row. |
| `book_id` | string or null | Booking id from the external source. |
| `datetime` | ISO-8601 or null | |
| `booking_url` | string or null | THE PER-USER ZOOM JOIN URL for a webinar booking - this is the field you want. `null` on a 1:1. See 8.3 on the key name. |
| `registered_email` | string or null | The address Zoom holds the registrant under. Surfaced because it is the attendance-matching key: when it disagrees with the user's current email, that IS the explanation for a missing attendance record. |
| `spoc_name` | string or null | 1:1 only. |
| `spoc_phone` | string or null | 1:1 only. |
| `gmeet_link` | string or null | 1:1 only. |
| `calendar_id` | string or null | 1:1 only. Google Calendar event id; a cancellation keys on it. |

`webinar` object - PRESENT ONLY WHEN `kind == "webinar"`. The key is omitted rather than null on a 1:1, so an
absent webinar cannot be mistaken for a broken one.

| Key | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string |
| `webinar_id_as_per_mf_sf` | integer or null |
| `webinar_name` | string |
| `webinar_type` | string |
| `webinar_description` | string |
| `webinar_start_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null |
| `webinar_end_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null |
| `webinar_duration_seconds` | integer or null, SECONDS |
| `zoom_id` | string or null |
| `caira_check` | boolean |
| `non_caira_check` | boolean |
| `active` | boolean |
| `cancellation_status` | boolean |
| `horizontal_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset |
| `vertical_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset |
| `square_image` | URL string, `""` when unset |

Image keys resolve to full public URLs, or to an empty string. They are never null and never a bare storage
key.

### 5.4 `attended_status` codes

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"1"` | Attended |
| `"2"` | Not attended |
| `"3"` | Registered (MF never advanced the row past registration) |
| `"4"` | Cancelled |
| `""` | MF has not reported on this booking yet |

Only `"1"` grants CPE / badge eligibility.

---

### 9.5 No badge / feedback overlay on `all-bookings` yet

The legacy `v2/allbookings` feed decorated every webinar card with a CPE / badge / feedback overlay. The CPE
half has moved - a webinar's credit is now the sum of its active fields of study, which `webinar-main-page`
already returns as `total_cpe_credits`. The BADGE and FEEDBACK overlay is outstanding work on `all-bookings`. It is
unbuilt, not blocked.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppCancelOneOnOneBookingViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-cancel-one-on-one-booking-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`POST app-api/v1/events/booking/cancel/` - cancel a 1:1 booking.

Resolves the caller's booking, cancels the Google Meet, then soft-cancels the row. Ported from legacy MilesOne `POST events/booking/cancel-visit/v2`.

TWO SECURITY DEFECTS IN THE LEGACY VERSION ARE FIXED HERE, and both were needed together. Legacy's `CancelVisitView` declared no `permission_classes`, and that project set no `DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES` - so DRF's own default `AllowAny` applied and the endpoint was reachable with no authentication at all. Its booking lookup was also UNSCOPED, matching on the id alone. Together, an anonymous caller who could guess an id could cancel any learner's booking. The permission class is declared below; the scope lives in `aresolve_booking_for_cancel`, which is the half that survives someone adding a second caller later.

AN UNKNOWN ID IS A 404, NOT A SCHEDULER CALL. Legacy fell back to cancelling the RAW id as a calendar event when no local booking matched - so an id that belonged to nobody here was still sent upstream. That turns a lookup miss into an outbound write, and it is how an unscoped endpoint reaches other people's meetings. Resolving locally first, and refusing when nothing matches, is the whole guard.

THE ORDER IS CANCEL-THEN-DEACTIVATE. If the scheduler refuses, the local row stays live and the learner still holds a real meeting - which is true. The reverse order would show a cancelled booking against a calendar invitation that is still in their diary.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppCareerCounsellingBookingViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-career-counselling-booking-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`POST app-api/v1/events/booking/career-counselling/` - book a session.

Schedules a 45-minute online Google Meet through Miles360, then writes the `Booking` and `BookingDetails` keyed on the calendar id it returns.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `POST events/booking/career-counsellor/v2`.

THE ORDER IS SCHEDULE-THEN-PERSIST, AND IT CANNOT BE THE OTHER WAY AROUND. The calendar id is minted by the far side, and it is the booking's only external handle - the column that a cancellation keys on and that carries the partial unique constraint. A local row written first would have nothing to put there, and a scheduler failure after it would leave a booking the learner can see and nobody can cancel.

THE FAILURE WINDOW THAT REMAINS is the reverse: the meeting is scheduled and the local write then fails. That leaves a calendar invitation with no booking row - visible to the learner in their calendar, absent from the feed. It is the smaller of the two and it is stated rather than hidden: closing it needs a compensating cancel on the write's failure path, which is itself a network call that can fail. The atomic local write means the row is whole or absent, never half.

`visit_date` IS THE ONLY INPUT. Duration, meeting type and booking type are server-decided - see `CareerCounsellingBookingRequestV1`.

**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppCareerCounsellingPostBookingViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-career-counselling-post-booking-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET app-api/v1/events/career-counselling/post-booking/` - the confirmation.

What a learner sees AFTER booking: their session, the editorial blocks, and the preparation checklist with their own ticks on it.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `GET v2/career_counselling/post_booking`.

NO BOOKING IS A 404, NOT A 500. Legacy dereferenced its booking-details row without checking it existed - `_format_visit_datetime(booking_details_obj .datetime)` on `None` raises `AttributeError`, which its handler caught and returned as a 500 with the exception text as the message. A learner who had not booked yet got "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'datetime'" on a 500. That is a real state, and it has a status code.

THE PLACEHOLDER COUNSELLOR IS NOT PORTED. Legacy, finding no counsellor for the booking, substituted a named individual from its table and rewrote that person's biography around whatever `spoc_name` the booking carried - and its own comment records the result when the name was null: "None is a seasoned counselor...". Google Meet bookings carry no SPOC at all, so that was the normal path, not the edge. Here `counsellor` is `null` when the booking has no SPOC, which is what is true.

THE CHECKLIST IS A TABLE, not the three hard-coded bullets legacy shipped beside a checklist model it was already reading elsewhere.

`GET app-api/v1/events/career-counselling/pre-booking/` - the sell page.

The blocks a learner sees BEFORE booking: the banner and its statistics, the call to action, and what to expect from the session.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `GET v2/career_counselling/pre_booking`.

EVERY BLOCK IS A CMS ROW NOW, WHERE LEGACY HAD LITERALS. The headings, the four "what to expect" bullets, the three statistics and the banner's lookup title were all hard-coded in the view, so correcting a number was a deploy. See `EventsPage.utils.page_slugs` for the section and the block keys.

THE COUNSELLOR BLOCK IS GONE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING THE PORT DROPS. Legacy's fourth block listed six people from a `CareerCounsellors` table. That model was REMOVED from this repository on 2026-09-15 (maintainer): zero rows, no inbound foreign key, and no reader outside its own admin registration. Rebuilding it to fill a block would be re-adding a table the maintainer deleted as dead. If the block is wanted, it is CMS assets under this same section - one per counsellor - and needs no model at all.

**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppEventsPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET v11/events/`

`GET app-api/v1/events/page/` - the app's events screen in one call.

FOUR BLOCKS, FIXED KEYS::

```
top_section_webinars       every upcoming webinar, CAIRA and not
caira_webinars_per_levels  CAIRA webinars grouped by level
global_certification       every non-CAIRA webinar, no priority gate
one_on_one_visits          the 1:1 booking catalogue
```

THE BLOCKS ARE FIXED, UNLIKE THE HOME PAGE'S SECTIONS. That page reads its order and headings from `CMS.Page` because its sections are a layout an operator arranges. These four are not a layout - they are four different QUESTIONS about webinars, and their keys are the contract. What DID come from CMS is the 1:1 catalogue, which legacy hard-codes in the view.

THE SAME WEBINAR APPEARS IN MORE THAN ONE BLOCK, on purpose. A CAIRA webinar is in the top section AND in its level's section; a non-CAIRA one is in the top section AND in global certification. The blocks answer different questions, so de-duplicating them would mean the client could not render any one of them on its own.

ARTWORK DIFFERS PER BLOCK, from three different columns, because the three render at three aspect ratios. The KEY is always `webinar_banner`; which column fills it is the block's decision.

CACHING. Per learner, 30 seconds, keyed on the shared CMS content version - so editing the 1:1 catalogue invalidates every cached page with one `INCR`. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: there is no separate global cache of webinar rows - the WHOLE payload is cached under `APP_EVENTS_PAGE_CACHE_PREFIX` + `v<version>:<user.pk>` + `test_viewer_cache_suffix(user)`, so the key is per learner already. Nothing but the TTL expires it on a registration or a webinar edit: the CMS version bump fires only on `CMS.Page` / `CMS.Asset` saves and deletes.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE QUERY STRING IS NOT VALIDATED. `get` reads no parameter and validates none, so an undeclared parameter is ignored with a 200 instead of answering 400, against the strict-input rule. DEFECT, not fixed here.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppWebinarAttendanceViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-webinar-attendance-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET app-api/v1/events/webinar-attendance/?limit=3`

The learner's PAST BOOKED webinars, split three ways - the merged-tree successor to legacy `GET /webinar/attendance`:

- `in_progress`  - booked and over, but the attendance service has not reported yet. Every verdict on these cards is `null`.
- `attended`     - attended, or overridden to attended by leadership. Each card carries the CPE verdict, the copy for it, and the badge links.
- `not_attended` - booked, over, and reported as a no-show.

Each group is `{count, items}`: `items` is the newest `?limit=` of them (default 3, ceiling 50) and `count` is the whole group, which legacy did not send and a "see all" affordance needs. A CAPPED PREVIEW, NOT A PAGINATED LIST - legacy's contract, and `?limit=` is the parameter the app already sends.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: EACH ITEM IS THE 19-KEY FLAT CARD from `attendance_card.flatten` (via `_flat_webinar_cards`), the same object `app-api/v1/events/all-bookings/` returns - NOT the details-page object with nested `eligibility` / `feedback` / `attendance` / `badge` blocks. Those blocks are computed and then flattened into `eligibility_status`, `status_message`, `attendance_label`, `polls_label`, `notice_tone`, `badge_included`, `primary_cta` / `secondary_cta` (badge and certificate URLs ride on the CTAs) and `bookings_additonal_data.badge_details`.

PAST MEANS NO LONGER UPCOMING by `webinar_is_upcoming`, legacy's own boundary, as on the events page. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT the instant the booking feeds use - they split on `active_till` (the webinar's end) plus 30 minutes, so a booking can sit in all-bookings `upcoming` and in this feed at once. Only webinars the app details page would open are listed - `_main_page_visible_webinars` - so a card never leads to a 404.

NOTHING IS CACHED. Every key here is about this learner.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `limit` - Optional. Default `3`. Items per group, 1 or more; values above 50 are answered with 50.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppWebinarDetailsPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-events-webinar-details-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET v3/eventsAsync/<types>/<int:webinar_id>/`

`GET app-api/v1/events/webinar-details-page/?webinar_id=<uuid>`

ONE webinar, in full, for the APP. The twin of `WebWebinarDetailsPageViewV1`, which serves the same page to the web.

A SEPARATE CLASS, AND NOT A SECOND ROUTE ONTO THE WEB ONE (maintainer, 2026-09-21). The first version of this endpoint pointed `app-api/v1/events/webinar-details-page/` at `WebWebinarDetailsPageViewV1` on the reasoning that the payloads were identical and a subclass overriding nothing is dead weight. That reasoning was wrong about what the prefixes are FOR: web and app are kept apart in this backend BECAUSE THEY ARE EXPECTED TO DIVERGE, and a single class shared between them turns the first divergence into a refactor - split the class, move the route, re-test both - at the moment someone is trying to ship one small difference. Two classes make that an edit to one file.

WHAT IS SHARED IS THE FUNCTIONS, WHICH IS THE POINT. `_details_page_params`, `_main_page_visible_webinars`, `_shape_webinar_details`, `_inject_webinar_extras`, `_inject_registration_state`, `_inject_webinar_details` and `_strip_private_keys` are module-level and called by both classes, so the two surfaces cannot drift by accident - only on purpose, by one of them calling something different. Sharing the shaping and sharing the ENDPOINT are different things, and only the first one is safe.

IDENTICAL TO THE WEB SURFACE TODAY, deliberately and visibly. Every behaviour below is the web view's: the same visibility filter, the same derived surface, the same 404 for a webinar this surface does not list, the same envelope. When the app needs something the web does not - a trimmed payload, a different image size, its own cache - it changes HERE and the web view is not touched.

**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppOldWebinarRecordingsViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `app-old-webinar-recordings-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET caira/old_webinar_recordings/v2/`

`GET app-api/v1/events/webinar-recordings/` - past webinars to replay.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRAOldWebinarRecordingsAsyncView` (`caira/views.py`) on 2026-09-29.

IT LIVES IN `BadgeCertificateCPE` RATHER THAN `EventsPage`, WHICH THE ROUTE DOES NOT SUGGEST. `Events.OldWebinarRecordings` is NOT this app's table. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the import rule in `EventsPage/views.py` (no module-scope `BadgeCertificateCPE.models`) does not force it here - this view reads only `Events.OldWebinarRecordings` and `Events.Webinar`, no model of this app. The route keeps the `events/` segment because that is the surface a learner is on; the app label is not the URL.

ONE QUERY, NOT ONE PER RECORDING. Legacy shaped each row in Python after a single `.values()` read and this does the same; the count does not move with the number of recordings on the shelf.

CACHED GLOBALLY AND PARTITIONED BY THE TEST-VIEWER FLAG. The shelf is the same for every learner, so a per-user key would be a cache miss per learner for content nobody personalises. The suffix is what stops the first caller deciding what everybody sees: an internal tester warming the key would otherwise publish test webinars to the whole cohort for the full TTL.

`.values()` BECAUSE THIS IS AN ASYNC VIEW - a model instance would raise `SynchronousOnlyOperation` the moment the shaper touched `webinar`.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebAllBookingsViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `web-events-all-bookings-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET web-api/v1/events/all-bookings/` - the caller's WEBINAR bookings.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `GET /v2/web/allbookings`.

WEBINARS ONLY. NO 1:1 BOOKINGS (maintainer, 2026-09-28). The web surface does not book career counselling and has no screen to render one, so the query filters `webinar__isnull=False` rather than returning an empty `one_on_one` bucket the client would have to ignore. That is enforced in SQL, not by shaping the response afterwards: a bucket that is always empty is a key somebody eventually writes code against.

THE RESPONSE HAS NO BUCKETS, because there is one kind. The app feed splits `upcoming` / `past` into `{webinar, one_on_one}`; here each window is a flat list. A client that cannot receive a 1:1 booking should not carry a branch for one. Neither surface carries a per-row `kind` tag any more - the app's was dropped 2026-10-06, so this is no longer a difference between the two.

THIS IS A SEPARATE ENDPOINT, NOT A VARIANT OF THE APP ONE. It shares no code with `AppAllBookingsViewV1` - not the column list, not the row shaper, not the fetch. Both read the same table, which is where the similarity is allowed to end; either can change without the other being re-reviewed.

`status=True` IS A HARD FILTER, as on the app feed. This project soft-deletes, so a cancelled booking is a row with `status=False` and must never reach a user-facing feed.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE 30-MINUTE GRACE SPLIT IS THE APP BOOKINGS FEED'S RULE, NOT THE EVENTS PAGE'S. Both booking feeds compare `active_till` (the webinar's END on rows written since 2026-09-15) against `now - 30 min`; the events page and attendance use `webinar_is_upcoming` (start plus `min(duration, 30 min)`), so a running webinar can read upcoming here and past there. A NULL `active_till` counts as upcoming - `Webinar.webinar_start_date_time` is nullable, and a plain `__gt` / `__lt` split drops a NULL from BOTH sides, so the learner would hold a real registration on a booking that appears nowhere.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1.
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100.
- `window` - Optional. One of: `all`, `upcoming`, `past`. Default `all`. One of all / upcoming / past.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebHighlightWebinarViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `web-events-highlight-webinars-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/events/highlight-webinars/`

The editorial webinar rail the web Masterclass home page renders, PRE-LOGIN ONLY.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ENDPOINT AND NOT A SECTION OF THE HOME PAGE. The home page is a Masterclass surface - tracks, courses, coming-soon - and this is a webinar read with entirely different visibility rules. Folding it in would make the Masterclass page's cache lifetime hostage to a webinar's start time, and the client renders the two rails independently anyway (maintainer, 2026-09-29).

WHY IT LIVES IN `EventsPage/views.py` RATHER THAN `MasterclassWeb`. It reuses `_main_page_visible_webinars`, which is where the five-bucket landing feed states its visibility rules ONCE. A copy of those rules in another app is the drift this codebase has already paid for twice - see the module docstring of `MilesPlatform/nasba_rules.py` on why a second implementation of a rule is a rule that will disagree with itself.

PRE-LOGIN ONLY, AND THAT IS ENFORCED BY HAVING NO PARAMETER. There is no `login_type` to pass. A signed-in visitor calling this gets the same `pre_login` rail, because the post-login highlight rail is `PinnedCourseLink` on the home page and these are different products. `HighlightWebinarQueryV1` still rejects a caller that sends anything, so a client aiming at the wrong endpoint learns that instead of receiving a plausible 200.

UPCOMING ONLY, narrowing `WebinarPriority`'s own rule deliberately. That model enforces "upcoming" at CREATE time, so a row goes stale by itself once its webinar ends; a landing rail pinning last month's session is worse than an empty one, so staleness is filtered here rather than waiting on a sweep.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1.
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebWebinarDetailsPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `web-events-webinar-details-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-details-page/?webinar_id=<uuid>`

ONE webinar, in full - the page behind a card on `webinar-main-page`.

IT IS THE SAME OBJECT THE FEED EMITS, PLUS FOUR KEYS. `description`, `trailer_url`, `trailer_thumbnail_url` and `product`. Every other key is shaped by the card's own function, so a client can render this page from the card type it already has and read the extras when present. A detail endpoint that re-derived the shared keys is the one that eventually formats a date differently from the feed that linked to it.

THE SURFACE IS DERIVED FROM THE REQUEST, NOT ASKED FOR (maintainer, 2026-09-18). There is no `login_type` parameter:

- an ANONYMOUS request is served the `pre_login` surface, with no `registration` block - there is no caller to report registration for;
- an AUTHENTICATED request is served `post_login`, with `registration`.

WHY DERIVED RATHER THAN DECLARED, which is the difference from `webinar-main-page`. That endpoint takes the parameter because a signed-in visitor may legitimately want to preview the signed-out landing page, so the surface is a genuine choice. A detail page has no such case: the bearer token already says which surface applies, and a parameter that could contradict it would be a second source of truth for one fact. Asking for `post_login` without a token would then have to be an error, which is a 401 the client can avoid entirely by not being asked the question.

THIS REPLACES AN `IsAuthenticated` VERSION THAT SHIPPED THE DAY BEFORE, and the reversal is worth recording because it retired two real defects rather than merely changing taste:

- The anonymous feed rendered cards that could not be opened - every click a login wall, with the 403 reaching clients as an error rather than a prompt. An anonymous caller now opens the page.
- With no `login_type` to pass, the visibility filter was PINNED to `post_login`, so a webinar an operator tagged pre-login ONLY was listed by the anonymous feed and then 404d for everybody, signed in or not, with nothing warning the operator. The filter now follows the caller, so that row opens for the surface that lists it. This was gap 9.7 in `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md`; it is closed, not moved.

A BAD TOKEN IS STILL REJECTED, NOT DOWNGRADED. `JWTAuthentication` returns None when there is no `Authorization` header, so an anonymous request is anonymous - but it RAISES for a header that is present and invalid. A client with an expired token therefore gets an error rather than being silently served the signed-out page, which is the correct answer: it has a problem it needs to see. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: that error is 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`, because `MilesPlatform.authentication.JWTAuthentication` implements `authenticate_header()`.

VISIBILITY IS THE FEED'S, NOT A LOOSER ONE, and this is the part worth getting right. The lookup runs through `_main_page_visible_webinars`, so a webinar that the feed would not list cannot be opened by guessing its id: soft-deleted rows, cancelled rows, the wrong login state and test webinars are all filtered before the id is matched. An endpoint that fetched by primary key and checked nothing would be a working way to read exactly the rows the feed exists to hide.

A HIDDEN WEBINAR ANSWERS 404, NOT 403. The two cases - no such id, and an id the caller may not see - are deliberately indistinguishable. Separating them would turn this endpoint into an oracle for which ids exist, and "this webinar exists but is not for you" is not a distinction a page can act on. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the authentication rejection above is a 401, not a 403 - DRF refusing the request before the view runs.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `registration` IS PRESENT ONLY ON AN AUTHENTICATED REQUEST. Since the 2026-09-18 switch to `AllowAny` there IS a second branch - an anonymous caller gets no `registration` key (nor `feedback` / `attendance`), which `login_type` in the response announces.

THE THREE PAST BUCKETS HAVE NO ANALOGUE HERE. `webinar-main-page` sorts a user's history into completed / absent / missed; a detail page is asked about one webinar, and the caller's relationship to it is already carried by `registration`. `eligible` is deliberately NOT emitted: it is a property of a BOOKING, the feed attaches it only on `completed_webinar`, and computing it here would mean a second definition of eligibility - the thing that view's docstring refuses to do for the same reason.

WHAT IT INHERITS FROM THE FEED'S KNOWN LIMITS. No enrolment filtering - `show_webinar_as_per_enrollment` is not applied here either, so a webinar outside the caller's enrolment opens rather than 404ing. No cache. Both are the feed's gaps and are fixed in the same place when they are fixed.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `webinar_id` - Required. Events.Webinar primary key (UUID), not the ingest integer.

---

> From `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 7. `GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-details-page/`

One webinar, in full - the page behind a card on `webinar-main-page`. **The surface follows your request**:
authenticated gets post-login, anonymous gets pre-login. There is no `login_type` parameter.

### 7.1 Query parameters

| Param | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webinar_id` | uuid | yes | the `id` a main-page card carries |

There is deliberately no `login_type`, and sending one is a 400 (`extra_forbidden`) like any undeclared
parameter. `webinar-main-page` takes it because a signed-in visitor may legitimately want to preview the
signed-out page, so there the surface is a real choice. Here your token already answers it, and a parameter
that could contradict the token would be a second source of truth for one fact.

The id is the UUID, never `webinar_id_as_per_mf_sf` - that integer is unique only when paired with
`webinar_type`, and nothing in this backend hands it to a client.

### 7.2 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Webinar details retrieved successfully.",
  "data": { "login_type": "post_login", "webinar": { } }
}
```

The webinar object carries `subject_details` and `level_details.level_id` exactly as the card does - they are
produced by the same function, so the two screens cannot disagree.

`login_type` is echoed and is `pre_login` or `post_login`. It is more useful here than on the feed: there you
chose it, here it was DERIVED, so the echo is how you confirm which surface you got - and therefore whether
`registration` is present - without inspecting your own token.

### 7.3 The webinar object

**It is exactly the card object from section 8, plus four keys.** Render this page from the card type you
already have; the extras are additive. The shared keys are produced by the same function that shapes the
feed, so they cannot drift.

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string \| null | The long-form page body; `short_description` is the one-liner. |
| `trailer_url` | string \| null | |
| `trailer_thumbnail_url` | string \| null | |
| `product` | object \| null | See below. Null as a whole when the webinar is tagged to no product. |

`product`:

| Key | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string |
| `name` | string |
| `mini_description` | string \| null |
| `description` | string \| null |
| `horizontal_image` | string (url, `""` when unset) |
| `vertical_image` | string (url, `""` when unset) |
| `square_image` | string (url, `""` when unset) |

`registration` (section 8.1) is present **only on an authenticated request**, exactly as on the feed. An
anonymous caller has no registration to report, so the key is absent rather than null.

`eligible` (section 8.2) is deliberately NOT emitted. It is a property of a BOOKING, the feed attaches it
only on `completed_webinar`, and computing it here would be a second definition of eligibility.

### 7.4 `product` and `subject` are two different columns and may disagree

Both name a row of `Masterclass.Subject`, reached by two different paths, and this endpoint reports both
rather than picking a winner:

- **`subject`** (a string, on the card) is the subject reached THROUGH `caira_masterclass_level`. The feed has
  emitted it since 2026-09-09 and it is untouched, so the two screens agree.
- **`product`** (an object, detail page only) is `Webinar.subject`, the direct FK, whose help text calls it
  "the Miles product this webinar is sold under" and says it SUPERSEDES the `caira_check` /
  `non_caira_check` pair.

They are independent columns, so a webinar tagged to a level of one subject and sold under another reports
both, honestly, under two names. **Which one wins is an open maintainer decision** - see section 9.8. Until
it is taken, prefer `product` where you need the commercial programme and `subject` where you need to match
what the feed showed.

### 7.5 Refusals

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `webinar_id` missing, not a uuid, or any undeclared parameter |
| `403` | a bad or expired token. A request with NO token is served the pre-login surface, not refused |
| `404` | no webinar with that id is visible on this surface |

**The 404 is deliberately ambiguous.** "No such id" and "an id you may not see" are the same answer, so the
endpoint cannot be used to discover which ids exist. Visibility is the feed's own filter - soft-deleted,
cancelled, wrong login state and test webinars are all excluded before the id is matched, so a row the feed
hides cannot be opened by guessing.

---

### 9.3 `details.booking_url` is the response key; the column is named something else

The column was renamed to `zoom_booking_url` on 2026-09-15 and moved to the `Booking` table. THE RESPONSE KEY
IS UNCHANGED AND WILL STAY `booking_url` in v1 - renaming it is a client-visible break and belongs in a
versioned change, not in a column rename. If you see `zoom_booking_url` in a schema document or a backend
discussion, it is the same value.

The same applies to `details.calendar_id`, whose column is now `google_calender_id`.

### 9.8 `product` and `subject` can disagree, and neither has been declared the winner

Described in full in section 7.4. `Webinar.subject` (emitted as `product`) and
`caira_masterclass_level.subject` (emitted as `subject`) are independent columns pointing at the same table.
The model's help text says the direct FK supersedes the `caira_check` / `non_caira_check` pair, which implies
it is the authoritative one - but the feed has emitted the level's subject since 2026-09-09 and changing that
is a breaking change for a shipped contract.

Both are therefore emitted, under two names, on the detail page only. Collapsing them into one key is a
maintainer decision that has not been taken.

---

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebWebinarMainPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `web-events-webinar-main-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-main-page/?login_type=pre_login|post_login`

The webinar landing feed, in five buckets, for both sides of login.

RUDIMENTARY FIRST PASS, by request. It reads what the schema already supports and adds no new columns and no cache. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: it IS paginated now - each of the five buckets is a `read_paging` block (`<bucket>.page` / `<bucket>.page_size`, default 6, a slug per bucket from `slug_registry`) over the at-most-20 rows the query caps. What it does get right is the shape, because that is the part a client codes against and the expensive thing to change later.

ONE ENDPOINT FOR BOTH LOGIN STATES, NOT TWO. The two surfaces answer the same question and share four fifths of their query plan; splitting them would duplicate the visibility rules, which is precisely where two surfaces drift apart. The parameter selects the surface, and it is also what decides which `WebinarPriority` rows apply - that table is keyed per login state for the same reason.

AUTHENTICATION IS OPTIONAL AT THE FRAMEWORK LAYER AND MANDATORY AT THE APPLICATION LAYER, which is the only arrangement that works here. DRF resolves `permission_classes` during dispatch, BEFORE the view can read `login_type` - so `IsAuthenticated` would 401 the anonymous pre-login caller this endpoint exists to serve, and there is no permission class that can branch on a query parameter it has not been handed. `AllowAny` plus an explicit check inside `get()` is therefore the design, not a relaxation:

- `pre_login`  - served anonymously. A bearer token, if one is sent, is still resolved and still ignored; the caller asked for the signed-out page and gets it.
- `post_login` - refused with 401 unless the request authenticated.

`JWTAuthentication` is still installed, and that matters: it returns `None` when there is no `Authorization` header (so the request is anonymous and pre-login works), and RAISES `AuthenticationFailed` for a header that is present but bad. A malformed or expired token is therefore REJECTED on both branches - including `pre_login` - rather than silently downgraded to the anonymous page, which is the correct answer: a client sending a broken token has a problem it needs to see.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THAT REJECTION ARRIVES AS 401, with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`, because `MilesPlatform.authentication.JWTAuthentication` now implements `authenticate_header()` (measured). The 401 this view returns itself is a DIFFERENT case with the same status: a well-formed anonymous request asking for the post-login page, which the authenticator never rejects.

THE FIVE BUCKETS, and which of them the anonymous surface can populate:

`highlight_webinars`  Editorial. Driven by `WebinarPriority` rows for

```
THIS login state, lowest `priority` first. The
absence of a row is the signal - a webinar with no
active row for this state is not ranked last, it
is simply not here. Available pre-login.
```

`upcoming_webinars`   Everything visible in this state that has not

```
started, soonest first. Available pre-login.
```

`completed_webinar`   Per-user. Past webinars the user ATTENDED, each

```
tagged `eligible`. Post-login only.
```

`absent_webinar`      Per-user. Past webinars the user booked and did

```
not attend. Post-login only.
```

`missed_webinar`      Past webinars the caller is not committed to.

```
AVAILABLE PRE-LOGIN (2026-09-18): signed in it is
"never booked, or booked and then CANCELLED by
either side"; anonymously the caller has no
bookings, so it is every past webinar in the
window - which is what they have missed by not
being signed up.
```

SO PRE-LOGIN POPULATES THREE OF THE FIVE - `highlight_webinars`, `upcoming_webinars` and `missed_webinar`. The two that stay empty are the two that are statements about a BOOKING, which an anonymous caller does not have. Post-login populates all five, the three past ones from the caller's own attendance.

EVERY KEY IS ALWAYS PRESENT, EMPTY RATHER THAN OMITTED. A client that has to test for a key's existence before reading it will eventually forget to, and an absent key and an empty list mean the same thing to a rendering loop but different things to a null check. Fixed shape, varying contents.

WHAT `eligible` MEANS, AND THAT IT IS A DECISION. It is true when the booking's `attended_status` is `"1"` (attended), or when leadership force-overrode it on `BookingDetails`.

## 6. `GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-main-page/`

The webinar landing feed, in five buckets, for both sides of login. Web only.

This is a rudimentary first pass by request. The shape is the part that is settled; the bucket rules are
deliberately simple and each is a single filter, so a product correction is a one-line change.

### 6.1 Query parameters

| Param | Type | Required | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login_type` | string | yes | `pre_login`, `post_login` |

DELIBERATELY REQUIRED, WITH NO DEFAULT. Defaulting to `pre_login` would mean a signed-in client that forgot the
parameter silently receives the anonymous page - a valid 200 that is wrong, with the two booking buckets empty
rather than absent. Omitting it is a 400 naming the parameter.

The vocabulary is `pre_login` / `post_login`, with underscores. Those two literals are the stored values in the
database columns this endpoint filters on, so there is one vocabulary end to end and no translation map.

### 6.2 Authentication is conditional

| `login_type` | Anonymous request | Request with a valid token | Request with a BAD token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pre_login` | `200` | `200`, token resolved and ignored | `403` |
| `post_login` | `401 authentication_required` | `200` | `403` |

This is the only route in the app that is reachable anonymously and also serves per-user data. The branch
cannot live in a permission class - DRF resolves permissions during dispatch, before any view has read a query
parameter - so the view carries `AllowAny` and enforces the rule itself. It is a design, not a missing
`IsAuthenticated`.

A malformed or expired token is rejected on BOTH branches, including `pre_login`, rather than silently
downgraded to the anonymous page: a client sending a broken token has a problem it needs to see. That rejection
is the `403` from 1.2. The `401` here is the different case - a well-formed anonymous request asking for the
signed-in page - and it carries `message`, not `detail`:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "code": "authentication_required",
  "message": "login_type=post_login requires an authenticated request. Send a bearer token, or ask for login_type=pre_login."
}
```

### 6.3 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Webinar main page retrieved successfully.",
  "data": {
    "login_type": "post_login",
    "highlight_webinars": [],
    "upcoming_webinars": [],
    "completed_webinar": [],
    "absent_webinar": [],
    "missed_webinar": []
  }
}
```

EVERY KEY IS ALWAYS PRESENT, EMPTY RATHER THAN OMITTED. Fixed shape, varying contents - a rendering loop treats
an absent key and an empty list the same way, but a null check does not.

`pre_login` POPULATES THREE OF THE FIVE (amended 2026-09-18): `highlight_webinars`, `upcoming_webinars` and
`missed_webinar`. The two that stay empty are `completed_webinar` and `absent_webinar`, which are statements
about a BOOKING that an anonymous caller does not have. `post_login` populates all five, the three
backward-looking ones from the caller's own attendance.

The two plural keys and the three singular keys are inconsistent, and that is preserved deliberately: they
match the requested contract, and renaming a client contract to tidy it is a breaking change for cosmetic gain.

### 6.4 The five buckets

| Bucket | Per-user? | What is in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlight_webinars` | no | Editorial. Driven by priority rows for THIS login state, lowest priority first. The absence of a row is the signal - an unranked webinar is not last, it is simply not here. Upcoming only. |
| `upcoming_webinars` | no | Everything visible in this login state that has not started, soonest first. |
| `completed_webinar` | yes | Past webinars the user ATTENDED. Each carries `eligible`. Post-login only. |
| `absent_webinar` | yes | Past webinars the user booked and did not attend. Post-login only. |
| `missed_webinar` | partly | Past webinars the caller is not committed to. BOTH login states - see below. |

`highlight_webinars` is a curated rail over the same webinars as `upcoming_webinars`, so the two lists overlap
by design. De-duplicate on `id` if your layout needs to.

Every bucket is capped at 20 rows. There is no pagination - this is a landing page, not a catalogue. The three
backward-looking buckets look back 90 days.

`absent` and `missed` are disjoint and the split is a product decision, not a schema fact: ABSENT is a live
booking the user did not honour, MISSED is a webinar they are not committed to.

THE ROUTING IS BY `attended_status`, AMENDED 2026-09-18. A booking the user CANCELLED now lands in
`missed_webinar`; it previously appeared in no bucket at all, so a cancelled webinar vanished from the page.

| `attended_status` | Bucket |
| --- | --- |
| `1` attended | `completed_webinar` |
| `2` not attended | `absent_webinar` |
| `3` registered | `absent_webinar` |
| `""` MF has not reported yet | `absent_webinar` |
| `4` cancelled | `missed_webinar` |
| no booking row at all | `missed_webinar` |

Cancellation reaches this endpoint on two independent columns - `status = false` (this system cancelled the
booking) and `attended_status = "4"` (MF reported it cancelled) - and BOTH route to `missed_webinar`, so the
same user action does not land in different buckets depending on which side recorded it.

ATTENDANCE OUTRANKS CANCELLATION. `attended_status = "1"` is `completed_webinar` even on a cancelled booking:
attendance is a fact about a session that already happened, a cancellation is a statement of intent about it,
and `completed_webinar` is the only bucket carrying `eligible` - so routing an attended row elsewhere would
withdraw the CPE / badge affordance from someone who earned it.

---

## 8. The webinar card, shared by all five main-page buckets

All five buckets carry identical objects, so one view model reads `highlight_webinars[0]` and
`missed_webinar[0]` alike.

```json
{
  "id": "3f1a9c7e-5b42-4d9a-8f10-2c6be7d41a55",
  "slug": "caira-level-1-orientation",
  "name": "CAIRA Level 1",
  "type": "webinar",
  "short_description": "...",
  "start_date_time": "2026-09-20T13:00:00+00:00",
  "end_date_time": "2026-09-20T14:00:00+00:00",
  "duration_seconds": 3600,
  "webinar_zoom_id": "84123456789",
  "is_test_webinar": false,
  "webinar_why_attend_points": [],
  "webinar_what_will_you_learn_points": [],
  "subject": "CAIRA",
  "subject_details": {
    "id": "b2c4e1a8-7f39-4c52-9d61-08ab3e7f4d12",
    "subject": "CAIRA"
  },
  "level_details": {
    "level_id": "d57e0b93-1a46-4f88-ae20-6c91f2b7e034",
    "level_number": 1,
    "level_name": "Level 1",
    "level_actual_name": "Foundations of AI for Accountants"
  },
  "horizontal_thumbnail": "https://.../h.png",
  "vertical_thumbnail": "https://.../v.png",
  "square_image": "https://.../s.png",
  "fields_of_study": [{ "id": "...", "name": "Information Technology", "cpe_credit": 1.0 }],
  "total_cpe_credits": 1.0
}
```

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string | This is what you send to `register-via-zoom`. |
| `slug` | string or null | |
| `name` | string | |
| `type` | string | `webinar`, `offline`, `orientation`, `premier`. Only the first two are registrable here. |
| `short_description` | string | |
| `start_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null | |
| `end_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null | |
| `duration_seconds` | integer or null | **SECONDS** from 2026-09-25; one hour is `3600`. Was `duration_minutes`. |
| `webinar_zoom_id` | string or null | The id Zoom keys the session on. Distinct from the MF/SF ingest anchor. |
| `is_test_webinar` | boolean | Visible only to an internal test user, in either login state. An ordinary user never receives one. |
| `webinar_why_attend_points` | array of strings, or null | Editorial copy. `null` when the operator never authored any - not an empty array. |
| `webinar_what_will_you_learn_points` | array of strings, or null | Same. |
| `subject` | string or null | THE CAIRA / CAIBA ANSWER. See below. `null` when the webinar carries no level. |
| `subject_details` | object or null | `{id, subject}`. Null together with `subject`. |
| `level_details` | object or null | `{level_id, level_number, level_name, level_actual_name}`, or null. |

`subject` plus `level_details.level_number` is what renders "CAIRA L1". `level_details` is NULL AS A WHOLE
when the webinar has no level, so you test one key rather than four - and "no level" stays distinct from "a
level whose name happens to be blank", which four flat nulls cannot express. `subject_details` is null
together with `subject`, for the same reason.

**`subject_details` AND `level_details.level_id` WERE ADDED ON 2026-09-17.** Both are additive - nothing was
removed or renamed, and `subject` stays exactly where it was because shipped clients read it. They exist
because **a name is not an address**: `Subject.name` is not unique, and a level's generated `level_name`
("Level 1") repeats across every subject, so neither could be used to link anywhere. The subject name is
REPEATED inside `subject_details` on purpose - a client rendering from that object should not have to reach
back out to a sibling key for its label.
| `horizontal_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `vertical_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `square_image` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `fields_of_study` | array | `{id, name, cpe_credit}` per active field of study. Empty array when nothing is tagged. |
| `total_cpe_credits` | float or null | The SUM of the above. `null`, not `0`, when nothing is tagged. |

**`total_cpe_credits` WAS `cpe_credits` UNTIL 2026-09-18** - a rename, with no alias kept. It is the sum over
`fields_of_study`, each of which carries its own `cpe_credit` (singular), and the old plural read as the same
quantity as the per-entry one. The rename is scoped to this payload: `Masterclass` course payloads and the
Netcore activity params still send `cpe_credits`, deliberately.

`caira_check` and `non_caira_check` are DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED on this endpoint (they are on `all-bookings`).
They are two booleans describing the same thing `subject` describes properly, and a client given both would
have to decide which wins. Use `subject`.

### 8.1 `registration` - on `highlight_webinars` and `upcoming_webinars`, `post_login` only

```json
"registration": {
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "registration_status": "REGISTERED",
  "attempt_id": "9c2f...",
  "join_url": "https://us06web.zoom.us/w/8412...",
  "error_code": null,
  "error_message": null,
  "zoom_attempts": 1,
  "completed_at": "2026-09-17T09:14:22.118+00:00",
  "route_to_web_lms": false
}
```

Same three-state contract as section 3.2 - branch on `registration_status`, not on `status`.

The key is ABSENT on the `pre_login` branch (anonymous callers have no registration to report) and on the three
past buckets (registration is an affordance - register vs join - and a webinar that already happened offers
neither; `completed_webinar` answers the question those rows raise with `eligible` instead).

A user who registered before the attempt-row pipeline existed has a booking and no attempt. That case comes
back as `registration_status: "REGISTERED"` with `status`, `attempt_id`, `join_url` and `completed_at` all
`null` and `zoom_attempts: 0`. Do not read "no attempt id" as "not registered" - registering again would spend
another Zoom registrant slot on a seat they already hold.

`route_to_web_lms` is `true` only for an internal test user on a CAIRA webinar today. When `true`, open the
session in the web-LMS surface instead of `join_url`.

### 8.2 `eligible` - on `completed_webinar` only

Boolean. `true` when the booking's `attended_status` is `"1"` (attended), or when leadership force-overrode it.

It is deliberately NOT recomputed from `attended_webinar_duration_seconds` against `total_webinar_duration_seconds`: the
thresholds live in the attendance ingest, and a second implementation of a rule that already exists elsewhere
is a rule that will disagree with itself.

---

### 9.1 `one_on_one` is always empty today

Reading 1:1 bookings works. Nothing in this repository CREATES one yet - the career-counselling write path is
not ported. So the `one_on_one` list is empty until that lands or historical rows are migrated in. An empty
list is not a fault. Build the card anyway; the shape is final.

Of the four `booking_type` values, only `career` can be newly booked. `office`, `resume` and `alumni` remain
legal to READ so historical rows keep resolving, so a reader must accept all four.

### 9.2 `webinar-main-page` does not filter by enrolment

`show_webinar_as_per_enrollment` (CPA / CMA / CAIRA / USP) is NOT applied, so the `post_login` upcoming list is
wider than a finished implementation's would be. Applying it needs the caller's enrolment set, which this pass
does not read.

### 9.6 No caching, no pagination on `webinar-main-page`

Every call hits Postgres, and the buckets are hard-capped rather than paginated. Expect that to change behind
the same response shape.
