request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `BrochureDownloadViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `brochure-download-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces 3 legacy MilesOne routes:** `POST caira/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`, `POST cpa/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`, `POST cma/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`

`POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CAIRA|CPA|CMA`

Records a brochure download: files a Salesforce lead, books the learner into that ONE programme's next webinar, and pushes the Netcore `brochure_downloaded` event.

ONE ROUTE FOR THREE BROCHURES AS OF 2026-09-29 (maintainer). It replaced `_FunnelLeadViewV1` and its three subclasses - `caira/`, `cpa/` and `cma/brochure-download/` - which were three paths, three classes and one body. All three 404 now, with no shim.

THE URLCONF ARGUED AGAINST EXACTLY THIS, AND THE ARGUMENT IS RECORDED THERE RATHER THAN DELETED. It held that a path segment is unspoofable and unomittable, so which brochure was tapped could not be lost. A REQUIRED `ChoiceField` on a `StrictInputSerializer` is the same guarantee by another mechanism - absent is a 400, unknown is a 400, and the vocabulary is closed. What the decision protected is intact; what it also bought, per-path permissioning and retirement, is what was given up, and these three never used it.

THE PROGRAMME IS A QUERY PARAMETER BECAUSE THERE IS NO BODY. These endpoints have never accepted one. Its sibling `api/v1/account/enquiry/` puts `programme` in the body, which looks inconsistent until you notice that endpoint already has a body for its optional `lead` block. Neither invents a container for one field.

A BODY IS STILL REFUSED, AND THAT IS CHECKED HERE. The query serializer never looks at one, so without this a caller could POST anything and be told it worked. Legacy got this for free from a field-less body serializer; the check moved rather than disappeared.

ONE AUDIENCE, NOT THE PATHWAY FAN-OUT, and no `course_id` on the lead - see `capture_brochure_download` for why those two are not the same decision.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `programme` - Required. One of: `CPA`, `CMA`, `CAIRA`. Which brochure was downloaded: CAIRA, CPA or CMA.

**No request body by design.** Programme is `?programme=`; no body is accepted.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 10.2 The brochure route - the learner acted ON a programme

| Route | Audience booked | Netcore push |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CAIRA` | CAIRA | `brochure_downloaded` |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CPA` | CPA | `brochure_downloaded` |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CMA` | CMA | `brochure_downloaded` |

**ONE ROUTE, NOT THREE, SINCE 2026-09-30.** The three paths did the same work and differed only in
which programme their own URL named, which is a parameter wearing a path segment. `?programme=` is
required and validated against the three values above; anything else is a 400 rather than a 404, so a
typo says what was wrong with it.

**IT STILL TAKES NO BODY AT ALL.** Any key you send is a 400 - the serializer declares no fields, and
the programme arrives on the query string. (RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the 400 comes from the view, which refuses
any non-empty body; the query serializer declares `programme` and never sees the body.)
The old `caira/`, `cpa/` and `cma/` paths answer 404 with no
shim.

**Exactly ONE audience is booked, not the pathway fan-out.** A CPA brochure tap names the programme;
routing it through the learner's pathway would also book them into CAIRA and CMA webinars off a signal
that said CPA. `enquiry/` with `programme: "CAIRA"` behaves the same way, for the same reason.

The lead itself is still filed against `user.pathway`, NOT against the brochure. The CRM's course field
answers "what are they buying" while the audience answers "what did they just look at", and legacy
filed it the same way.

### 10.3 What happens after the 200

The Salesforce lead is **awaited** - you are told whether it was recorded. The webinar booking and the
Netcore push are **detached**, and their outcome is not in the status code. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: only the
booking is detached. The Netcore push is AWAITED, before the lead - `notify_brochure_downloaded` runs through
`sync_to_async` and makes a blocking POST - so a slow Netcore delays the response; its outcome still never
changes the status code. A 200 means the lead was
filed; it does not mean a seat was confirmed.

Auto-registration fires even when Salesforce refused. A CRM outage is not a reason to withhold a
webinar seat from a learner who just expressed interest.

**Module:** `Notification.views`  
**Route name:** `notification-app-inbox-bell-mark-all-read-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Mark every unread bell row for this caller as read.

`POST api/v1/notification/app-inbox-bell/mark-all-read/`

TAKES NO BODY. The caller is the token and the scope is "everything of theirs that is unread", so there is nothing to send and this endpoint ships no request template.

ONE BULK UPDATE, NOT A ROW-AT-A-TIME LOOP, so a learner with hundreds of notifications costs one statement. `count` in the response says how many rows actually changed, which is `0` on a second call - that makes it idempotent and safe to retry.

SCOPED TO THE AUTHENTICATED CALLER; there is no way to clear somebody else's bell.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the filter is `user` + `is_read=False` only - it does NOT exclude `to_be_deleted` rows, so soft-deleted rows are flipped too and `count` can exceed the unread-count badge. Nothing validates the body, so a stray body is ignored with a 200 - DEFECT against the strict-input rule, not fixed here.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: enveloped by the default renderer, which lifts
`message`.
200 OK: `{success, message, data: {status, count}}`.
401: no or invalid Bearer token (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`).
500 Internal Server Error: When the bulk update failed; `data` is
    `{status, error}`.
```

**No request body by design.** Acts on the caller's whole inbox; nothing to scope.

**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Return one product addressed by its Miles360 programme `code`.

A PEER OF `CatalogueProductViewV1`, NOT A SUBCLASS. Subclassing read well - resolve the code, delegate to `super().get()` - but the override renames `product_id` to `product_code`, which is a narrower signature than the base promises and both checkers report it. Two views over one shared `_cached_product_payload` says the same thing without lying about the inheritance.

THE SAME PAYLOAD AND THE SAME CACHE ENTRY. Both routes resolve to a primary key before the cache is consulted, so a product is stored once however it was addressed.

`code` IS THE MILES360 REGISTRY KEY, NOT A URL SLUG, and this couples the two deliberately (maintainer, 2026-09-22). The consequence to hold onto: that field's help_text says to retire a code in place rather than edit it, and this route is now a second reason why - editing one breaks every link that used it. A product with a BLANK code has no address here at all, which is most of the catalogue.

AMBIGUITY IS A 404, NEVER A GUESS. `cat_uniq_product_code` is case-SENSITIVE, so `cma` and `CMA` can both exist as distinct products while a case-insensitive lookup matches both. Rather than pick one - serving the wrong product with a 200 - this refuses. See `_resolve_code`.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CatalogueProductsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Catalogue.views`  
**Route name:** `catalogue-products-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One page of active products, newest catalogue surface for both clients.

`GET api/v1/catalogue/products/?page=&page_size=&is_book=&search=`

UNIVERSAL. The app and the web ask the same question of the same catalogue and read the same answer, so this keeps the shared `api/` prefix rather than splitting by surface.

`ProductListQueryV1` validates the query STRICTLY, so an undeclared or misspelled parameter is a 400 rather than a silently ignored filter. `search` matches `title` case-insensitively as a substring; `is_book` is a tri-state - omit it for every product, send it to pick a side.

THE ORDERING IS RESTATED ON THE QUERYSET, NOT LEFT TO `Meta`. Under OFFSET pagination a non-total order lets one row appear on two pages and another on none, and an ordering a stray call could strip is not a guarantee.

CACHED UNDER A KEY THAT CONTAINS NO USER ID, and never may - the product list is identical for every learner. The page, the page size and both filters are all in the key, so two different filters cannot read each other's page. See the module docstring for why folding a user in is the mistake `HOMEPAGE_DATA_ASGI_PREFIX` was retired for.

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

- `search` - Optional.

Return this learner's progress for one variant.

READS BOTH LEVELS AND SAYS SO. `Variant_Progress` is the per-variant rollup; `SubjectProgress` is content-level and counts across every variant that sells the same subject. A client showing "3 of 8 subjects done" needs the second, and a client showing the variant's own completion badge needs the first, so the response carries both rather than picking one and being wrong for the other caller.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `GET api/v1/catalogue/progress/variant/<variant_id>/` (`catalogue-progress-variant-v1`), JWTAuthentication + IsAuthenticated. `variant_id` scopes only the 404 gate (unknown or retired variant) and `variant_rollup`. `subjects` and `watched_video_ids` are EVERY row this learner holds, unfiltered by the variant - the view reads no variant-to-subject mapping. `variant_rollup` is null unless an operator wrote the row: nothing in this API writes `Variant_Progress` (its only other reference is the admin registration). Responses: 200, 404, 500.

**View:** `CatalogueVariantViewV1`  
**Module:** `Catalogue.views`  
**Route name:** `catalogue-variant-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One variant with its content blocks, media and this learner's watch flags.

`GET api/v1/catalogue/variant/<variant_id>/`

UNIVERSAL, and the only catalogue read whose body differs per caller.

THE SHARED PAYLOAD IS CACHED; THE WATCH FLAGS ARE NOT. The variant, its posts and its media are identical for everybody and come from one user-free key. This learner's watched-video set is read live on every request and laid over the top. Folding the user into that key would multiply a shared blob by the user base with no invalidation.

THE WATCH FLAG IS KEYED ON THE YOUTUBE ID, NOT ON A FILE ROW, so a clip watched inside one variant reads as watched everywhere it appears. A per-file flag would make the same clip unwatched again the moment it was sold inside a second variant - see `CatalogueVideoProgressViewV1`.

TWO QUERIES FOR POSTS AND FILES, NOT ONE PER POST. Django's async queryset methods are `sync_to_async` wrappers that run one after another on the request's single-thread executor, so gathering them buys nothing; the fix is fewer round trips, not parallel ones.

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

```
GET
```

```
200 OK: The variant.
404 Not Found: When unknown or retired.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CommerceAddressViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-address-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET, PATCH, DELETE  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One of this learner's addresses - read it, edit it, or remove it.

`GET    api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/` `PATCH  api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/` `DELETE api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/`

UNIVERSAL. THE PATH CARRIES AN ID AND THE QUERYSET IS STILL USER-SCOPED. An object-id lookup that is not scoped to the caller is an IDOR, and this is the endpoint shape where that is easiest to forget.

SOMEONE ELSE'S ADDRESS IS A 404, NOT A 403, and the difference is the point: 403 would confirm the row exists and hand an attacker a membership oracle over the id space.

A DELETE THAT A SETTLED ORDER STILL POINTS AT IS A 409, NOT A DELETE. Every FK into an address is a historical record of where something was actually sent, and an order whose address vanished cannot be reconstructed. The learner is told to add a new address instead.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the 409 test is ANY `Order` or `Order_Line` naming the address as shipping or billing, whatever its status (pending, failed and cancelled included) - not only a settled one. Otherwise the row is HARD deleted (`Address` has no `active` flag), and the two `Checkout` FKs, which are `SET_NULL` and not checked, are silently blanked on any cart that used it. A 500 is also possible on every verb.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET, PATCH, DELETE
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: On read or edit.
204 No Content: On a successful delete.
404 Not Found: When the address is unknown or not this learner's.
409 Conflict: When an order references it.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed body.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CommerceCartViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-cart-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET, PATCH  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

This learner's live cart with its lines, created empty if they have none.

`GET api/v1/commerce/cart/`

UNIVERSAL. ONE LIVE CART PER LEARNER - there is no cart id in the path because there is never a choice of which one to read.

A GET CREATES A ROW, WHICH LOOKS LIKE A WRITE ON A READ AND IS DELIBERATE. Every client's first action is to show the cart, and answering 404 there would make "no cart yet" a special case in every caller. The row is empty and costs one insert per learner, once.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT PRICED AT READ TIME. The GET reads the money columns STORED on `Checkout` and `Checkout_Line` and calls no pricing code, so a price change published after a line was added is NOT reflected when the cart is opened. A line is repriced only when it is added again or PATCHed (`price_for_variant`); the totals are re-summed only on a line write.

THIS SURFACE STOPS SHORT OF PAYMENT. A cart can be built, priced and read, and nothing here turns it into an `Order` - the payment gateway is out of merge scope, and an endpoint that creates a paid order without a payment is worse than a missing one.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The cart.
```

**View:** `CommerceCartViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-cart-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET, PATCH  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

This learner's live cart with its lines, created empty if they have none.

`GET api/v1/commerce/cart/`

UNIVERSAL. ONE LIVE CART PER LEARNER - there is no cart id in the path because there is never a choice of which one to read.

A GET CREATES A ROW, WHICH LOOKS LIKE A WRITE ON A READ AND IS DELIBERATE. Every client's first action is to show the cart, and answering 404 there would make "no cart yet" a special case in every caller. The row is empty and costs one insert per learner, once.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT PRICED AT READ TIME. The GET reads the money columns STORED on `Checkout` and `Checkout_Line` and calls no pricing code, so a price change published after a line was added is NOT reflected when the cart is opened. A line is repriced only when it is added again or PATCHed (`price_for_variant`); the totals are re-summed only on a line write.

THIS SURFACE STOPS SHORT OF PAYMENT. A cart can be built, priced and read, and nothing here turns it into an `Order` - the payment gateway is out of merge scope, and an endpoint that creates a paid order without a payment is worse than a missing one.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CommerceCartLineViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-cart-line-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** PATCH, DELETE  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Change or remove one line of this learner's cart.

`PATCH  api/v1/commerce/cart/line/<line_id>/`  quantity or booking choice `DELETE api/v1/commerce/cart/line/<line_id>/`  remove the line

UNIVERSAL, and user-scoped in the queryset like every other Commerce read - another learner's line is a 404, never a 403.

AN EMPTY PATCH BODY IS A 400, NOT A NO-OP 200. `exclude_unset` separates "set this to null" from "do not touch this", so a request that names no field at all is a client bug worth reporting rather than a successful request that changed nothing.

THE CART IS RETURNED WHOLE after either verb, so quantity changes and their effect on the total arrive together. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: only the PATCHed line is repriced; a DELETE reprices nothing (a hard delete of the line, then the totals re-summed). An explicit `null` is NOT "set to null" here: `{"quantity": null}` passes the empty-body check and `patch_cart_line` treats None as "keep", so it is a 200 that changed nothing. The cart returned is the caller's latest pending cart, re-read after the write.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

```
PATCH, DELETE
```

```
200 OK: The repriced cart.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed or empty body.
404 Not Found: When the line is unknown or not this learner's.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CommerceCheckoutViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-checkout-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Freeze the learner's open cart into a pending Order, or reconcile the one it already has.

CALLING THIS TWICE AGAINST ONE CART RETURNS THE SAME ORDER (D-L3). The first call creates the order; every later call while that order is still unpaid RECONCILES its lines to the cart's current contents in place and answers with the SAME `order_id`, so support, receipts and order history keep one identifier across the buyer's whole session. The response shape is identical either way - the client never has to know which happened - and the activity log records `reconciled` to tell them apart. `create_order_from_cart` decides which path runs, off `cart.pending_order_id`; this view only reads the `order_id` out of whichever success shape comes back.

STOPS AT `pending`, NOT `paid` - see the module docstring's note on where this surface stops. This is the endpoint that turns a cart into an `Order`; nothing here or downstream of it moves money or marks that order paid - it only starts the Stripe Checkout Session that can.

ALSO STARTS THE FIRST PAYMENT SESSION, IN THE SAME REQUEST (D-P15). One order can have N payment attempts, so the standalone `CommercePaymentSessionViewV1` remains for attempt 2 onward; this view only saves the client the round trip for attempt 1. Session creation runs AFTER the order is committed and can never undo it - see `post` for why a gateway failure still returns `201`.

NEVER `get_or_create_cart`. That helper exists for `GET /cart/` and the cart-line endpoints, where a brand-new visitor needs SOMETHING to render or add to, so auto-creating an empty cart on read is correct there. Checkout is the opposite case: a cart stays `"open"` through checkout itself (D-L1), but if the learner's most recently touched cart has since been purchased or cancelled, silently handing back a FRESH empty cart here would mask that and answer "your cart is empty" instead of the true "you already paid for this" or "you cancelled this". `_cart_to_check_out` below reads a cart of ANY status and hands its id straight to `create_order_from_cart` - the one place that already knows how to tell "empty" apart from "not open" for that id.

THE BODY MAY NAME THE CART THREE WAYS - an exact `cart_id`, a `country` naming a market, or nothing at all for the current cart. An earlier revision of this docstring said checkout took NO cart id, which was true when multi-cart did not exist; `cart_id` was added 2026-09-23 because market addressing re-resolves at confirm time and so cannot pin the cart a buyer was actually SHOWN. See `CheckoutBodyV1` for which form to use when.

Body template generated from `CheckoutBodyV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `CommerceCheckoutCancelViewV1`  
**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-checkout-cancel-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** none

Where Stripe sends the buyer who backed out of the hosted page.

READ-ONLY. It reports the attempt's state and changes nothing - no session is expired, no record is failed, and the order is untouched and still payable from `POST /api/v1/commerce/payment/session/`.

AN EARLIER DRAFT DID MUTATE, AND THAT WAS WRONG. It expired the session at Stripe and failed the attempt, reasoning that a cancelled session stays payable for 24 hours (D-P16). The reasoning mislocated the protection: `start_payment_for_order` already expires every outstanding session before creating a new one, so the double-pay window closes at the moment it would otherwise open. Mutating here added nothing and cost something, because `cancel_url` is a plain GET anyone can replay - a mutating cancel is a way to fail a stranger's pending attempt.

THE ORDER IS NEVER CANCELLED EITHER. Clicking back is not abandoning a purchase; doing so would burn an order row per moment of hesitation and make `cancelled` mean two different things.

TAKES `?order_id=` RATHER THAN `?session_id=`, and Stripe forces that: it substitutes `{CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` into `success_url` only, and the session id does not exist when `cancel_url` is built. A `session_id` is still accepted and preferred when a caller holds one. The weaker identifier is tolerable precisely because this endpoint does nothing.

**Module:** `Commerce.views`  
**Route name:** `commerce-checkout-success-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** none

Where Stripe sends the buyer after a completed payment.

ASKS STRIPE, THEN SETTLES - IT DOES NOT TRUST THE REDIRECT (HZ-P2). The browser arriving proves nothing and is not consulted. This settles only when Stripe, asked directly, reports `payment_status` is `paid`; the redirect merely names which session to ask about. A buyer who visits this URL by hand moves no money.

WHY IT SETTLES AT ALL, GIVEN THE WEBHOOK. A webhook can be undeliverable, or acknowledged by a delivery that then crashed, and before this endpoint existed such a payment sat `pending` with money already taken and nothing to surface it. The buyer's return is the one moment somebody demonstrably cares about that order. Settlement is idempotent, so a webhook arriving afterwards credits nothing extra.

Receive and settle Stripe events.

UNAUTHENTICATED BY NECESSITY, SIGNATURE-VERIFIED IN FACT. Stripe cannot hold a JWT. `authentication_classes = []` and NO permission class: a permission class runs before the handler and cannot see the raw body verification needs (HZ-P1), so putting the check there would mean parsing the body twice and failing the signature.

NON-2XX MEANS RETRY, DELIBERATELY (D-P13). Stripe redelivers a failed event for up to three days. A bad signature is 400 and will never succeed on retry. A processing failure AFTER a valid signature is 500 precisely so Stripe tries again, which `Gateway_Event` makes safe.

DISPATCH IS WIRED (Task 6): this view verifies the signature, de-duplicates by `(gateway, event_id)`, and hands the verified event to `webhook_events. dispatch_stripe_event`, which maps the event type to a `Commerce.utils.gateways.settlement` action through a dict lookup - or acknowledges it with 200 and no effect when the type is not one this application acts on. An unhandled event type is not an error, and a non-2xx here would make Stripe retry something nothing will ever act on; see `webhook_events`'s module docstring for why that policy is the opposite of the refusal maps elsewhere in this file.

**Body template could not be resolved from the code.** Fill it in by hand and add the pattern to the generator.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL

**Methods on this view:** POST

Mark one target watched, or un-watch it.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE WRITER FOR `watched_by_me`, AND THREE SURFACES READ IT: the AI-in-Accounting reels feed (`watched_by_me` per card), Varun Masterclass (`is_watched` per clip) and the Programs stories rail (`watched` per story, `ProgramsPage/views.py::_watched_asset_ids`). All are `CMS.Asset` rows - the endpoint accepts `cms_asset` and nothing else. Before this endpoint's predecessor existed nothing wrote the row those feeds read, so the field was structurally incapable of being true. Ported from legacy's `POST /watched_by_me/` (`FileWatchedView`), which legacy shipped as a pair with the reels reader.

`Masterclass` IS DELIBERATELY NOT ONE OF THEM (maintainer, 2026-10-01). A course carries its own progress, chapter by chapter, in its own tables - a coarser "watched" here would be a second answer to a settled question, and it is not something a learner is shown. `_TARGETS['masterclass_course']` sets `interaction_fk = None` and the word is absent from `InteractionTargetKind`, so a watch naming a course is a 400 at the edge rather than a stored row.

THE THIRD READER NAMED HERE UNTIL 2026-10-01 WAS `IndustryUnplugged`, and that app is gone - its family left `_TARGETS` the same day, measured at zero rows in all three tables.

RENAMED FROM `ContentWatchedViewV1`, which lived in `HomepageContent`. The "Content" was accurate while homepage content was the only watchable thing; it stopped being accurate when `IndustryUnplugged` landed, and a class name that names one of the three families it serves is the kind of thing a reader trusts and should not.

Idempotent: sending the same value twice returns 200 with `changed=False`, so a client replaying a scroll event needs no special case. That path is also the CHEAPEST one - see `set_interaction`, which reads before it writes precisely because a player re-posts this on every playback.

THE CALL SHAPE, SINCE 2026-10-08::

```
POST api/v1/engagement/watched/?target_kind=cms_asset
{"target_id": "<uuid>", "value": true}
```

`value` defaults to true, so marking something watched is one body field. `value: false` withdraws it by UPDATING the row rather than deleting it (H-14), so "never watched" and "changed their mind" stay distinguishable.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `target_kind` - Required. One of: `cms_asset`. Which family the body's `target_id` belongs to.

Record that a learner finished one LMS content item.

`POST api/v1/lms/progress/`

ONE CALL FOR A VIDEO, AN E-BOOK OR AN MCQ::

```
POST api/v1/lms/progress/?item_type=mcq
{"item_id": "<uuid>", "completed": true}
```

THE QUERY SAYS WHICH KIND, THE BODY SAYS WHICH ROW. `item_type` is a CROSS-CHECK, not a lookup key - the server reads the row's own type either way, and refuses with a 400 when the two disagree. A client holding an MCQ's id while believing it is marking a video gets told, instead of a 200 and a completion filed against the wrong thing.

IDEMPOTENT. Sending the same value twice returns 200 with `created: false` and changes nothing, so a player re-posting on playback needs no special case. `completed: false` undoes a mark by UPDATING the row rather than deleting it, so "never started" and "changed their mind" stay distinct.

AN `item_id` NAMING NO ACTIVE ROW IS A 404, not a 500. `item` is a foreign key, so an unknown id would otherwise surface as an `IntegrityError` out of the upsert - and until `LMSContentItem` is seeded, every id is unknown.

```
200 OK: `{status, created, result: {item_id, item_type, completed}}`.

    `item_type` that disagrees with the row

404 Not Found: When no active content item carries that id.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

📜 The Spectrum of Audit Opinions:
• Unmodified Opinion – A clear signal that the financials are fairly presented with no material misstatements
• Qualified Opinion – A cautionary flag indicating a specific issue, such as a GAAP violation or audit limitation
• Adverse Opinion – A direct statement that the financials cannot be trusted, leading to a collapse in investor confidence
• Disclaimer of Opinion – A sign that the auditor could not obtain enough evidence to express any opinion
• Resignation – The most drastic move, where the auditor steps away completely, signalling deep systemic issues

                "long_description": "Success in business isn’t just about growth. It’s about knowing what to measure, when to act, and how to sustain performance. Just like a car’s dashboard keeps a driver informed, businesses rely on performance metrics to stay on course. CMAs guide this process by focusing on:

• Profitability metrics like net profit margin and return on investment
• Efficiency indicators such as working capital and inventory turnover
• Liquidity ratios including current ratio and quick ratio
• Solvency metrics like debt-to-equity and debt coverage ratios
• Operational leverage and break-even analysis to understand cost structures

4. Learning, growth, and innovation

CMAs help businesses track what truly matters. Performance management is not just about reporting results. It’s about using insights to drive better decisions and long-term value.

                "long_description": "What brings down a company isn’t always bad business decisions or market crashes. Sometimes, it’s something far more silent. A missing approval. This isn’t just compliance talk. It’s the difference between order and chaos, between transparency and deception.

💼 Start with the Five Pillars of Internal Control:
1. Control Environment - A company’s ethical backbone. Without it, even the best policies collapse.
2. Risk Assessment - Spotting weaknesses before fraudsters do.
3. Information and Communication - Transparency wins. Secrecy gives fraud a place to hide.
4. Monitoring Activities - What isn’t reviewed isn’t controlled.  
5. Control Activities - The locks on the financial doors: segregation of duties, reconciliations, authorisations.

These are not optional features. They’re what turn a financial system into a fortress.

🚨 Then come the cautionary tales:
• Enron, once the darling of Wall Street, built on manipulated profits and hidden debt. When the truth came out, it wasn’t just the company that fell — it was investor confidence across the market.
• Satyam, often called India’s Enron, where the chairman personally inflated numbers with fake invoices and bank statements. Billions were wiped out overnight.
• Wells Fargo, where a culture of aggressive sales targets led to thousands of fake accounts. No one questioned the numbers until it was too late.
• Walmart, whose global ambitions stumbled over bribery scandals in Mexico, Brazil, China, and India — all because compliance took a back seat.

In each case, it wasn’t just a rogue employee or a one-off mistake. It was a failure of the system. Internal controls were ignored, bypassed, or overridden.

🎯 So, what does a strong internal control system really look like?
• Governance that starts at the top.
• Segregation of duties so no single person has too much control.
• Regular reviews and independent checks.
• And now, even AI and analytics to detect anomalies faster than humans ever could.

Fraud rarely happens in a flash. It builds in the silence of unchecked moments. But when internal controls are strong, they close the doors before anyone can sneak through.

A well-governed system doesn’t just protect a balance sheet, it protects reputation, investor trust, and long-term business integrity.

**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppVarunMasterclassSubjectViewV1`  
**Module:** `VarunMasterclass.views`  
**Route name:** `app-varun-masterclass-subject-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One Varun Masterclass subject and its clips.

`GET app-api/v1/varun-masterclass/subject/<subject_id>/`

THE DETAIL READ behind a rail tile. `subject_id` is a `CMS.Page` id - Varun content is authored as CMS pages, so the subject is a page and its clips are the assets hanging off it.

AN UNKNOWN OR INACTIVE SUBJECT IS A `404`, soft delete included, so a withdrawn subject stops resolving rather than rendering empty. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: so is a subject whose rail is inactive or not a `varun-` root; the 200 body is `{subject, rail}` (`rail` without its subjects); 500 on a handled failure.

NOTE ON UAT MEDIA: the clip URLs in a non-production environment are STAND-IN HLS renditions of real Masterclass recordings, not this subject's own video. The card's title, thumbnail and copy are its own; the stream behind it is someone else's course until the real recordings are transcoded.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The subject and its clips.
404 Not Found: When the subject is unknown or inactive.
```

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET v2/learn`

The Learn page - LMS tokens first, then every section with its cards.

`GET app-api/v1/learn/page/`

ONE READ PER SCREEN. Sections and their cards arrive together, so a cold open is a single request rather than one per rail.

THE LMS TOKENS COME FIRST, AND THE ORDER IS THE CONTRACT. The client needs them to address the LMS at all, so they lead the payload rather than sitting inside a section the renderer might reach late.

A MISSING PAGE TREE IS A `404`, not an empty 200: the Learn page is authored content, and nothing configured is an operator problem worth surfacing rather than a blank screen.

TAKES NO PARAMETERS. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: and REJECTS NONE - the view never reads `request.query_params`, so `?anything=1` is silently ignored with a 200, against the strict-input rule (undeclared parameters must error). DEFECT, not fixed here.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: missing or failed
auth is a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"` (measured).
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The page.
404 Not Found: When the page tree is not configured.
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: 500 Internal Server Error on a handled failure
(`data = {"status": "error"}`). The route is `app-learn-page-v1`.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppAiInAccountingReelsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Homepage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-ai-in-accounting-reels-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The AI-in-Accounting reels feed for the app home screen.

GET /app-api/v1/home/ai-in-accounting-reels/?page=1&page_size=10

APP-ONLY, hence the `app-api/` prefix and the `App` marker on the class - the surface rule's reads-split-by-surface half. There is no web twin today.

PAGINATION IS `utils.pagination`, the module every paginated surface uses, so this feed answers with the same block as the Programs feed and the web lists. It slices in SQL and passes the true count; the module only builds the window and the block, so nothing here leaves the event loop. Defaults are the module's (6 per page, 100 ceiling), not legacy's 10 / 50.

A BAD `?page=` IS A 400 NOW, and so is any parameter this endpoint does not read. It used to fall back to page one, which hid a client building the query string wrong - the strict-input rule's case.

EVERY READ IS A `.values()` PROJECTION and the two per-caller flags are `Exists` subqueries, so nothing materialises a model instance and no lazily loaded relation is touched on the event loop.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: every branch below is enveloped as `{success,
message, data}` by the default `EnvelopeJSONRenderer`; the shapes
listed are what lands in `data`.
200 OK: `{"slug", "count", "page", "page_size", "total_pages",
"has_next", "has_previous", "next", "previous", "results": [...]}`.
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: `slug` is always `null` - this route has no
`slug_registry` row and `read_paging` is called without `slugs`.
Each row carries `id, asset_slug, title, short_description,
long_description, image_url, video_url, duration_seconds, like_count,
position, liked_by_me, watched_by_me`.
THE LIST WAS `"ai_in_accounting"` UNTIL 2026-10-06, and
`"AI In Accounting"` before 2026-10-05 (legacy's spelling). It is
`results` now, as on every block `utils.pagination` builds. CLIENT
VISIBLE, and there is no alias.
400 Bad Request: a pagination value that is not a whole number, or a
query parameter this endpoint does not read (`data` is
`{status, reason: "invalid_query", errors}`). RECHECKED 2026-10-07:
an out-of-range `page_size` is CLAMPED to 1..100, not rejected.
401: no or bad bearer token, before this method runs.
500: `HANDLED_VIEW_ERRORS`, message "Unable to load the reels feed.".
200 OK with an empty list when the section is absent or deactivated -
NOT a 404. A section an editor turned off is a feed with nothing in it,
which is a normal state, not a missing resource.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppHomePageViewV1`  
**Module:** `Homepage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-home-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET homepage_V8_async/`

`GET app-api/v1/home/page/` - the whole app home page in one call.

Ported from legacy MilesOne's `/homepage_V8_async/`. THE `V8` WAS THEIRS, NOT OURS - this surface is v1 like everything else here, and the page's shape lives in the database rather than in a version number.

WHY ONE CALL. The app previously fanned out to the header, level, coming-soon, AI-Lab and referral endpoints separately, so the first screen cost five round trips on a phone network. This returns the lot.

THE PAGE IS DATA

```
Section order, titles and presence come from `CMS.Page` - a root row
with `page_slug="homepage"` and one active child per section, ordered
by `position`. What FILLS each section is decided by its slug, in
`_build_section`.
```

```
So re-ordering the page or renaming a heading is an admin edit. Only a
genuinely new KIND of section is a code change. Legacy hard-codes eleven
positions in the view, which is why every redesign there needed a whole
new endpoint.
```

EVERY ACTIVE SECTION SHIPS, EVEN EMPTY

```
`data` is always a list, and a section with nothing in it is `[]`
rather than omitted - so a rail that is merely empty today keeps its
slot and the client hides it.
```

```
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A SECTION IS DEACTIVATED IS DIFFERENT, and this
paragraph used to get it wrong. A row with `active=False` is filtered
out by `_page_sections` and does NOT ship as an empty section.
```

```
THE GUARANTEE THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS is that the survivors keep their
numbers: `position` is STORED on each row, not computed from list order,
so deactivating Level 2 leaves Level 3 at position 7. It does not slide
up into 6 and start impersonating Level 2. That is the property worth
having, and it is the reason `position` is read from the database rather
than enumerated at render time - a computed ordinal would renumber
everything after any removal.
```

```
POSITIONS ARE 1..11 AND CONTIGUOUS, seeded by
`Miscellaneous/Scripts/load_home_page_sections.py`. They are a display
counter, not a sparse sort key.
```

TWO GATES, DELIBERATELY NOT THE SAME TEST

```
`is_enrolled`            hides the continue-watching rail.
`can_access_masterclass` decides whether there is a subscription to
                           sell, and rewrites a locked card's CTA.
```

```
A CPA-only learner is ENROLLED and still holds none of what the
subscription offers, so one test cannot do both jobs. The second runs
SERIALLY AFTER the enrolment refresh, because that refresh persists the
learner's programme list and the access category is derived from it -
running them concurrently would read the category off the previous value.
```

CACHING

```
Per learner, 30 seconds, keyed on the shared CMS content version - so an
admin edit to any page, section or card invalidates every cached copy
with one `INCR` rather than a sweep nothing can perform. The cache
holds the UNCAPPED payload; the per-section cap runs after it, on both
hit and miss, so changing the cap does not keep serving the old one for a
TTL.
```

NO QUERY PARAMS

```
Unknown ones are IGNORED, not rejected, so an old client still gets an
ordinary response. A section needing more than `SECTION_LIMIT` items
needs its own endpoint. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: measured - `get` never
reads `request.query_params`; this departs from the platform's
strict-input rule (undeclared params must 400). DEFECT against that
rule, not fixed here.
```

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: CACHE INVALIDATION, measured. The only receivers that bump the shared content version are `CMS.utils.signals` (`invalidate_on_page_change` / `invalidate_on_asset_change`, post_save + post_delete on `CMS.Page` / `CMS.Asset`, via `on_commit`). `Homepage.utils.cache.invalidate_for_user` has 0 callers, and course, level, webinar and enrolment changes bump nothing - they age out on the 30-second `HOME_PAGE_CACHE_TTL`. Reads go to the replica (no atomic block).

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `BadgeClaimedByUserViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `badge-claimed-by-user-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces 3 legacy MilesOne routes:** `POST caira/level_based_badge_clicked/`, `POST caira/feedback_or_badge_status_v2/`, `POST caira/claim_alumni_badge/`

`POST api/v1/badges/badge-claimed-by-user/` - record that a learner claimed a badge.

THE ONE CLAIM ENDPOINT, FOR EVERY BADGE TYPE AND EVERY SURFACE (maintainer, 2026-10-08). It replaces three that did the same write keyed three ways - `api/v1/badges/alumni-claim/` (allocation id), `api/v1/badges/level-badge-clicked/` (accept URL or assertion id) and `web-api/v1/masterclass/level-badge-clicked/` (assertion id) - and the `{"claimed": true}` form briefly carried here. Removed, not aliased: no shipped client is on any of them.

BODY: EXACTLY ONE of `badge_id`, `credly_assertion_id` or `credly_accept_url` - whichever the screen was handed. See `BadgeClaimedByUserRequestSerializerV1`.

WHAT IT DOES, in order:

```
1. Finds the allocation by that identifier AND
   `credly_badge_for_user = caller`. Not found and not yours answer
   the same 404, deliberately - telling them apart tells a caller which
   ids exist.
2. Refuses a badge Credly has not issued (409). Every claim before this
   one marked a Pending row clicked, and the walls then showed a badge
   as claimed before it existed.
3. Sets `credly_badge_clicked_by_user` and rewrites the stored URL to
   the public `https://www.credly.com/badges/<assertion_id>`, in one
   `.aupdate()`. A click is not an allocation event, so the
   `post_save` "badge allocated" receiver is not run.
4. Deletes the alumni wall's per-learner cache, so a claimed alumni card
   reads as claimed on the next request rather than for up to 5 minutes.
```

IDEMPOTENT. A second claim answers 200 with `already_claimed: true`, so a client retrying after a dropped response does not need to care.

RESPONSES - one shape for success, one for every refusal:

```
200  `data`: `badge_id`, `credly_assertion_id`, `badge_type`,
     `claimed`, `already_claimed`, `credly_badge_url`
400  `data.code` `invalid_body` (with `data.errors`) or
     `invalid_credly_url`
404  `data.code` `badge_not_found`
409  `data.code` `badge_not_issued`
500  internal error
```

`badge_type` is one of `webinar`, `masterclass_course`, `level`, `ai_lab`, `archived_course`, `archived_podcast`, `archived_reel`, `alumni`, or null for a template attached to nothing.

Body template generated from `BadgeClaimedByUserRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppAlumniBadgesViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `app-alumni-badges-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET caira/get_alumni_badges/`

`GET app-api/v1/badges/alumni/` - the learner's CPA / CMA alumni cards.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRAGetAlumniBadgesView` (`caira/views.py`) on 2026-09-29.

THE THIRD BADGE ENDPOINT, AND THE THREE ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. Keep them straight before adding a field to the wrong one:

```
`badges/page/`           the CATALOGUE - every configured badge, with
                           the learner's state painted on top.
`account/user-details/`  the FLAGS - five booleans per programme,
                           including LMS login state, as
                           `enrolled_course`. No artwork. This was
                           `badges/alumni-status/` until 2026-10-07,
                           when that endpoint was removed as a strict
                           subset of `user-details`.
here                       the CARDS - what the learner actually holds,
                           with the Credly URLs needed to claim one.
```

THREE STATES PER PROGRAMME, which is the whole shape of the response:

```
not enrolled     no card at all. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the message
                 `NOT_ENROLLED_MESSAGE` is sent only when the learner
                 is enrolled in NEITHER programme (`data: []`).
enrolled, not    a card with the static artwork and the heading, and
alumni yet       nulls where the allocation's own values would go.
alumni           the full card, from the allocation row.
```

THE STATIC IMAGE URLS ARE LEGACY'S, CARRIED VERBATIM. They are Credly's own CDN, not ours, and they are what the app has rendered since this endpoint shipped - so they are constants here rather than a lookup that could answer differently. A card for a learner who is not yet alumni has no allocation to read an image off, and an empty card is worse than a greyed-out one.

CACHED PER LEARNER FOR 5 MINUTES, on a user-scoped key. Every field is about one person, so a shared key would serve one learner's badges to another for the whole TTL. `BadgeClaimedByUserViewV1` below deletes this key on every claim, so a claim is visible on the next read rather than up to five minutes later.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppFeedbackOrBadgeStatusViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `app-feedback-or-badge-status-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET caira/feedback_or_badge_status_v2/`

`GET app-api/v1/badges/feedback-or-badge-status/` - feedback due, or a badge to claim.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRAFeedbackAndGetBadgeStatusV2View` (GET half of `caira/feedback_or_badge_status_v2/`) on 2026-10-07. The walk that picks the webinar is in `utils/feedback_or_badge.py`, with every divergence from legacy listed under its WHAT CHANGED ON PORT.

THREE ANSWERS, legacy's contract key for key inside `data`:

```
feedback due   `showfeedback: true`, `id` = the WEBINAR id - the
               client opens `webinar/<id>/feedback/questions/`.
badge ready    `showfeedback: false`, `id` = the Credly ACCEPT URL,
               not an id. Legacy overloaded the key and the app reads
               it that way, so it is kept.
nothing        `data: {}`.
```

Both found answers also carry `webinar_name`, `subtitle` (always null, as in legacy), `cpe_credit_allocated` and `cpe_credit_label`.

NOT CACHED, AND LEGACY WAS NOT EITHER IN PRACTICE. Legacy read its 30-second per-learner key only when the request carried NO bearer token, and an authenticated request always carries one, so every read was computed fresh and the key was write-only. The registry row (`CAIRA_FEEDBACK_BADGE_STATUS_USER_PREFIX`) is left as it is.

`app-api/` BECAUSE IT IS A READ SHAPED FOR THE APP. The claim is a write and sits on the shared prefix: `BadgeClaimedByUserViewV1`, which takes the `id` from the badge answer as `credly_accept_url`. Legacy's `{"claimed": true}` POST on this same path is not carried. API_VERSIONING_STANDARD section 1.1.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppBadgesPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `app-badges-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET caira/badges_catalog/V2/`

`GET app-api/v1/badges/page/` - the app's CPE Tracker badge wall.

A `cpe_summary` progress strip followed by four sections, in screen order: `level_badges`, `webinar_badges`, `masterclass_badges` and `global_certifications`.

CATALOGUE-CENTRIC, NOT EARNED-CENTRIC. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the earned-centric endpoint is `AppAlumniBadgesViewV1` (`badges/alumni/`), which lists the alumni cards a learner holds; the per-programme FLAGS now come from `GET api/v1/account/user-details/` as `enrolled_course` (`alumni-status` was removed 2026-10-07). This one lists EVERY configured Production badge (alumni badges excluded) and paints the learner's state on top, so a learner with zero badges still gets a full wall of cards rather than an empty screen.

READ-ONLY. Every action a card fires - claim, feedback, register - already has its own endpoint, and the `cta` block names which.

THE FOUR SECTIONS

```
`level_badges`          one per active level with a Production badge,
                          ordered by level number, category-gated.
`webinar_badges`        CAIRA webinar badges, next session ascending,
                          cards with nothing scheduled last.
`masterclass_badges`    course badges, most actionable first.
`global_certifications` NON-CAIRA webinar badges, with their session.
```

THE CAIRA SPLIT IS WHY THE FOURTH SECTION EXISTS, and the two halves use the SAME predicate so a webinar cannot land in both or neither: `webinar_badges` takes `is_caira` true, `global_certifications` takes it false. Without the split a non-CAIRA webinar carrying a badge would appear twice in one response.

CACHING. Only the global catalogue layer is cached, partitioned by the test-viewer flag - see `badge_catalog`. The per-learner overlay is always fresh, because every field in it is an entitlement a learner acts on immediately, and a badge that does not change when it is claimed reads as a broken button.

`{}` IS NOT `null`. `next_session` and `cta` use an empty object for "nothing here", which is truthy in JavaScript - clients must test `Object.keys(x).length`.

PORTED FROM LEGACY MILESONE `CAIRABadgesCatalogAsyncViewV2`, 2026-09-28. The response contract is carried across; the reads underneath were rewritten against re-normalised models, and `badge_catalog`'s docstring holds the table. THREE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES, each recorded where it happens:

1. `global_certifications` IS BUILT HERE, NOT BORROWED FROM THE EVENTS PAGE. Legacy instantiates the events view and calls five of its private methods, which this repository bans (H-21, no inline `protected-access`) and which would couple two endpoints' internals. The session half is projected through `EventsPage.serializers_page.card` instead - the SHAPE is shared, the pipeline is not - so a client keeps one binding. 2. THE CPE CREDIT IS DERIVED. Legacy reads a stored credit column that does not exist here; `EventsPage.utils.webinar_maps.acpe_map` sums the webinar's active fields of study, which is the one place CPE is derived. 3. THE TEST-WEBINAR GATE IS NEW. Legacy has no such flag; here it is the outermost gate and the catalogue cache is partitioned by it.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `limit` - Optional. Default `0`. Per-section cap. 0 means use the endpoint's own default.
- `section` - Optional. One of level / webinar / masterclass / global_certifications.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebBadgesPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `web-badges-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET web-api/v1/badges/page/` - the web CPE Tracker badge wall.

A `cpe_summary` progress strip followed by THREE sections, in screen order: `level_badges`, `webinar_badges`, `masterclass_badges`.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `GET caira/web/badges_catalog/`.

WRITTEN OUT IN FULL, NOT INHERITED (maintainer, 2026-09-28). Legacy's web view is a nine-line subclass of its V1 catalogue that overrides NOTHING, so every edit to the app wall silently changed the web contract and the direction of that coupling was invisible at the call site. This shares no code with `AppBadgesPageViewV1` - not the section list, not the caps, not the query model. Both call the same READ layer (`badge_catalog`) and the same PROJECTIONS (`serializers`), which is where the similarity is allowed to end: those are a catalogue and a card shape, not this endpoint's contract.

TWO DIVERGENCES FROM THE APP WALL, AND BOTH ARE INHERITED FROM WHICH LEGACY ENDPOINT EACH ONE COMES FROM. The app wall is ported from V2; this is ported from V1, and legacy's web view extends V1 rather than V2.

1. NO `global_certifications` SECTION. V2 added it; V1 has none. 2. `webinar_badges` IS NOT FILTERED ON `is_caira`, so it carries every webinar badge - CAIRA and not. On the app wall the non-CAIRA badges are split out into `global_certifications`, and filtering them out of the webinar section there stops one badge appearing twice in one response. There is no competing section here, so the same filter would simply LOSE those cards - legacy records exactly that reasoning for leaving V1 alone, and it still holds.

CACHING is the shared global catalogue, partitioned by the test-viewer flag; the per-learner overlay is never cached. See `badge_catalog`.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Default 1.
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Default 6, ceiling 100.
- `section` - Optional. One of level / webinar / masterclass.

`POST app-api/v1/webinar/<uuid:webinar_id>/feedback/submit/` - record, award.

ALL OR NOTHING. Every active question must be answered in one request; a partial set writes nothing and is a 400.

WHAT IS AWARDED IS WHAT THE WEBINAR OFFERS - CPE where it carries credit, a Credly badge where a template is configured, a certificate where a certificate template is set. All three, or any subset, decided by configuration rather than by this endpoint.

Body template generated from `WebinarFeedbackSubmitRequestV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppWebinarFeedbackResponsesViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `app-webinar-feedback-responses-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

`GET app-api/v1/webinar/feedback/responses/?webinar_id=<uuid>`.

THE LEARNER READING BACK THEIR OWN ANSWERS - the CTA on an individual report, not a moderation tool. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: the answer-row query is filtered on `request.user`; the other two (webinar exists, active question count) read no learner data. So changing the id in the query string reaches a different WEBINAR and never a different PERSON.

NO ELIGIBILITY GATE, deliberately. `decide`/`gate` answer "may they give feedback", which stops being true the moment they answer; this answers "what did they say", which stays true forever. Running the gate here would hide a learner's own answers from them once the webinar aged out.

ALWAYS ANSWERS for a webinar that exists: `submitted` is False and `responses` is `[]` when they never filled the form, so the client renders the empty state without branching on a 404.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `webinar_id` - Required.

```
permanently, so anything we can record we accept and report in
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `ZoomWebhookReceiverV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `events-webhook-zoom-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

Receive Zoom events and register a webinar for poll-report ingestion.

POST /api/v1/events/webhook/zoom/

UNIVERSAL AND UNAUTHENTICATED BY DESIGN. Zoom is not a surface and holds no JWT, so `authentication_classes` is empty and `AllowAny` applies - the request is authenticated by an HMAC over its RAW body, verified here.

TWO EVENTS ARE HANDLED AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS A FAST 200:

- `endpoint.url_validation` - the one-time challenge Zoom runs when the endpoint is registered. It is NOT signed, so it is answered BEFORE signature verification; answering it after would make the endpoint impossible to register. Because that branch signs caller-supplied text while nothing has authenticated yet, the token is validated first - see `_url_validation`.
- `webinar.ended` - the real trigger. Resolves the webinar, upserts the tracking row with the verbatim envelope on it, and stops.

A NON-200 MAKES ZOOM RETRY, which is why an unusable event is ignored with a 200 rather than refused: a malformed body, an unknown webinar or an event this backend does not care about will never become usable, so a retry schedule against it is pure noise. 401 is reserved for a signature that does not verify - RECHECKED 2026-10-07: including when OUR secret is unset (`NO_SECRET` also answers 401). The unsigned `endpoint.url_validation` branch has two more non-200s: 503 when the secret is unset and 400 for a malformed `plainToken` - see `_url_validation`.

IT DOES NOT ENQUEUE ANYTHING. The row is registered and the fetch is left to the sweep, because Zoom's report lags the end of the webinar and a Celery countdown longer than the Redis visibility timeout is redelivered repeatedly. See `EventsPage/tasks.py`.

SYNCHRONOUS, unlike every other view in this file. It does two short queries and no external I/O, and `hmac.compare_digest` plus `request.body` are both synchronous - an async wrapper here would add a thread hop to save nothing.

**Surface:** WEBHOOK

**Module:** `Notification.views`

**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** HasValidMilesOneWebhookSecretV1

POST one CRM/Events-CMS webinar payload, stored VERBATIM.

THE ONE ENDPOINT IN THIS APP WITHOUT A STRICT INPUT SERIALIZER, and that is deliberate. The body is a third party's record, kept whole in a JSON column with no mapping into the live `Webinar` model - normalisation is a later phase. A strict serializer would have to enumerate the CMS's field set and would reject every field it adds, which for a landing table is the wrong failure. Only `document_id` is required.

DEDUP IS AN UPSERT ON `document_id`. A repeat push overwrites the stored payload and RESETS the row to `received`, dropping any prior webinar link and `processed_at` - because a re-pushed payload makes earlier normalisation stale.

DELIVERY MODEL, and it drives the response codes: the CMS is fire-and-forget. It logs a non-2xx and does NOT retry, so RECHECKED 2026-10-07: any 400 or 401 (a rejected secret is 401, not 403) returned here means that event is permanently lost on the CMS side. Respond 2xx quickly.

Payload conventions, not to be fought: every field is always present with `null` for unset; the big-integer fields arrive as STRINGS to preserve precision and must stay strings; media fields are a URL or `null`.

Auth:

```
`X-Webhook-Secret` matching `MILES_ONE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. No JWT.
```

Responses:

```
201: created. 200: upserted. Both carry
    `{status, message, id, document_id, created}`.
400: body is not a JSON object, or `document_id` is missing.
401: header missing or wrong, or the secret is not configured.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `ReferralMilesForceWebhookViewV1`  
**Module:** `Referral.views`  
**Route name:** `referral-milesforce-webhook-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** HasValidMilesForceVendorTokenV1

MilesForce tells us a referral's verdict.

POST /api/v1/referral/webhook/milesforce/

ANONYMOUS TO DRF, AUTHENTICATED BY A SHARED SECRET. MilesForce holds no JWT, so the only credential is the `x-vendor-token` header compared against `settings.X_VENDOR_TOKEN` by `HasValidMilesForceVendorTokenV1`.

THREE THINGS ABOUT THAT COMPARISON, ALL LOAD-BEARING, and all now the shared `SharedSecretPermission`'s rather than this view's:

```
1. `secrets.compare_digest`, not `==`. A plain comparison returns
   early on the first differing byte, which leaks the secret's prefix to
   anyone who can time the response.
2. AN UNSET SETTING REFUSES EVERY CALLER, with 401. If `X_VENDOR_TOKEN`
   is blank nothing is compared - an unconfigured environment must not be
   an open door onto a table that decides who gets paid. It answered 503
   until 2026-10-07; 401 is legacy's pinned contract and does not invite
   MilesForce to retry against an environment that will never accept it.
3. NO FALLBACK TO THE SETTING WHEN THE HEADER IS ABSENT. Legacy once
   substituted `settings.X_VENDOR_TOKEN` for a missing header and then
   compared it against itself, so a request with no credential matched.
   That was fixed in legacy and the fix is carried, named, so nobody
   reintroduces the convenience.
```

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT enveloped (`NullForBlankJSONRenderer`).
200 OK: `ok`, `referral_id`, `status`, `matched_on`,
`forced_transition`, `updated_fields`, `unparsed_fields`.
400: a body that fails `MilesForceWebhookRequestSerializerV1` (missing
`id` / `bonus_status`, a non-UUID `referrance_id`, or an
undeclared key), or `{"detail": ...}` for a `bonus_status` we do not
recognise.
401: `{"detail": "A valid x-vendor-token header is required."}` for a
missing, wrong or unprovisioned vendor token, with no
`WWW-Authenticate` header (measured).
404: `{"detail": ...}` when no referral matched either key.
500: `internal_error_response`'s body, detail in the span.
```

Body template generated from `MilesForceWebhookRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Authorised by the `x-vendor-token` header, NOT by the bearer token. Set `{{x_vendor_token}}` in the environment.

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST api/referral-page/`

File a referral: the caller names somebody they want referred.

POST /api/v1/referral/refer/

SHARED PREFIX, BECAUSE IT IS A WRITE. The rule is that writes stay shared and reads split by surface, so the class name carries a bare `V1`.

THE LOCAL ROWS COMMIT FIRST AND THE UPSTREAM CALL CANNOT UNDO THEM. n8n creates the MilesForce lead, and MilesForce's id for the referral comes back later on the webhook - so until that lead exists, `Referral.referral_code` is NULL and the webhook cannot address the row. That makes the call important, and still not important enough to fail a request over: a referrer who filled the form in correctly must not be told it failed because an automation host was unwell. The outcome is reported in `mf` instead, and a row with no code is a row a retry sweep can find.

IT FIRES NO NOTIFICATION, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Legacy called `notify_referrer_referral_created` here. Referral notifications are PARKED by the maintainer (2026-10-01) pending the Netcore template parameters - see `Miscellaneous/Documentation/MASTER_TODO.md`. Sending to a Netcore activity with no template is a 200 and a silent drop, so wiring it now would look delivered and reach nobody.

Responses:

```
Wrapped by the default `EnvelopeJSONRenderer` as
`{success, message, data}`; the shapes below are what lands in `data`,
and `message` is lifted into the envelope.
201 Created: the referral is new. `referral_id` (this platform's row
id), `referral_code` (MilesForce's id, NULL until their webhook
supplies it), `status`, `referee` and `mf`.
200 OK: this referrer had already named this person. Same shape - the
pair is unique by constraint, so a repeat is not a second bonus.
400 Bad Request: a missing, malformed or undeclared field.
409 Conflict: `phone_already_exists` or `email_already_exists` - see
`Referral.utils.filing` for why the first one also refuses an identical
resubmission that carries no email.
401 Unauthorized: missing or failed JWT.
500: an internal error, detail in the span rather than the body.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `ReferralValidateCodeViewV1`  
**Module:** `Referral.views`  
**Route name:** `referral-validate-code-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST verify-referral/apply-six-digit-code/`

Would this referral code be accepted for the caller?

POST /api/v1/referral/validate-code/

SHARED PREFIX, NOT `app-api/` OR `web-api/`. The rule is that writes stay shared and reads split by surface; this writes nothing and both surfaces ask the identical question about the same learner and read the identical answer, so it is universal and the class name carries a bare `V1`.

AUTHENTICATED, BECAUSE THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON THE CALLER. Two of the four refusals - self-referral, and a different code already applied - are facts about who is asking, not about the code. An anonymous version could only answer "does this string exist", which is the one question worth not answering: six characters from a 36-character alphabet is a small enough space to walk.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: every answer is wrapped by the default
`EnvelopeJSONRenderer` as `{success, message, data}`; the shapes
below are what lands in `data`.
200 OK: `{"ok": true, "code": "<CODE>"}` - the code would be applied,
echoed upper-cased. The `"code": null` branch is UNREACHABLE: the
serializer refuses a blank or whitespace-only `code` with 400 before
`acheck` can return `None`.
400 Bad Request (refusal): `{"ok": false, "reason": "<outcome>"}` with
the display sentence lifted into the envelope's `message`. `reason`
is one of `invalid`, `expired`, `self_referral`,
`already_redeemed`.
400 Bad Request (body): `code` missing, blank, not six A-Z/0-9
characters, or an undeclared key - DRF's validation-error body.
401 Unauthorized: missing or failed JWT, with
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`.
500: an internal error, with the detail in the span rather than the body.
```

`reason` AND `message` ARE DIFFERENT AUDIENCES. Legacy returned only a sentence, so a client that wanted to branch had to match on English prose. The outcome constants are part of the wire contract; the sentences are not.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppLikedAssetViewV1`  
**Module:** `Engagement.views`  
**Route name:** `app-favourites-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Everything the calling learner has liked, grouped by what it is.

GET /app-api/v1/favourites/

THE CLASS SAYS "LIKED ASSET", THE PATH SAYS "FAVOURITES", AND THAT IS ON PURPOSE (maintainer, 2026-10-01). "Favourites" is the learner-facing word and is what legacy's route was called, so the path keeps it; the class is named for what it actually reads, which is `User_Like` rows. The naming standard wants path, route name and class to agree, so this is a recorded exception rather than drift - say the word and the path becomes `liked-assets/`, which costs nothing today because no client is bound to it yet.

APP-ONLY, hence the `app-api/` prefix and the `App` marker - reads split by surface, and there is no web twin today.

SCOPED TO `request.user` AND NOT ADDRESSABLE. There is no user id in the path or the query, so one caller cannot read another's favourites by guessing a UUID - the same reasoning as `ProfileViewV1`.

BOTH BUCKETS SHIP ON EVERY RESPONSE, empty as `[]` rather than omitted. A client that renders a section per key must not have a section appear and disappear depending on what the learner happens to have liked.

`reels` IS THE AI-IN-ACCOUNTING SECTION ONLY, not every CMS asset the learner has liked - see the note above this class for why, and for what that hides.

TWO QUERIES, NOT ONE PER ROW. Legacy issued one query and then walked `select_related` chains three relations deep per row to find the page a file belonged to. Both reads here are `.values()` projections that join what they need in SQL, so nothing is materialised and no lazily loaded relation is touched on the event loop.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: enveloped `{success, message, data}`.
200 OK: `data` is `{"masterclass": [...], "reels": [...]}`.
401: missing or failed Bearer token, from DRF before `get` runs.
500: an internal error, with the detail in the span rather than the body;
`message` is "Unable to load your favourites.", `data` is
`{"status": "error"}`.
```

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST 7DC/masterclass/course-released/`

S3.5 inbound - partner reports a learner ABANDONED / the challenge EXPIRED.

Lifts the first-start-wins lock by setting `released_from_7dc=True` on the `(user, course)` enrollment, so the learner can finish the SAME course in our in-app player (the chapter-start guards honour this flag). `started_via_7dc` is left `True` for origin audit - release is additive, never a rewrite.

**Service-key authed** (`X-LMS-OPEN-API-KEY`), NOT user-JWT: the "expired" trigger is a server-side timer on the partner with no logged-in learner, so the user is identified by `user_sso_id` in the body (resolved to an active `account.user`) rather than a JWT subject. This is the only S3.5 write, and the only partner endpoint that mutates enrollment state without a learner session - deliberate, per the abandon/expire product decision.

Fire-and-forget friendly: benign "nothing to release" states return `200` with `released=false` (not 4xx), so the partner's postback worker never retries on them; only genuine payload errors are 4xx. Idempotent on `(user, course)` - a second release is a `200` no-op.

**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET 7DC/masterclass/course-started/<uuid>/`

Check whether the authenticated user has started a course IN OUR IN-APP MILESONE PLAYER (i.e. not via the 7DC partner flow).

This is for LMS 7 Day Challenge only - read-only by design.

The 7DC partner calls this BEFORE starting the gamified flow on their side. `course_started` answers ONE question for them: "is this learner already going through the course in the MilesOne app?" - because that is the only case the partner must not start (it would 409 on `course-start` as `already_started_in_app`, and the learner is genuinely "stuck in MilesOne").

Semantics (note: this is NOT a blanket "any enrollment exists" flag):

- `course_started=true`  -> an enrollment row exists that was created by the in-app player (`started_via_7dc=False`). The learner is learning on the MilesOne app; the partner must not start.
- `course_started=false` -> EITHER no enrollment exists at all, OR the only enrollment was created by the partner's own `course-start` POST (`started_via_7dc=True`). In both cases the partner is free to (re)enter the 7DC flow - its own `course-start` is idempotent, so a 7DC-originated enrollment is never reported as "started" back to the partner.

GET /7DC/masterclass/course-started/<uuid:course_id>/

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `MyPlansViewV1`  
**Module:** `Subscriptions.views`  
**Route name:** `subscriptions-my-plans-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

List the personal and fallback prices the caller currently holds.

Answers "what have I been given?", which an app needs for a banner without naming a product. The plans listing answers a different question - "what can I buy" - per product.

*** READ ONLY. *** This GET creates, updates and expires NOTHING: no `get_or_create`, no lazy expiry sweep, no stamping `notified_at`. A GET that mints offers is a recorded pitfall of the predecessor project ("anyone could mint one"); the only writers of an assignment are the admin form and the EMI-failure webhook.

*** THE RAISING `JWTAuthentication`, NOT `OptionalJWTAuthentication`. *** This endpoint REVEALS a learner's private grants, so a bad token must be a 401. The optional class would turn it into an anonymous call and an empty list, which tells a learner with a broken token that they have no offers - a wrong answer presented as a true one.

LIVE MEANS `status` AND `expires_at` TOGETHER, and only `Subscriptions.utils.assignments.live_assignments_sync` is allowed to say so; a row is `open` yet stale between its expiry and the next sweep.

AN ASSIGNMENT WHOSE PLAN IS NO LONGER SELLABLE IS OMITTED, via the same `_assigned_plan_rows` the listing uses, so the two surfaces never disagree: a banner must not advertise a price the learner cannot then buy.

Response: `{"status": "ok", "count": n, "results": [{id, source, expires_at, plan}]}`, soonest-expiring first. No assignments is `count: 0` and an empty list, not an error.

The nested `plan` repeats the same expiry as `assignment_expires_at`, because one plan renderer serves both this endpoint and the listing; the two values are always equal.
