**Module:** `Subscriptions.views`  
**Route name:** `subscriptions-plans-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** OptionalJWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** none

List the purchasable subscription plans, priced for the caller's country.

ANONYMOUS IS ALLOWED, and that is a deliberate exception on this app. The other two routes here are service-to-service and the rest of the learner surface needs a token, but a pricing page is the screen somebody sees BEFORE they have an account - requiring a token to find out what a subscription costs is a sign-up funnel that starts with a sign-up. Nothing per-learner is returned: no entitlement, no order, no identity. The precedent in this codebase is `events/webinar-main-page?login_type=pre_login`.

NOT PAGINATED. There are a handful of plans and every client renders all of them side by side on one pricing page; a page-size parameter would be an interface nobody uses and one more thing a caller can get wrong.

THE CURRENCY FOLLOWS THE PLAN ITSELF, never the caller's country. Since D-SP3/D-SP4 (2026-09-25) a plan prices itself - there is no `Product_Price` row being resolved here any more - see `shape_plan`.

THE PRICING COUNTRY COMES FROM THE `X-Country-Code` HEADER. This docstring said the OPPOSITE until 2026-09-23 - that the build specification's header was deliberately not followed, because `resolve_country_id` read a query parameter and a second mechanism would mean one question answered two ways. That reasoning was sound and its conclusion was reversed by the maintainer on that date: the header is now the ONE mechanism, `resolve_country_id` reads it, and `?country=` is an unknown parameter and a 400 everywhere. Recorded rather than deleted, because the argument still explains why there is exactly one way to name a market.

A CREDENTIAL IS OPTIONAL AND CHANGES ONLY WHOSE PRICES COME BACK (D-UP4). Since 2026-10-07 a plan carries `audience`, and a `Plan_Assignment` says which learner may buy a `personal` or `fallback` one and until when. So:

| caller                              | answer                          | | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | no credential                       | general plans. Cached, as ever  | | credential, no live assignment      | general plans. NOT CACHED       | | credential, live assignment for X   | X's rows become the assignment's| |                                     | plan; every other product's     | |                                     | rows stay general. NOT CACHED   |

A LIVE ASSIGNMENT WHOSE PLAN IS NO LONGER SELLABLE READS AS NO ASSIGNMENT, FOR THAT PRODUCT ONLY - the learner sees the product's general plans, not an empty space where it used to be. `live_assignments_sync` tests `status` and `expires_at` and not `plan.active`, so this case is real; the rule and the ruling behind it are in `_assigned_plan_rows`.

The first line of that table is byte-for-byte what this endpoint returned before any of this existed, and that is a requirement rather than a coincidence - see `shape_plan` on why a general row gained no wire keys.

*** AN AUTHENTICATED REQUEST READS NOTHING FROM THE CACHE AND WRITES NOTHING TO IT (D-UP9 / HZ-UP1). *** The key is market plus product with NO user component, so ONE authenticated response written to it serves a private price to every anonymous visitor in that market until the TTL runs out. The bypass is therefore unconditional on `request.user .is_authenticated` and is NOT conditional on the learner actually holding an assignment: a learner with none is the commonest authenticated caller, and "bypass only when there are assignments" is the bug this paragraph exists to forbid - it writes the general response under the shared key on almost every authenticated request and then, on the one request that matters, has already taught a reader that the write is usually fine. A PER-USER KEY IS ALSO REJECTED (D-UP9): it multiplies a hot cache by the user base to serve a response that differs for a small minority, and it fails the same way the moment the credential is absent while the key is built.

A STALE OR MALFORMED TOKEN STILL RETURNS PRICES, NOT 401, which is why `OptionalJWTAuthentication` exists - `JWTAuthentication` RAISES `AuthenticationFailed` on a bad token, and this endpoint's urlconf entry documents it "ANONYMOUS BY DESIGN - a pricing page is seen before sign-up". Failing open is safe HERE because anonymous is the strictly less privileged outcome: the credential only ever ADDS the caller's own rows. Read that class's docstring before copying this line anywhere else.

IT READS THE REPLICA, AND AN ASSIGNMENT GRANTED SECONDS AGO CAN BE MISSED. `DATABASE_ROUTERS` is active and `db_for_read` sends every read outside a transaction to the replica, so under replication lag a learner can be shown general prices moments after an operator granted them a personal one. THAT IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN FIXED, deliberately: a refresh resolves it, this is a cacheable GET on a pricing page, and the two fixes available - pinning the alias with `.using(router.db_for_write(...))` or wrapping the read in `transaction.atomic()` so it is pinned to the primary - both move every listing read onto the primary to close a window measured in seconds on a read nobody is charged against. `Subscriptions.utils.assignments` says the same thing and leaves the choice to each caller for this reason; the CART is the caller that may well decide differently, because a wrong price there is money. Anyone debugging "the assignment exists but the listing ignores it" should look here first and at the logic second.
